dominicalIntent: You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskins, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you (*ve-hayah le-oth berith beyni u-veynaykhem*). Cutting the foreskin inscribes the covenant directly into the organ of human generation, sanctifying family life and reminding Israel that the Messianic Seed comes through divine election.
cccReferences: CCC 1150 (Visible bodily sign of the covenant); CCC 527; Rom 4:11.
historicalContext: Surgical removal of the prepuce (*orlah*) as a permanent physical sign of sacred consecration.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-nemalthem eth besar orlathkhem ve-hayah le-oth berith beyni u-veynaykhem*: *orlah* (foreskin). *Oth berith* (sign of the covenant).
historicalTrivia: Romans 4:11 explains that Abraham 'received the sign of circumcision as a seal (*sphragis*) of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised'.

dominicalIntent: He who is eight days old among you shall be circumcised (*U-ven shemonath yamim yimmol lakhem kol-zakhar*). THE EIGHTH DAY! Circumcision is commanded precisely on the **Eighth Day** (*shemonath yamim*). The Eighth Day is the day of Resurrection and New Creation! Christ rose on the Eighth Day (Sunday), making the 8th day the supreme day of Christian rebirth in Baptism.
cccReferences: CCC 1219 (Circumcision on the Eighth Day prefiguring Baptism on the Eighth Day of Resurrection); CCC 349 (The Eighth Day of New Creation); Luke 2:21.
historicalContext: Medical / pediatric timeline: infant blood coagulation factors reach peak levels on the 8th day post-birth.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-ven shemonath yamim yimmol lakhem kol-zakhar le-dorothaykhem*.
historicalTrivia: Modern hematology confirms that prothrombin (clotting factor) peaks at 110% of normal value on the 8th day of life, making it the safest day for infant circumcision.

dominicalIntent: Both he who is born in your house and he who is bought with your money shall be circumcised; so shall my covenant be in your flesh an everlasting covenant. The covenant encompasses the entire household, slave and free. This household inclusion prefigures **Infant Baptism** in the Catholic Church, where entire households are baptized into Christ (Acts 16:33).
cccReferences: CCC 1252 (Infant Baptism prefigured in household circumcision); CCC 1219; Acts 16:33.
historicalContext: Household solidarity including all servants (*yelid bayith*) and acquired persons in covenant rites.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Himmol yimmol yelid beythkha u-miqnath kaspekha ve-hayethah berithi bi-vsarkhem le-berith olam*.
historicalTrivia: The Catholic Church grounds the ancient practice of Infant Baptism (CCC 1252) in the Old Testament precedent of infant circumcision on the 8th day.

dominicalIntent: Any uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that person shall be cut off from his people (*ve-nikhrethah ha-nephesh ha-hi mi-ammeyha*); he has broken my covenant. Refusing the covenant sign results in being 'cut off' (*nikhrethah*). In the New Covenant, obstinate rejection of Baptism and Holy Sacraments separates the soul from the Body of Christ.
cccReferences: CCC 1257 (Baptism as necessary for salvation for those to whom the Gospel has been proclaimed); CCC 1131 (Sacraments as necessary means of grace); CCC 1854.
historicalContext: Excommunication / legal excision (*kareth*) from the covenant assembly for deliberate treaty rejection.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-arel zakhar asher lo-yimmol eth-besar orlatho ve-nikhrethah ha-nephesh ha-hi mi-ammeyha eth-berithi hephar*: *kareth* (severance/excision).
historicalTrivia: Exodus 4:24-26 records Moses almost dying under divine judgment because he neglected to circumcise his son Gershom, until Zipporah performed the rite.

dominicalIntent: And God said to Abraham: 'As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name' (*ki Sarah shemah*). GOD RENAMES SARAI TO SARAH! Sarai ('My Princess') becomes **Sarah** ('Princess of Nations' / 'Queen'). Sarah is elevated to matriarch of the royal covenant line, prefiguring the Blessed Virgin Mary, Queen of Heaven and Mother of all nations.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (Sarah renamed as royal matriarch prefiguring Our Lady); CCC 2032 (Renaming); Gal 4:26-31.
historicalContext: Royal renaming of the matriarch alongside Abraham to mark her mothering of royal nations.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Elohim el-Avraham Sarai ishtekha lo-thiqra eth-shemah Sarai ki Sarah shemah*: *Sarah* (Princess / Queen / Lady).
historicalTrivia: The name change from *Sarai* (possessive: 'my princess') to *Sarah* (absolute: 'Princess / Queen') universalizes her royal status to all nations.

dominicalIntent: I will bless her, and moreover, I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she shall become nations; kings of peoples shall come from her (*ve-hayethah le-goyim melakhim ammim mimmennah yihyu*). GOD PROMISES ISAAC! Sarah herself will give birth to the promised son. Kings of nations shall come from Sarah! This rules out Ishmael as the covenant heir and establishes Isaac as the child of miracle and promise.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (Miraculous promise of Isaac through barren Sarah prefiguring the Virgin Birth); CCC 60; Gal 4:23; Rom 9:7-9.
historicalContext: Divine promise of miraculous fertility to a 90-year-old post-menopausal woman.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-verakhti othah ve-gam nathatti mimmennah lekha ben u-verakhtiha ve-hayethah le-goyim melakhim ammim mimmennah yihyu*.
historicalTrivia: Romans 9:9 quotes Genesis 17:16 / 18:10 as the foundational word of promise: 'At this time I will return, and Sarah shall have a son'.

dominicalIntent: God announces: 'Behold, I bring a flood of waters (*mabbul mayim*) upon the earth to destroy all flesh... everything on earth shall die.' The Flood waters represent both death to sin and the cleansing of creation, prefiguring Holy Baptism which buries the old man of sin and raises the believer to new life in Christ.
cccReferences: CCC 1219 (The waters of the Flood as a image of Baptism: death to sin and birth to new life); CCC 58 (Cosmic purging of evil); CCC 1021 (Divine judgment).
historicalContext: Hebrew *mabbul* (cataclysmic deluge) is a unique technical term used almost exclusively for Noah's flood, distinct from normal flooding (*shetheph*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va-ani hineni mevi eth-ha-mabbul mayim al-ha-aretz*: *mabbul* (deluge/cataclysm), cognate with Akkadian *bibbulu*. *Yigva* ('shall expire/die').
historicalTrivia: Geological sediment core samples in the Black Sea basin show evidence of a catastrophic marine inundation around 5600 BC, matching ancient ANE flood memories.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham said to God: 'Oh that Ishmael might live before you!' (*Lu Yishmael yichyeh le-phaneykha*). Abraham expresses tender paternal love for Ishmael, pleading that Ishmael be included in divine favor. God hears Abraham's prayer for Ishmael.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham interceding for his son Ishmael); CCC 2605.
historicalContext: Paternal interversional prayer for a firstborn son according to the flesh.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avraham el-ha-Elohim Lu Yishmael yichyeh le-phaneykha*: *Lu* ('Oh that! / Would that!').
historicalTrivia: Abraham's prayer for Ishmael demonstrates that righteous fathers pray for all their children regardless of covenant status.

dominicalIntent: God said: 'No, but Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac (*Yitzchaq*). I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.' GOD NAMES ISAAC BEFORE BIRTH! The covenant line passes strictly through Isaac (*Yitzchaq*), the son of miracle and promise. Isaac is the premier Old Testament type of Jesus Christ, the Only-Begotten Son.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (The covenant lineage passing through Isaac); CCC 489; Gal 4:28; Rom 9:7.
historicalContext: Divine name assignment (*Yitzchaq*) commemorating Abraham's joyful laughter and ratifying the messianic election.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Elohim aval Sarah ishtekha yoladeth lekha ben ve-qaratha eth-shemo Yitzchaq ve-haqimothi eth-berithi itto le-berith olam*: *Yitzchaq* ('He laughs / Laughter').
historicalTrivia: Galatians 4:28 declares to all baptized Christians: 'Now you, brethren, like Isaac, are children of promise'.

dominicalIntent: As for Ishmael, I have heard you; behold, I have blessed him and will make him fruitful and multiply him exceedingly. He shall father twelve princes (*sheney-asar nesi'im*), and I will make him into a great nation. God answers Abraham's prayer for Ishmael! Ishmael receives 12 princes (*nesi'im*) and a great national blessing, though distinct from the messianic covenant of Isaac.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God answering Abraham's prayer for Ishmael); CCC 58; Gen 25:12-16.
historicalContext: 12 Arabian tribal princes (*nesi'im*) descended from Ishmael, matching the 12 tribes of Israel descended from Jacob.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-le-Yishmael shema'tikha hinneh berakhti otho ve-hiphrethi otho... sheney-asar nesi'im yolid*: *nesi'im* (princes/chieftains).
historicalTrivia: Genesis 25:12-16 lists the exact names of Ishmael's 12 princes (Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, Kedemah).

dominicalIntent: But I will establish my covenant with Isaac (*Ve-eth-berithi aqim eth-Yitzchaq*), whom Sarah shall bear to you at this time next year. The Messianic Covenant belongs exclusively to Isaac. Salvation history narrows to the child of divine promise.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (The divine election of Isaac); Rom 9:7; Gal 4:28.
historicalContext: Specific prophetic calendar timestamp: 'at this time next year' (*la-mo'ed ha-zeh ba-shanah ha-achereth*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-eth-berithi aqim eth-Yitzchaq asher teled lekha Sarah la-mo'ed ha-zeh ba-shanah ha-achereth*: *la-mo'ed* ('at the appointed sacred time').
historicalTrivia: The word *mo'ed* means 'appointed feast / sacred time', indicating that Isaac's birth was scheduled on God's liturgical calendar.

dominicalIntent: When he had finished talking with him, God went up from Abraham (*Vayya'al Elohim me-al Avraham*). The divine revelation concludes. God 'ascends' (*vayya'al*) after delivering His covenant word.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Conclusion of the divine encounter); CCC 707.
historicalContext: Formal conclusion of a divine theophany.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaykhal ledabber itto vayya'al Elohim me-al Avraham*: *vayya'al* (ascended / went up).
historicalTrivia: The phrase *Vya'al Elohim* ('God ascended from him') echoes Jesus' Ascension in Luke 24:51 (*diestē ap autōn*).

dominicalIntent: Then Abraham took Ishmael his son and all more born in his house or bought with his money... and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very same day (*be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh*), as God had Said to him. IMMEDIATE OBEDIENCE OF FAITH! Abraham executes the covenant of circumcision *on the selfsame day* (*be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh*). True faith hesitates not a single day to obey God's sacraments.
cccReferences: CCC 145 (Prompt, absolute obedience of faith); CCC 1150; CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Immediate mass household circumcision of all males in Abraham's encampment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqach Avraham eth-Yishmael bno... vayyamol eth-besar orlatham be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh ka-asher dibber itto Elohim*: *be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh* ('on the selfsame day').
historicalTrivia: Psalm 119:60 describes Abraham's action: 'I hasten and do not delay to keep your commandments'.

dominicalIntent: Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin (*Ve-Avraham ben-tish'im ve-thesha shanah*). At 99 years old, Abraham submits his own body to the painful rite of circumcision, sealing his lifelong faith with a physical mark.
cccReferences: CCC 145 (Abraham's heroic submission to God's command); CCC 1150; Rom 4:11.
historicalContext: Adult circumcision of a 99-year-old patriarch.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Avraham ben-tish'im ve-thesha shanah be-himmolo besar orlatho*.
historicalTrivia: Abraham's circumcision at 99 proves that age is no barrier to entering into deeper sacramental covenant with God.

dominicalIntent: And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin (*U-Yishmael bno ben-shelos esreh shanah*). 13-year-old Ishmael is circumcised alongside his father.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Ishmael included in household circumcision).
historicalContext: 13 years old was the traditional ANE puberty age for youth circumcision among Arabian tribes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-Yishmael bno ben-shelos esreh shanah be-himmolo eth besar orlatho*.
historicalTrivia: To this day, many traditional Islamic communities perform circumcision when a boy reaches 13 years of age, honoring Ishmael's age in Genesis 17:25.

dominicalIntent: That very same day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised (*Be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh nimmel Avraham u-Yishmael bno*). Re-emphasizing the exact day timestamp to underscore covenantal solidarity between father and son.
cccReferences: CCC 1150 (Covenant seal); CCC 145.
historicalContext: Simultaneous father and son covenant initiation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh nimmel Avraham u-Yishmael bno*: *nimmel* (was circumcised).
historicalTrivia: The repetition of *be-etzem ha-yom ha-zeh* (vv. 23, 26) highlights the historical precision of the event.

dominicalIntent: And all the men of his house, those born in the house and those bought with money from a foreigner, were circumcised with him. The entire household of faith is circumcised together, completing the institution of the Covenant of Circumcision. This prepares the way for the dramatic appearance of the Holy Trinity at Mamre in Genesis 18.
cccReferences: CCC 1252 (Household initiation into God's covenant prefiguring household Baptism); CCC 1150; CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Complete consecration of Abraham's multi-hundred member household camp.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-chol-anshey veytho yelid bayith u-miqnath-kesepu me-eth ben-nekhar nimmolu itto*.
historicalTrivia: Genesis 17 concludes with every male in Abraham's camp bearing the physical mark of the covenant, setting the stage for the divine visitation of Genesis 18.

dominicalIntent: The Lord appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre (*Vayyera elav YHVH be-eloney Mamre*), as he sat at the door of his tent in the heat of the day. THIS IS THE FAMOUS THEOPHANY OF MAMRE! The Lord appears to Abraham as he sits at his tent door during the midday heat (*ke-chom ha-yom*). In Christian tradition and iconography (e.g., Rublev's Trinity icon), the manifestation of Yahweh in three visitors at Mamre is the premier Old Testament prefiguration of the Holy Trinity.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The hospitality of Abraham at Mamre welcoming God); CCC 237 (Prefiguration of the Mystery of the Holy Trinity); CCC 706 (Theophany of Yahweh).
historicalContext: The terebinth grove of Mamre at Hebron, sitting at the tent flap during the scorching afternoon heat (*ke-chom ha-yom*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyera elav YHVH be-eloney Mamre ve-hu yoshev petach-ha-ohel ke-chom ha-yom*: *Vayyera* (and He appeared). *Petach-ha-ohel* (tent entrance).
crossReferences: Genesis 12:7; Genesis 13:18; Genesis 17:1; Hebrews 13:2; John 8:56; Rublev Trinity Icon.
historicalTrivia: St. Andrei Rublev's 15th-century 'Trinity Icon' depicts the three visitors of Genesis 18 seated around an altar-table, representing the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

dominicalIntent: He lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, three men were standing in front of him (*hinneh sheloshah anashim nitzavim alav*). When he saw them, he ran from the tent door to meet them and bowed himself to the earth. Abraham sees THREE MEN (*sheloshah anashim*), yet addresses them in the singular ('My Lord' / *Adonai* in v. 3)! This grammatical mystery (three persons, one Lord) reveals the Trinitarian nature of God. Abraham's swift running (*vayyaratz*) demonstrates heroic Christian hospitality (*philoxenia*).
cccReferences: CCC 237 (Trinitarian mystery: three men, one Lord); CCC 2571 (Abraham running to offer hospitality); Heb 13:2 (Entertaining angels unawares).
historicalContext: Hospitality (*philoxenia*) in desert Bedouin culture was a sacred, inviolable duty required to protect travelers from heat, thirst, and bandits.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyissa eynev vayyar ve-hinneh sheloshah anashim nitzavim alav... vayyaratz liqra'tham... vayyishtachu artzah*: *vayyishtachu* (prostrated himself to the earth).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 13:2 directly commentary on Genesis 18:2: 'Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares'.

dominicalIntent: He said: 'O Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, do not pass by your servant' (*Adonai im-na matzathi chen be-eyneykha al-na tha'avor me-al avdekha*). Abraham addresses the three visitors as *Adonai* ('My Lord' / 'Lord'). He places himself in the posture of a humble servant (*avdekha*), begging the Divine Presence to abide with him.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's humble prayer begging God to abide with him); CCC 2096 (Adoration); CCC 2665.
historicalContext: Formal Semitic address of high honor (*Adonai*) combined with self-deprecation (*avdekha*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Adonai im-na matzathi chen be-eyneykha...*: *Adonai* (Lord/Master, pointed as divine name). *Chen* (grace/favor).
historicalTrivia: In Masoretic text tradition, the vowels for *Adonai* in Genesis 18:3 are pointed with *Qamets* (the divine title), proving ancient Jewish recognition of God's presence.

dominicalIntent: 'Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.' Foot-washing (*rechatz ragleykhem*) is the supreme gesture of humble service. Christ fulfills this gesture at the Last Supper (John 13:1-15), washing the feet of His disciples and commanding us to serve one another.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Humble service of Abraham); CCC 520 (Christ washing the feet of the disciples); John 13:1-15.
historicalContext: Washing the dust of desert travel from visitors' feet before entering a tent or home was essential Levantine hospitality.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Yuqqach-na me'at-mayim ve-rachatzu ragleykhem ve-hishsha'anuthachath ha-etz*: *hishsha'anu* (lean back / rest yourselves).
historicalTrivia: 1 Timothy 5:10 lists 'washing the feet of the saints' as a key qualification for holy widows in the early Church, rooted in Genesis 18:4.

dominicalIntent: 'While I fetch a morsel of bread, that you may refresh your hearts, and after that you may pass on... So they said, Do as you have said.' Abraham humbly offers a 'morsel of bread' (*path-lechem*), but proceeds to prepare a lavish royal banquet! True Christian charity under-promises and over-delivers out of love.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Generosity of Eucharistic hospitality); CCC 1334 (Offering bread); CCC 2447.
historicalContext: Refreshing the heart (*se'adu livkhem*) with food before midday travel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-eqchah phath-lechem ve-si'adu livkhem achar tha'avoru... Vayyo'mru ken ta'aseh ka-asher dibbartah*: *se'adu* (refresh/sustain, root *sa'ad*).
historicalTrivia: Psalm 104:15 ('and bread to strengthen man's heart') uses the exact phrase *lechem yis'ad levav-enosh* from Genesis 18:5.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham went quickly into the tent to Sarah and said: 'Quick! Three seahs of fine flour! Knead it, and make cakes' (*Mahari shelosh se'im qemach soleth lushi u-asi ugoth*). Abraham runs to Sarah to prepare THREE SEAHS OF FINE FLOUR (*shelosh se'im qemach soleth*). In Matthew 13:33, Jesus uses this exact measure in the Parable of the Leaven: 'The Kingdom of heaven is like leaven which a woman took and hid in THREE MEASURES OF FLOUR (*sata tria*)!' Sarah's three measures prefigure the Eucharistic Bread of the Kingdom.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Eucharistic preparation of fine flour); CCC 1334 (Fine flour offerings); Matt 13:33.
historicalContext: Three seahs (*shelosh se'im*) equals approx. 1 Ephah (approx. 22 liters / 50 lbs of flour), an enormous royal feast quantity capable of feeding over 30 people!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Mahari shelosh se'im qemach soleth lushi u-asi ugoth*: *soleth* (fine/choice wheat flour). *Ugoth* (flat bread cakes baked on hot stones). LXX *tria meiktra*.
historicalTrivia: Matthew 13:33 (*sata tria*) is Jesus' direct quotation of the Septuagint translation of Genesis 18:6 (*tria meiktra* / three seahs of flour).

dominicalIntent: And Abraham ran to the herd and took a calf, tender and good (*ben-baqar rach va-tov*), and gave it to a young man, who prepared it quickly. Abraham runs (*ran*) to the herd to select the absolute best, most tender calf. He spares no expense for his guests, modeling the lavish generosity of God.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Lavish sacrificial hospitality); CCC 1383 (The Eucharistic feast); Luke 15:23.
historicalContext: Slaughtering a prime fatted calf (*ben-baqar*) was the highest luxury honor reserved for royal guests in ANE culture.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-el-ha-baqar rutz Avraham vayyiqach ben-baqar rach va-tov vayyitten el-ha-na'ar vaymraher la'asoth oto*.
historicalTrivia: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:23), the father commanding 'Bring the fatted calf and kill it' mirrors Abraham's royal hospitality in Genesis 18:7.

dominicalIntent: Then he took curds and milk and the calf that he had prepared, and set it before them. And he stood by them under the tree while they ate (*ve-hu-oved aleyhem thachath ha-etz vayyo'khelu*). Abraham stands by as a waiting servant while his guests eat! The patriarch of nations acts as table servant. Christ mirrors this at the Last Supper: 'I am among you as one who serves' (Luke 22:27).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham standing as servant at the table); CCC 520 (Christ as table servant); Luke 22:27.
historicalContext: Curds (*chemah*, clarified butter/yogurt) and milk (*chalav*) served alongside roasted meat under the shade of a sacred tree.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyichach chemah va-chalav u-ven-ha-baqar asher asah vayyitten li-phneyhem ve-hu-oved aleyhem thachath ha-etz vayyo'khelu*: *oved* (standing/waiting upon them).
historicalTrivia: Luke 12:37 records Jesus' promise to watchful servants: 'He will gird himself and have them sit at table, and he will come and serve them'—fulfilling Genesis 18:8.

dominicalIntent: They said to him, 'Where is Sarah your wife?' And he said, 'She is in the tent.' The divine visitors inquire about Sarah by her new royal name ('Sarah'), demonstrating divine knowledge of her renamed covenant identity.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Divine inquiry initiating the Messianic promise); CCC 489.
historicalContext: Respecting Middle Bronze Age tent privacy where women remained in the inner domestic tent compartment (*ohel*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru elav ayyeh Sarah ishtekha vayyo'mer hinneh ba-ohel*.
historicalTrivia: The visitors using the new name *Sarah* (revealed only in Gen 17:15) proved to Abraham that these guests possessed divine omniscience.

dominicalIntent: The Lord said: 'I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife shall have a son' (*Shov ashov eleykha ka-eth chayyah ve-hinneh-ven le-Sarah ishtekha*). And Sarah was listening at the tent door behind him. THE SOLEMN PROMISE OF ISAAC'S BIRTH! The visitor speaks as Yahweh ('I will surely return...'). This promise is cited by St. Paul in Romans 9:9 as the word of divine election.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (The promise of Isaac's miraculous birth); CCC 60 (Divine election); Rom 9:9; Gal 4:23.
historicalContext: Prophetic announcement timestamp *ka-eth chayyah* ('at the return of the season of life' = 9 months / next spring).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Shov ashov eleykha ka-eth chayyah ve-hinneh-ven le-Sarah...*: *Shov ashov* (infinitive absolute: 'I will returning return'). *Ka-eth chayyah* ('at the springtime of life').
historicalTrivia: Romans 9:9 quotes Genesis 18:10 word-for-word: 'For this is what the promise said: "About this time next year I will return, and Sarah shall have a son".'

dominicalIntent: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in years. The way of women had ceased to be with Sarah (*chadal lihyoth le-Sarah Orah ka-nashim*). The text underscores human biological impossibility: Abraham at 100, Sarah at 90, post-menopausal. Isaac's birth must be a 100% supernatural miracle of grace, prefiguring the Virgin Birth of Christ.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (Human impossibility overcome by divine power, preparing for the Virgin Birth); CCC 2374; Rom 4:19; Heb 11:11.
historicalContext: Physiological cessation of fertility (*orah ka-nashim*) confirming natural barrenness.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Avraham ve-Sarah zeqenim ba'im ba-yamim chadal lihyoth le-Sarah Orah ka-nashim*: *Orah ka-nashim* (menses / way of women).
historicalTrivia: Romans 4:19 notes that Abraham 'considered his own body as good as dead (*nenekrōmenon*), since he was about a hundred years old, and the barrenness of Sarah's womb'.

dominicalIntent: So Sarah laughed to herself (*Vattitzchaq Sarah be-qirbah*), saying: 'After I am worn out, and my lord is old, shall I have pleasure?' Sarah laughs inwardly out of disbelief. Human nature struggles to grasp the boundless power of divine grace.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Sarah's inner struggle with faith); CCC 489; CCC 145.
historicalContext: Private inner monologue behind the tent curtain.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattitzchaq Sarah be-qirbah le'mor acharey velothi hayethah-li ednah va-adoni zaqen*: *Vattitzchaq* (and she laughed, root *tzachaq*). *Ednah* (delight/pleasure). *Adoni* ('my lord', referring to Abraham).
historicalTrivia: 1 Peter 3:6 praises Sarah's virtue: 'as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord (*kyrion*)', citing her inner monologue from Genesis 18:12 (*va-adoni zaqen*).

dominicalIntent: The Lord said to Abraham: 'Why did Sarah laugh and say, "Shall I indeed bear a child, now that I am old?"' Yahweh exposes Sarah's hidden inner laughter! God knows the secret thoughts of every heart (Ps 139:2).
cccReferences: CCC 2569 (God knowing the inner heart); CCC 2083; Ps 139:2.
historicalContext: Divine omniscience piercing behind the physical tent flap.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH el-Avraham lammah zeh tzachaqah Sarah...*.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 4:13 ('no creature is hidden from his sight, but all are naked and exposed') is illustrated by God detecting Sarah's silent inner laughter behind the tent wall.

dominicalIntent: Is anything too hard for the Lord? (*Ha-yippale me-YHVH davar*). At the appointed time I will return to you, about this time next year, and Sarah shall have a son. THIS IS ONE OF THE GREATEST DECLARATIONS OF DIVINE OMNIPOTENCE IN SCRIPTURE! 'Is anything too hard for Yahweh?' The Archangel Gabriel quotes this exact verse to the Virgin Mary at the Annunciation: 'For with God nothing will be impossible' (Luke 1:37)!
cccReferences: CCC 269 (God's Almightiness: 'Nothing is impossible with God'); CCC 273 (Faith in divine omnipotence); CCC 497; Luke 1:37; Jer 32:17.
historicalContext: Rhetorical divine question asserting absolute sovereignty over biological laws.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ha-yippale me-YHVH davar la-mo'ed ashuv eleykha...*: *yippale* (be too wonderful/extraordinary/impossible, root *pala*). LXX *mē adynatei para tō Theō rhēma*, quoted in Luke 1:37.
crossReferences: Luke 1:37; Jeremiah 32:17; Jeremiah 32:27; Matthew 19:26; Mark 10:27; Zechariah 8:6.
historicalTrivia: Luke 1:37 (*oti ouk adynatēsei para tō Theō pan rhēma*) is Gabriel's Greek translation of Genesis 18:14 LXX (*mī adynatei para tō Theō rhēma*).

dominicalIntent: But Sarah denied it, saying, 'I did not laugh,' for she was afraid. He said, 'No, but you did laugh' (*Lo ki tzachaqt*). Sarah denies her laughter out of fear, but God gently insists on truth: 'No, but you did laugh.' God corrects our fear and brings us into the light of truth.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Correction in truth); CCC 2571 (Sarah brought to mature faith); Heb 11:11.
historicalContext: Fearful human denial in the presence of divine omniscience.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattakhachash Sarah le'mor lo tzachaqti ki yare'ah vayyo'mer lo ki tzachaqt*.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:11 records the ultimate spiritual victory: 'By faith Sarah herself received power to conceive, even when she was past the age, since she considered him faithful who had promised'.

dominicalIntent: Then the men set out from there, and they looked down toward Sodom. And Abraham went with them to set them on their way (*ve-Avraham holech immam le-shallecham*). Abraham escorts his divine guests as they turn their gaze toward Sodom. The transition from the peaceful, holy hospitality of Mamre to the impending judgment of Sodom.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham walking with God); CCC 1021 (Impending divine judgment).
historicalContext: Escorting guests (*le-shallecham*) to the boundary of one's territory was the final act of Semitic hospitality.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyaqumu misham ha-anashim vayyashqiphu al-pney Sedom ve-Avraham holech immam le-shallecham*: *vayyashqiphu* (looked down from a high cliff).
historicalTrivia: From the high ridge east of Hebron (Beni Na'im, elevation 3,100 ft), one can look directly down 4,000 feet into the Dead Sea depression toward Sodom.

dominicalIntent: The Lord said: 'Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?' (*Ha-mkhasseh ani me-Avraham asher ani oseh*). GOD SHARES HIS SECRETS WITH ABRAHAM! God treats Abraham not as a slave, but as a trusted friend (*chaver*). Christ repeats this intimacy to His disciples: 'No longer do I call you servants... but I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you' (John 15:15).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham as the Friend of God admitted into divine counsel); CCC 206 (Divine intimacy); John 15:15; Jas 2:23; Amos 3:7.
historicalContext: A sovereign king sharing royal judicial decrees with a trusted covenant partner (*councillor*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-YHVH amar ha-mkhasseh ani me-Avraham asher ani oseh*: *mkhasseh* (covering/concealing).
historicalTrivia: Amos 3:7 directly reflects Genesis 18:17: 'For the Lord God does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets'.

dominicalIntent: Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him (*ve-nivrechu vo kol goyey ha-aretz*). God re-affirms the Messianic Promise: Abraham's election is ordered to the universal salvation of all nations.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (Universal scope of Abraham's election); CCC 762; Gal 3:8.
historicalContext: Divine justification for revealing upcoming geopolitical judgments to the father of nations.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Avraham hayoh yihyeh le-goy gadol ve-atzum ve-nivrechu vo kol goyey ha-aretz*.
historicalTrivia: The inclusion of *ve-atzum* ('and mighty') alongside *goy gadol* emphasizes the moral and spiritual power of Abraham's lineage.

dominicalIntent: For I have chosen him (*ki yedativ*), that he may command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord by doing righteousness and justice (*li-shmor derekh YHVH la'asoth tzedaqah u-mishpat*). THE PURPOSE OF ELECTION! God chose (*yedativ* = 'knew/loved') Abraham so that he would raise his household to keep **the Way of the Lord** (*derekh YHVH*) by doing **righteousness and justice** (*tzedaqah u-mishpat*). Early Christianity was called 'The Way' (Acts 9:2), rooted directly in Genesis 18:19!
cccReferences: CCC 2221-2226 (The primary duty of parents to educate their children in the faith and moral law); CCC 2571; Acts 9:2.
historicalContext: Patriarchal covenant education (*katechesis*) transmitting moral and liturgical law to successive generations.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki yedativ le-ma'an asher yetzavveh eth-banav ve-eth-beytho acharav ve-shamru derekh YHVH la'asoth tzedaqah u-mishpat*: *yedativ* ('I have known/chosen him intimately'). *Derekh YHVH* ('the Way of Yahweh').
historicalTrivia: The earliest title for the Christian Church in the Book of Acts was 'The Way' (*Hē Hodos*, Acts 9:2; 19:9), directly deriving from *derekh YHVH* of Genesis 18:19.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord said: 'Because the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great and their sin is very grave' (*ki-chavthah me'od*). THE OUTCRY OF SIN! The 'outcry' (*tza'aqah*) of Sodom's victims reaches heaven. The Catechism lists the sin of Sodom (unnatural perversion and oppression of the weak) among the four **Sins that Cry to Heaven for Vengeance**.
cccReferences: CCC 1867 (The sin of the Sodomites listed as one of the four sins that cry to heaven for vengeance); CCC 1854; CCC 2357; Gen 4:10; Jas 5:4.
historicalContext: In ancient legal terminology, *tza'aqah* was the formal victim's cry for judicial intervention before the king's throne against violent oppressors.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH tza'aqath Sedom va-Amorah ki-rabbah ve-chattathah ki chavthah me'od*: *tza'aqath* (outcry of victims). *Chavthah* (heavy/grave).
historicalTrivia: CCC 1867 lists the four sins that cry to heaven: (1) The blood of Abel, (2) The sin of the Sodomites, (3) The cry of the oppressed in Egypt, (4) Cheating laborers of their just wages.

dominicalIntent: 'I will go down to see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry that has come to me; and if not, I will know.' God's investigation displays perfect judicial fairness. God never judges on rumor, but inspects with total justice, setting the standard for human magistrates.
cccReferences: CCC 1854 (Divine justice and objective investigation); CCC 2109.
historicalContext: Judicial inspection (*descent for verdict*) by the Supreme Judge prior to sentence execution.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Aredah-na ve-er'eh ha-ke-tza'aqathah ha-ba'ah elai asu kalah ve-im-lo eda'ah*: *Aredah-na* ('Let me descend now').
historicalTrivia: The anthropomorphic language *Aredah-na ve-er'eh* ('I will go down and see') demonstrates divine condescension adjusting to human legal comprehension.

dominicalIntent: So the men turned from there and went toward Sodom, but Abraham still stood before the Lord (*ve-Avraham odennu oved li-phney YHVH*). ABRAHAM'S INTERCESSION BEGINS! While the two angelic messengers proceed toward Sodom, Abraham remains standing before Yahweh. Abraham steps into the role of High Priest and Intercessor, standing in the gap between divine justice and human sin.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's intercession for Sodom as the archetype of all Christian intercessory prayer); CCC 2634 (Intercession asking on behalf of others); CCC 2572.
historicalContext: Standing before Yahweh (*oved li-phney YHVH*) was the formal posture of a priest or prophet offering intercessory prayer.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiphnu misham ha-anashim vayyelechu Sedomah ve-Avraham odennu oved li-phney YHVH*: *oved li-phney* ('standing before / ministering in the presence of').
historicalTrivia: An ancient scribal correction (*Tiqqun Sopherim*) notes that the original text read 'and Yahweh still stood before Abraham', but scribes altered it out of reverence to 'and Abraham still stood before Yahweh'.

dominicalIntent: Then Abraham drew near and said: 'Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?' (*Ha-tophseh tzaddik im-rasha*). Abraham DRAWS NEAR (*vayyiggash*) to God! True prayer draws near to the Divine Presence with filial boldness. Abraham appeals to God's own character: divine justice cannot slay the righteous (*tzaddik*) with the wicked (*rasha*).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham drawing near to God in bold intercession); CCC 2610 (Filial boldness in prayer); Heb 4:16; Heb 10:22.
historicalContext: Drawing near (*nagash*) in ANE legal protocol meant stepping forward to address the judge's bench.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiggash Avraham vayyo'mer ha-tophseh tzaddik im-rasha*: *Vayyiggash* (and he drew near / stepped forward, root *nagash*). *Tzaddik* (righteous). *Rasha* (wicked).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 4:16 ('Let us then with confidence draw near (*proserchōmetha*) to the throne of grace') uses the LXX equivalent of *vayyiggash* from Genesis 18:23.

dominicalIntent: Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city. Will you then sweep away the place and not spare it for the fifty righteous who are in it? Abraham's intercession introduces the principle of **substitutionary righteousness**: for the sake of a righteous remnant, God spares the whole city! This finds supreme fulfillment in Jesus Christ, the ONE perfectly Righteous Man, for whose sake God spares and redeems the entire world!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Principle of vicarious salvation and intercession); CCC 615 (Christ as the Righteous One saving the many); Rom 5:19.
historicalContext: Pleading vicarious merit (*tzidqath tzaddik*) to shield an entire metropolitan district from military execution.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ulay yesh chamishim tzaddiqim be-thoch ha-ir ha-aph tophseh ve-lo-thissa la-maqom le-ma'an chamishim ha-tzaddiqim asher be-qirbah*: *thissa* (pardon/forgive/spare, lit. 'lift up').
historicalTrivia: Jeremiah 5:1 echoes Genesis 18:24: 'Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem... if you can find a man, one who does justice and seeks truth, then I will pardon her'.

dominicalIntent: Far be it from you to do such a thing, to put the righteous to death with the wicked, so that the righteous fare as the wicked! Far be that from you! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justice? (*ha-Shophet kol-ha-aretz lo ya'aseh mishpat*). Abraham proclaims the absolute justice of God: 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?' God's justice is perfect, holy, and unassailable.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Appealing to divine justice and mercy in prayer); CCC 212 (God as supreme Judge of all the earth); CCC 1021.
historicalContext: Formal theological title *Shophet kol-ha-aretz* ('Judge of all the earth').
translationNuances: Hebrew *Chalilah lekha me-asoth ka-davar ha-zeh... ha-Shophet kol-ha-aretz lo ya'aseh mishpat*: *Chalilah lekha* ('Profane / Far be it from you!'). *Shophet* (Judge).
historicalTrivia: Romans 3:6 quotes the theology of Genesis 18:25: 'By no means! For then how could God judge the world?'

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said: 'If I find at Sodom fifty righteous in the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake' (*ve-nasathi le-chol-ha-maqom ba-avuram*). God grants Abraham's first petition! God's mercy eagerly looks for reasons to spare rather than destroy.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God accepting intercessory prayer); CCC 212; CCC 1847.
historicalContext: Judicial grant of stay of execution based on vicarious righteous presence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH Im-emtzah ve-Sedom chamishim tzaddiqim... ve-nasathi le-chol-ha-maqom ba-avuram*: *ve-nasathi* (and I will forgive/pardon).
historicalTrivia: The verb *nasa* ('to pardon / lift up sin') used here is the primary Old Testament verb for divine forgiveness.

dominicalIntent: Abraham answered and said: 'Behold, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes' (*ve-anochi afar va-epher*). PROFOUND HUMILITY IN PRAYER! Abraham acknowledges his creaturely nothingness: 'I who am but dust and ashes' (*afar va-epher*). Used in the Ash Wednesday liturgy, this verse teaches that effective intercession combines filial boldness with deep humility.
cccReferences: CCC 2559 (Humility as the foundation of prayer); CCC 2571 (Abraham's humility in intercession: 'dust and ashes'); CCC 1439; Ash Wednesday Liturgy.
historicalContext: Ritual self-abasement formula (*afar va-epher*) acknowledging mortal fragility before the Creator.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'an Avraham vayyo'mer Hinneh-na ho'althi ledabber el-Adonai ve-anochi afar va-epher*: *afar va-epher* (dust and ash - poetic rhyme).
crossReferences: Job 30:19; Job 42:6; Ecclesiastes 12:7; Sirach 10:9; Ash Wednesday Liturgy.
historicalTrivia: The Ash Wednesday formula *Remember man that thou art dust, and unto dust thou shalt return* draws directly from Genesis 3:19 and Genesis 18:27 (*afar va-epher*).

dominicalIntent: Suppose five of the fifty righteous are lacking. Will you destroy the whole city for lack of five? And he said: 'I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.' Abraham begins his step-by-step bargaining of mercy, reducing the number from 50 to 45.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Persistent, step-by-step intercession); CCC 2613 (Importunate prayer).
historicalContext: Incremental judicial petitioning before the divine court.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ulay yakhserun chamishim ha-tzaddiqim chamashah ha-tashchith ba-chamashah eth-kol-ha-ir...*.
historicalTrivia: Abraham's persistent stepping down of numbers prefigures Jesus' parables on persistent prayer (the Friend at Midnight, Luke 11; the Persistent Widow, Luke 18).

dominicalIntent: Again he spoke to him and said: 'Suppose forty are found there.' He answered: 'For the sake of forty I will not do it.' Abraham presses forward to 40. True intercessory prayer does not stop at the first answer, but perseveres in love.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Perseverance in intercessory prayer); CCC 2742.
historicalContext: Continued diplomatic intercession for human lives.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo-seph od ledabber elav vayyo'mer ulay yimmatz'un sham arba'im vayyo'mer lo e'eseh ba-avur ha-arba'im*.
historicalTrivia: Each time Abraham reduces the number, God instantly grants the request without hesitation, showing divine eagerness to bestow mercy.

dominicalIntent: Then he said: 'Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak. Suppose thirty are found there.' He answered: 'I will not do it, if I find thirty there.' Abraham humbly asks God not to be angry (*al-na yichar la-Adonai*). Reaching 30.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Reverent persistence in prayer); CCC 2100.
historicalContext: Deepening reverence during intense judicial intercession.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer al-na yichar la-Adonai va-adabberah ulay yimmatz'un sham sheloshim...*.
historicalTrivia: Gideon uses Abraham's exact phrase *al-na yichar* in Judges 6:39 when asking for his second fleece test.

dominicalIntent: He said: 'Behold, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord. Suppose twenty are found there.' He answered: 'For the sake of twenty I will not destroy it.' Abraham reduces the count to 20.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Importunate intercession); CCC 2634.
historicalContext: Approaching the absolute minimum righteous core required to preserve a city.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer hinneh-na ho'althi ledabber el-Adonai ulay yimmatz'un sham esrim...*.
historicalTrivia: 20 righteous persons would represent less than 1% of Sodom's population, showing how far divine mercy extends for a tiny righteous remnant.

dominicalIntent: Then he said: 'Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak again but this once. Suppose ten are found there.' He answered: 'For the sake of ten I will not destroy it' (*Lo ashchith ba-avur ha-asarah*). THE FINAL INTERCESSION AT TEN! Abraham stops at **TEN** (*asarah*). Ten represents a complete minyan / family core (Lot, his wife, 2 married daughters, 2 sons-in-law, 2 unmarried daughters, etc.). God promises: 'For the sake of TEN I will not destroy it!' Even ten righteous souls would have saved Sodom. But Sodom lacked even ten righteous persons, demonstrating the absolute justice of its impending destruction.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The culmination of Abraham's intercession: God willing to spare Sodom for just ten righteous); CCC 2572; CCC 1867; Jer 5:1.
historicalContext: Ten (*asarah*) was the minimum legal quorum required for a recognized judicial assembly or worshipping community in ancient Semitic culture.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer al-na yichar la-Adonai va-adabberah ach ha-pa'am ulay yimmatz'un sham asarah vayyo'mer Lo ashchith ba-avur ha-asarah*: *ach ha-pa'am* ('only this once!').
historicalTrivia: The Jewish requirement of a *Minyan* (a quorum of 10 adult believers required for public synagogue prayer) is traditionally rooted in the 10 righteous needed to save Sodom in Genesis 18:32.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord went his way, when he had finished speaking to Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place (*ve-Avraham shav le-meqomo*). The dialogue concludes. God departs to execute judgment, while Abraham returns to Hebron. Abraham has done all that prayer could do; he rests in total trust in divine justice and mercy.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The conclusion of Abraham's prayer of intercession, leaving all in God's hands); CCC 2572; CCC 1021.
historicalContext: Conclusion of the divine interview at the Hebron ridge overlooking the Jordan Valley.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyelech YHVH ka-asher kullah ledabber el-Avraham ve-Avraham shav le-meqomo*: *kullah* (had completed/finished).
historicalTrivia: Abraham returning to 'his place' (*meqomo*) refers to his altar at Mamre/Hebron, where he would stand early the next morning to watch the smoke of Sodom rise (Gen 19:27).

dominicalIntent: The two angels came to Sodom in the evening (*U-sheny ha-mal'akhim ba'u Sedomah ba-erev*), and Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he rose to meet them and bowed himself with his face to the earth. Two angels (sent from the three at Mamre) arrive at Sodom in the evening. Lot sitting in the gate (*be-sha'ar Sedom*) shows he had become a prominent civic magistrate in corrupt Sodom. Yet Lot retains enough righteousness to offer hospitality, bowing in prostration.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Lot's hospitality amidst Sodom); CCC 1854 (Civic magistrate in a corrupt city); 2 Peter 2:7-8 (Righteous Lot).
historicalContext: The city gate (*sha'ar*) was the ancient Near Eastern venue for elder councils, legal trials, and civic governance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-sheny ha-mal'akhim ba'u Sedomah ba-erev ve-Lot yoshev be-sha'ar Sedom vayyar-Lot vayyaqam liqra'tham vayyishtachu appayim artzah*: *sheny ha-mal'akhim* (the two angels). *Sha'ar* (city gate).
historicalTrivia: 2 Peter 2:7-8 describes Lot: 'He was greatly distressed by the licentious conduct of the ungodly, for that righteous man dwelt among them day after day, vexing his righteous soul'.

dominicalIntent: He said: 'My lords, turn aside, I pray you, to your servant's house and spend the night and wash your feet...' They said: 'No, we will spend the night in the street.' Lot insists on sheltering the travelers because he knows the extreme moral danger of Sodom's public square at night.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Urgency of hospitality in a dark world); CCC 1867; Heb 13:2.
historicalContext: Public plazas (*rechov*) in ANE cities were unsafe for travelers at night; offering private lodging was vital for life safety.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Hinneh na-adonai suru na el-beyth avdekhem ve-linu ve-rachatzu ragleykhem... vayyo'mru lo ki va-rechov nalim*: *rechov* (city square/plaza).
historicalTrivia: The visitors' initial refusal ('No, we will spend the night in the street') tested Lot's persistence in hospitality, mirroring Jesus in Luke 24:28.

dominicalIntent: But he urged them strongly; so they turned aside to him and entered his house. And he made them a feast and baked unleavened bread (*matzoth*), and they ate. Lot bakes unleavened bread (*matzoth*) for his guests! This is the FIRST MENTION OF UNLEAVENED BREAD (*matzoth*) in Scripture, prefiguring the haste of the Passover and the Eucharistic Host.
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Unleavened bread as biblical sign); CCC 1339 (Passover matzoth prefiguring the Eucharist); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Quick baking of unleavened bread (*matzoth*) was required when time did not permit yeast fermentation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiph'tzar-bam me'od vayyasuru elav... u-matzoth aphah vayyo'khelu*: *matzoth* (unleavened bread cakes). *Vayyiph'tzar* (urged/pressed strongly).
historicalTrivia: This first appearance of *matzoth* in Genesis 19:3 establishes unleavened bread as the sacred bread of urgent deliverance.

dominicalIntent: Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, both young and old, all the people to the last man, surrounded the house (*kol-ha-am mi-qqatzeh*). TOTAL DEPRAVITY OF SODOM! The mob surrounds the house: 'young and old, ALL the people to the last man' (*kol-ha-am mi-qqatzeh*). Not even ten righteous men could be found in Sodom; the entire city was united in violent wickedness.
cccReferences: CCC 1867 (Systemic gravity of Sodom's sin); CCC 2357 (Universal corruption of Sodom); CCC 1854.
historicalContext: Aggressive mob encirclement of a magistrate's home to violate asylum rights.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Tterem yishkavu ve-anshey ha-ir anshey Sedom nasabbu al-ha-bayith mi-na'ar ve-ad-zaqen kol-ha-am mi-qqatzeh*: *kol-ha-am mi-qqatzeh* ('every single person to the outermost perimeter').
historicalTrivia: The textual note *kol-ha-am mi-qqatzeh* ('all the people from every quarter') confirms that Abraham's minimum count of 10 righteous (Gen 18:32) did not exist.

dominicalIntent: They called to Lot: 'Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them' (*ve-neda'ah otham*). THE SIN OF SODOM! The mob demands the guests be handed over for gang rape (*ve-neda'ah* = euphemism for sexual assault). This is a double atrocity: violent violation of sacred hospitality and unnatural homosexual assault. The Catechism (CCC 2357) explicitly cites this passage regarding homosexual acts as gravely contrary to natural law.
cccReferences: CCC 2357 (Homosexual acts as gravely contrary to natural law, citing Genesis 19:1-11); CCC 1867 (Sin of Sodom crying to heaven); CCC 2259; Jude 1:7.
historicalContext: Homosexual gang rape of male travelers as an act of xenophobic subjugation and extreme moral depravity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqre'u el-Lot vayyo'mru lo ayyeh ha-anashim asher-ba'u eleykha ha-laylah hotzi'em eleynu ve-neda'ah otham*: *neda'ah* (Qal cohortative of *yada*, to know carnally/sexually).
historicalTrivia: Jude 1:7 commentary on Sodom: 'Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities... indulged in sexual immorality and pursued unnatural lust (*sarkos heteras*), serving as an example of eternal fire'.

dominicalIntent: Lot went out to the men at the entrance, shut the door after him. Lot steps outside to reason with the mob, shutting the door behind him to protect his guests.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Lot attempting to protect guests); CCC 1854.
historicalContext: A magistrate confronting an armed mob outside his own house threshold.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayetze alehem Lot ha-pethchah ve-ha-deleth sagar acharav*: *pethach* (doorway/entrance). *Deleth* (wooden door leaf).
historicalTrivia: Distinction between *pethach* (the architectural doorway opening) and *deleth* (the solid movable door panel).

dominicalIntent: And said: 'I beg you, my brothers, do not act so wickedly' (*Al-na achay thare'u*). Lot addresses the mob as 'brothers' (*achay*), begging them not to commit this monstrous evil.
cccReferences: CCC 2357 (Denunciation of Sodom's wicked act); CCC 1867.
historicalContext: Conciliatory appeal to civic brotherhood to avert a mob crime.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mar al-na achay thare'u*: *thare'u* (do evil/wickedness, Hiphil of *ra'a*).
historicalTrivia: Lot's plea echoes Abram's peace proposal in Gen 13:8 ('we are brothers'), but while Abram accepted peace, Sodom rejected it.

dominicalIntent: 'Behold, I have two daughters who have not known any man; let me bring them out to you... only do nothing to these men, for they have come under the shelter of my roof.' Lot offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests! While Lot's defense of hospitality is fierce, his compromise offering his daughters reveals the moral confusion caused by living in Sodom.
cccReferences: CCC 1854 (Moral confusion resulting from living in corrupt culture); CCC 2571; Judg 19:24.
historicalContext: Extreme ancient view of hospitality where protecting guests (*shadow of my roof* / *tzell qorathi*) took priority over family members.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hinneh-na li shtey vanoth asher lo-yadh'u ish... raq la-anashim ha-el al-ta'asu davar ki-al-ken ba'u be-tzell qorathi*: *tzell qorathi* ('shadow of my roof beam').
historicalTrivia: St. Augustine (*Contra Mendacium*) notes that Lot chose a lesser sin (offering daughters) to prevent a greater sin (gang rape of guests), but emphasizes that both were morally flawed.

dominicalIntent: But they said: 'Stand back!' And they said: 'This fellow came to sojourn, and he has become the judge! Now we will deal worse with you than with them.' Then they pressed hard against Lot and drew near to break the door. The mob turns on Lot! They mock him as a foreign sojourner (*ger*) acting as a judge, threatening to rape Lot himself. Worldly mobs turn viciously on those who reprove their sin.
cccReferences: CCC 1867 (Totalitarian malice of unrepentant sinners); CCC 1854; Wis 2:12-20.
historicalContext: Xenophobic rejection of a resident alien (*ger*) who dares to exercise moral correction over local citizens.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru Gesash-halah... ha-echad ba-la-gur vayyishpot shaphot attah nare'a lekha mehem... vayyiggeshu lishbor ha-deleth*: *Gesash-halah* ('Step back! Stand aside!').
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 2:12 describes the exact attitude of Sodom's mob: 'Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us and opposes our actions'.

dominicalIntent: But the men reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house with them and shut the door. The two angels intervene! They pull Lot inside to safety and shut the door. Divine intervention rescues the imperiled servant of God.
cccReferences: CCC 332 (Angels protecting the righteous); CCC 2571 (Divine rescue); Ps 91:11.
historicalContext: Angelic physical intervention pulling a magistrate out of mob violence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishlechu ha-anashim eth-yadam vayyavi'u eth-Lot eleyhem ha-baythah ve-eth-ha-deleth sagaru*.
historicalTrivia: The angels shutting the door (*ha-deleth sagaru*) echoes God shutting the door of Noah's Ark (Gen 7:16), marking sanctuary safety.

dominicalIntent: And they struck with blindness the men who were at the entrance of the house, both small and great, so that they wore themselves out groping for the door (*vayyil'u limtzo ha-pethach*). THE ANGELS STRIKE THE MOB WITH BLINDNESS (*sanverim*)! Physical blindness mirrors their intense spiritual blindness. Even when struck blind, the mob furiously continues groping for the door to commit sin! Sin blinds the soul and drives it to self-destruction.
cccReferences: CCC 1865 (Spiritual blindness resulting from habitual mortal sin); CCC 2000; 2 Kings 6:18; Acts 13:11.
historicalContext: Supernatural blindness (*sanverim*, confusion of vision / flash blindness) inflicted on the aggressors.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-eth-ha-anashim asher-petach ha-bayith hikku ba-sanverim mi-qqaton ve-ad-gadol vayyil'u limtzo ha-pethach*: *sanverim* (blinding light / dazzlement). *Vayyil'u* (they exhausted themselves).
historicalTrivia: The rare word *sanverim* (blinding dazzlement) occurs only twice in Scripture: here in Genesis 19:11 and in 2 Kings 6:18 when Elisha strikes the Syrian army blind.

dominicalIntent: Then the men said to Lot: 'Have you anyone else here? Sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone you have in the city, bring them out of the place.' The angels command an immediate evacuation! Divine mercy seeks to save all who belong to Lot's household.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Evacuation of the righteous before judgment); CCC 1655 (Household salvation); 2 Peter 2:9.
historicalContext: Urgent evacuation order issued prior to divine bombardment of a doomed city.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru ha-anashim el-Lot Od mi-lekha phoh chathan u-vaneykha u-venotheykha ve-chol asher-lekha va-ir hotze min-ha-maqom*.
historicalTrivia: Revelation 18:4 ('Come out of her, my people, lest you take part in her sins') directly quotes the angelic evacuation command of Genesis 19:12.

dominicalIntent: 'For we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against its people has become great before the Lord, and the Lord has sent us to destroy it.' The angels declare their commission: Yahweh has sent them to execute judgment upon Sodom because its sin cries to heaven.
cccReferences: CCC 1867 (Sin crying to heaven requiring judgment); CCC 332 (Angels executing divine judgment); CCC 1021.
historicalContext: Angelic executioners of divine judicial decrees against irredeemable cities.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki-mashchithim anachnu eth-ha-maqom ha-zeh ki-gadlah tza'aqatham eth-pney YHVH vay-shallechenu YHVH le-shachathah*: *shachath* (to destroy/ruin).
historicalTrivia: The verb *shachath* (destroy) used here for Sodom's judgment is the exact verb used for the Flood in Genesis 6:13.

dominicalIntent: So Lot went out and said to his sons-in-law, who were to marry his daughters: 'Up! Get out of this place, for the Lord is about to destroy the city.' But he seemed to his sons-in-law to be jesting (*vayyehi khi-metzacheq be-eyney chathanav*). Lot warns his sons-in-law, but they think he is JOKING (*metzacheq*)! The worldly mind dismisses divine warnings of judgment as ridiculous fairy tales, sleeping right up to the hour of destruction.
cccReferences: CCC 678 (Worldly blindness mocking the warnings of final judgment); CCC 1021; Luke 17:28-30; 2 Peter 3:3-4.
historicalContext: Betrothed sons-in-law (*chathanim*) bound by marriage contract to Lot's daughters.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayetze Lot vaydabber el-chathanav... Qumu tze'u min-ha-maqom ha-zeh... vayyehi khi-metzacheq be-eyney chathanav*: *metzacheq* (joking / jesting / making sport).
historicalTrivia: Luke 17:28-30 records Jesus' warning: 'Likewise as it was in the days of Lot... so will it be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed'.

dominicalIntent: When morning dawned, the angels urged Lot, saying: 'Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are here, lest you be swept away in the punishment of the city' (*pen-tissapeh be-avon ha-ir*). Dawn breaks! The angels urge immediate departure. Delaying when God commands flight leads to destruction.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Urgency of fleeing sin without hesitation); CCC 1021; 2 Cor 6:2.
historicalContext: Dawn (*khe-moth ha-shachar*) marked the execution hour for divine judgment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-khe-moth ha-shachar ala vay-a'itzu ha-mal'akhim be-Lot... pen-tissapeh be-avon ha-ir*: *vay-a'itzu* (urged/pressed in haste). *Avon* (iniquity/punishment).
historicalTrivia: The urgency *U-khe-moth ha-shachar ala* ('As dawn broke') establishes that divine grace acts swiftly at the first light of dawn.

dominicalIntent: But he lingered (*vayyithmahmah*). So the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the Lord being merciful to him (*be-chemleth YHVH alav*), and they brought him out and set him outside the city. LOT LINGERS (*vayyithmahmah*)! Even with destruction imminent, Lot hesitates. But God's mercy (*chemleth YHVH*) is so great that the angels SEIZE THEM BY THE HAND and drag them out of the city! God's grace literally pulls us out of danger when our willpower falters.
cccReferences: CCC 2000 (Preventing grace grabbing the sinner to pull him to safety); CCC 2571 (Mercy of God over Lot's lingering); CCC 212.
historicalContext: Angels physically grasping human hands to pull reluctant evacuees beyond the municipal gate.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyithmahmah vayyachaziqu ha-anashim be-yado u-ve-yad-ishto... be-chemleth YHVH alav vayyotzi'uhu vayyannichuhu mi-chutz la-ir*: *Vayyithmahmah* (and he lingered/hesitated). *Be-chemleth* ('in Yahweh's compassion/pity').
historicalTrivia: Jude 1:23 commands Christians to imitate the angels of Genesis 19:16: 'Save others by snatching them out of the fire (*ek pyros harpazontes*)'.

dominicalIntent: And as they brought them out, one said: 'Flee for your life! Do not look back (*Al-tabbet achareykha*) nor stop anywhere in the valley; flee to the hills, lest you be swept away.' THE TRIPLE COMMAND OF DELIVERANCE: (1) Flee for your life, (2) DO NOT LOOK BACK, (3) Flee to the mountains! Looking back signifies longing for the old life of sin. Christ commands: 'No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God' (Luke 9:62).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Fleeing sin without looking back); CCC 1428 (Renunciation of past sin); Luke 9:62; Luke 17:32.
historicalContext: Fleeing the Dead Sea rift basin up into the high Judean mountain caves.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi khe-hotzi'am otham ha-chutzah vayyo'mer Himmalet al-naphshekha al-tabbet achareykha ve-al-ta'amod be-chol-ha-kikkar ha-harah himmalet pen-tissapeh*: *Al-tabbet* ('Do not gaze/look back!').
historicalTrivia: Jesus in Luke 17:32 gives one of the shortest and most solemn commands in the Gospel: 'REMEMBER LOT'S WIFE!' (*mnēmoneuete tēs gynaikos Lōt*).

dominicalIntent: And Lot said to them: 'Oh, no, my lords!' (*Al-na Adonai*). Lot hesitates again, pleading against fleeing into the steep mountains. Human weakness fears the steep mountain paths of high perfection.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Human frailty pleading for easier refuge); CCC 2004.
historicalContext: Lot fearfully assessing the rugged 3,000-ft mountain ascent.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Lot alehem Al-na Adonai*: *Al-na* ('Oh no, please!').
historicalTrivia: Lot's plea reveals his spiritual weakness compared to Abraham: Abraham loved the mountain altars, while Lot feared the mountains.

dominicalIntent: 'Behold, your servant has found favor in your sight, and you have shown great mercy to me in saving my life; but I cannot escape to the hills, lest the disaster overtake me and I die.' Lot acknowledges God's great mercy (*chesed*), yet fears he cannot survive the mountain trek.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Acknowledging mercy yet harboring fear); CCC 1817.
historicalContext: Fear of exhaustion or wild beasts on the mountain slopes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hinneh-na matza avdekha chen be-eyneykha vatagdel chasdekha... ve-anochi lo ukhal le-himmalet ha-harah*: *chasdekha* (your covenant mercy/lovingkindness).
historicalTrivia: The word *chesed* (covenant mercy) used by Lot marks his gratitude for angelic rescue.

dominicalIntent: 'Behold, this city is near enough to flee to, and it is a little one. Let me escape there—is it not a little one?—and my life will be saved!' Lot begs to flee to the small nearby city of Bela, renaming it **Zoar** ('Little One'). God accommodates human weakness, granting refuge in Zoar.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God accommodating human weakness in prayer); CCC 212.
historicalContext: Bela (Zoar), situated at the southeastern tip of the Dead Sea (modern es-Safi, Jordan).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Hinneh-na ha-ir ha-zoth qerovah la-nus shammah ve-hi mitz'ar immaleta na shammah ha-lo mitz'ar hi u-thechi naphshi*: *mitz'ar* (small/little thing -> *Tzo'ar*).
historicalTrivia: Zoar survived the cataclysm and remained an inhabited agricultural oasis through the Roman, Byzantine, and Islamic periods (mosaics of Zoar in Madaba Map).

dominicalIntent: He said to him: 'Behold, I grant you this favor also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken' (*Nasathi phaneykha gam la-davar ha-zeh*). Divine condescension! God grants Lot's request, sparing the town of Zoar for Lot's sake. God hears the prayers of His fragile servants.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Divine condescension accepting Lot's petition); CCC 2605.
historicalContext: Granting a judicial exemption (*lifting the face*) for a specific town.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer elav Hinneh nasathi phaneykha gam la-davar ha-zeh le-vilti haphkhi eth-ha-ir...*: *nasathi phaneykha* ('I have lifted up your face / granted your request'). *Haphkhi* (overturning/destroying).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew phrase *nasa panim* ('lift up the face') is the technical legal term for granting a royal pardon or approving a petition.

dominicalIntent: 'Make haste, escape there; for I can do nothing until you arrive there.' Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar. ANGELIC IMPOTENCE UNTIL THE RIGHTEOUS ARE SAFE! The Angel says: 'I CAN DO NOTHING until you arrive there!' God delays cosmic judgment until His righteous ones are secured in safety. This prefigures the sealing of the saints before the Great Tribulation (Rev 7:3).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God withholding judgment until the righteous are safe); CCC 1021; Rev 7:3.
historicalContext: Renaming Bela to *Tzo'ar* ('Little One') to commemorate Lot's rescue petition.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Maher himmalet shammah ki lo ukhal la'asoth davar ad-bo'akha shammah al-ken qara shem-ha-ir Tzo'ar*: *lo ukhal* ('I am not able'). *Tzo'ar* (Little One).
historicalTrivia: Revelation 7:3 quotes the principle of Genesis 19:22: 'Do not harm the earth or the sea or the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads'.

dominicalIntent: The sun had risen on the earth when Lot came to Zoar (*Ha-shemesh yatza al-ha-aretz ve-Lot ba Tzo'arah*). As the sun rises over the horizon, Lot reaches Zoar. The sunrise marks the exact moment when divine grace completes salvation and divine wrath descends upon unrepentant sin.
cccReferences: CCC 1021 (The fixed moment of divine judgment at sunrise); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Early morning sunrise (approx. 6:00 AM) over the Moabite mountains.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ha-shemesh yatza al-ha-aretz ve-Lot ba Tzo'arah*: *yatza* (went forth / shone forth).
historicalTrivia: The timestamp *Ha-shemesh yatza* ('The sun had risen') contrasts with the evening arrival of the angels in v. 1, completing the 12-hour night of rescue.

dominicalIntent: Then the Lord rained on Sodom and Gomorrah sulfur and fire from the Lord out of heaven (*Va-YHVH himtir al-Sedom ve-al-Amorah gophrith va-esh me-eth YHVH min-ha-shamayim*). THE CATACLYSMIC DESTRUCTION OF SODOM AND GOMORRAH! Yahweh on earth rains sulfur (*gophrith*) and fire (*esh*) from Yahweh out of heaven! Patristic writers (e.g., St. Justin Martyr, St. Irenaeus) saw in this dual mention of Yahweh ('Yahweh rained... from Yahweh out of heaven') a clear Trinitarian manifestation: God the Son on earth executing judgment from God the Father in heaven! Sodom's destruction is the supreme Old Testament type of Gehenna (Hell) and the final judgment (Jude 1:7; 2 Pet 2:6).
cccReferences: CCC 1867 (Destruction of Sodom as physical manifestation of divine judgment on grave sin); CCC 1033-1035 (Hell and eternal fire prefigured by Sodom); 2 Peter 2:6; Jude 1:7; St. Justin Martyr *Dialogue with Trypho* 56.
historicalContext: Cataclysmic geological explosion: ignition of subterranean pressurized natural gas, sulfur (*gophrith*), and molten bitumen deposits along the Dead Sea fault rift.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va-YHVH himtir al-Sedom ve-al-Amorah gophrith va-esh me-eth YHVH min-ha-shamayim*: *gophrith* (brimstone/sulfur). *Esh* (fire). *Me-eth YHVH min-ha-shamayim* ('from Yahweh out of heaven').
crossReferences: 2 Peter 2:6; Jude 1:7; Luke 17:29; Revelation 19:20; Revelation 20:10; Deuteronomy 29:23; Psalm 11:6.
historicalTrivia: Geological core drilling at the southern Dead Sea rift reveals massive hyper-saline sulfur and petroleum-bitumen deposits ignited by seismic faulting around 1900 BC.

dominicalIntent: And he withdrew those cities, and all the valley, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and what grew on the ground (*vayyahaphoch eth-ha-he-arim ha-el...*). Total overthrow (*haphak*) of the four doomed cities of the plain (Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim). The fertile valley is turned into an uninhabitable salt wasteland.
cccReferences: CCC 1033 (Hell as eternal desolation); CCC 1867; Deut 29:23.
historicalContext: Complete tectonic collapse and incineration of the urban Pentapolis region.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyahaphoch eth-ha-he-arim ha-el ve-eth kol-ha-kikkar ve-eth kol-yoshey ha-he-arim ve-tzeMach ha-adamah*: *haphak* (to overturn/invert/destroy).
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 29:23 describes the permanent result: 'a waste of brimstone and salt, not sown, yielding nothing... like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim'.

dominicalIntent: But Lot's wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt (*vattabit ishto me-acharav vatyehi netziv melach*). LOT'S WIFE LOOKS BACK! Disobeying the explicit angelic command (v. 17), Lot's wife looks back with longing toward Sodom's luxury and lifestyle, and is instantly encrusted into a pillar of salt (*netziv melach*). Jesus commands every Christian: 'REMEMBER LOT'S WIFE!' (Luke 17:32). Looking back to the old life of sin brings spiritual death.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The warning of Lot's wife: spiritual death of looking back to sin); CCC 1428; Luke 17:32; Wis 10:7.
historicalContext: Encrustation by airborne vaporized sodium chloride (salt) and ash along the Dead Sea salt crags (*Jebel Usdum*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattabet ishto me-acharav vatyehi netziv melach*: *vattabet* (gazed intently / looked back with longing). *Netziv melach* (pillar / statue / monument of salt).
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 10:7 commentary: 'A pillar of salt standing as a monument to an unbelieving soul (*apistousēs psychēs mnēmeion*)'.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham went early in the morning to the place where he had stood before the Lord (*el-ha-maqom asher-amad sham eth-pney YHVH*). Abraham rises early and returns to his sanctuary of prayer! Abraham returns to the exact spot where he had interceded for Sodom (Gen 18:22), standing before Yahweh in silent adoration.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's morning prayer of quiet trust after intercession); CCC 2572; CCC 2096.
historicalContext: High ridge east of Hebron (Beni Na'im) overlooking the Dead Sea basin.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyasqem Avraham ba-boqer el-ha-maqom asher-amad sham eth-pney YHVH*: *Vayyasqem* (rose early in the morning). *Amad* (stood).
historicalTrivia: The site Beni Na'im (5 miles east of Hebron) has been venerated since antiquity as 'Maqam An-Nabi Yaqin' ('The Place of the Prophet's Certainty'), where Abraham stood in Genesis 19:27.

dominicalIntent: And he looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and toward all the land of the valley, and looked and behold, the smoke of the land went up like the smoke of a furnace (*qitor ha-kivshan*). Abraham sees the dense column of black smoke rising like a furnace (*kivshan*). The smoke of Sodom's judgment prefigures the smoke of Babylon's destruction in Revelation 18:9 ('when they see the smoke of her burning').
cccReferences: CCC 1033 (The smoke of eternal judgment prefigured); CCC 1867; Rev 18:9; Rev 19:3.
historicalContext: Dense black smoke (*qitor*) from burning bitumen, sulfur, and petroleum deposits rising thousands of feet into the sky.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyashqeph al-pney Sedom ve-Amorah... vayyar ve-hinneh alah qitor ha-aretz ke-qitor ha-kivshan*: *qitor* (thick smoke/steam). *Kivshan* (smelting furnace/kiln).
historicalTrivia: Revelation 19:3 ('The smoke from her goes up forever and ever') directly quotes the imagery of Genesis 19:28.

dominicalIntent: So it was that, when God destroyed the cities of the valley, God remembered Abraham (*Vayyizkor Elohim eth-Avraham*) and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow when he overthrew the cities in which Lot had lived. GOD REMEMBERED ABRAHAM! Why was Lot saved from Sodom's destruction? NOT because of Lot's merit, but because **God remembered ABRAHAM** and his intercessory prayer (Gen 18:23-32)! This reveals the immense power of intercessory prayer: the prayers of the righteous save others from destruction.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God saving Lot because He remembered Abraham's intercessory prayer); CCC 2634 (Power of intercessory prayer for others); CCC 2572; Wis 10:6.
historicalContext: Covenantal remembrance (*zakar*) executing intercessory salvation for kin.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi be-shachath Elohim eth-areyy ha-kikkar vayyizkor Elohim eth-Avraham vay-shalach eth-Lot mi-thoch ha-haphekhah*: *vayyizkor* (and God remembered).
historicalTrivia: Wisdom 10:6 summarizes Genesis 19:29: 'Wisdom rescued a righteous man when the ungodly were perishing; he escaped the fire that descended on the Five Cities'.

dominicalIntent: Now Lot went up out of Zoar and lived in the hills with his two daughters, for he was afraid to remain in Zoar. So he lived in a cave with his two daughters. Lot flees Zoar out of fear, settling in a mountain cave (*ba-m'arah*). Fear drives Lot into isolated isolation, setting up the final tragic episode of his life.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Isolation born of fear); CCC 1854.
historicalContext: Living in natural limestone caves (*m'arah*) in the Moabite mountains above the Dead Sea.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'al Lot mi-Tzo'ar vayyeshev ba-har u-sheny venothav itto ki yare la-sheveth be-Tzo'ar vayyeshev ba-m'arah hu u-sheny venothav*: *m'arah* (cave).
historicalTrivia: The 'Cave of Lot' (Deir 'Ain 'Abata in Jordan) contains a Byzantine monastery built over a natural cave venerated since antiquity as Lot's shelter.

dominicalIntent: And the firstborn said to the younger: 'Our father is old, and there is not a man on earth to come in to us after the manner of all the earth.' Lot's daughters assume the whole world has been destroyed (like the Flood). Living in isolation from faith leads to despair and moral distortion.
cccReferences: CCC 1854 (Moral distortion in isolation from the community of faith); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: False assumption that the Dead Sea cataclysm was global, leaving no surviving men for marriage.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatyo'mer ha-bekhirah el-ha-tze'irah avinu zaqen ve-ish ein ba-aretz lavo aleynu ki-derekh kol-ha-aretz*.
historicalTrivia: The daughters' panic reflects the apocalyptic trauma of witnessing the cataclysmic destruction of their entire urban world.

dominicalIntent: 'Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve offspring through our father.' Desperate human maneuvering through intoxication and incest (*incestus*). They use wine to bypass moral conscience.
cccReferences: CCC 2290 (Abuse of alcohol obscuring moral reason); CCC 2388 (Incest as a grave moral evil); CCC 1854.
historicalContext: Pagan Moabite/Ammonite ancestral origin traditions recorded with stark biblical objectivity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lechah nashqeh eth-avinu yayin ve-nishkevah immo u-nechayyeh me-avinu zera*: *nashqeh* (let us give drink). *Zera* (seed/lineage).
historicalTrivia: Scripture records this incestuous plot with clinical objectivity, neither excusing the act nor hiding the dark origin of Israel's future enemies.

dominicalIntent: So they made their father drink wine that night. And the firstborn went in and lay with her father; he did not know when she lay down or when she arose. Intoxication strips Lot of moral awareness. Excess wine leads to moral blindness and shame.
cccReferences: CCC 2290 (Dangers of drunkenness blurring moral responsibility); CCC 2388.
historicalContext: Heavy intoxication disabling cognitive awareness of incestuous assault.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattashqeyna eth-avihen yayin ba-laylah ha-hu vatavah ha-bekhirah vattishkav eth-aviha ve-lo-yada be-shikhvah u-ve-qumah*.
historicalTrivia: The note *he did not know when she lay down or when she arose* preserves Lot's lack of conscious consent while highlighting his culpable drunkenness.

dominicalIntent: The next day, the firstborn said to the younger: 'Behold, I lay last night with my father; let us make him drink wine tonight also; then you go in and lie with him, that we may preserve offspring through our father.' The younger daughter repeats the incestuous scheme.
cccReferences: CCC 1865 (Repetition of sin creating habit of sin); CCC 2388.
historicalContext: Systematic repetition of the incestuous plan.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi mi-machorath vatyo'mer ha-bekhirah el-ha-tze'irah hen-shakhavti emesh eth-avi...*.
historicalTrivia: The symmetrical repetition between the firstborn and younger daughters highlights how sin replicates within a family isolated from divine grace.

dominicalIntent: So they made their father drink wine that night also. And the younger arose and lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down or when she arose. Execution of the second incestuous act under cover of intoxication.
historicalContext: Conception of the second ancestral line in the mountain cave.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattashqeyna gam ba-laylah ha-hu eth-avihen yayin vattaqam ha-tze'irah vattishkav immo ve-lo-yada be-shikhvah u-ve-qumah*.
historicalTrivia: Both daughters conceive from their father, yielding the ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites.

dominicalIntent: Thus both the daughters of Lot became pregnant by their father (*Vathareyna shtey venoth-Lot me-avihen*). The origin of Moab and Ammon through incest. Yet divine grace works even through dark human lineages: **Ruth the Moabite** converts to the God of Israel and enters the direct genealogy of Jesus Christ (Matt 1:5)!
cccReferences: CCC 401 (Divine grace transcending dark human origins); CCC 488 (Ruth the Moabite in the genealogy of Christ); Matt 1:5; Ruth 4:13-17.
historicalContext: Ethno-genealogical origin account of Moab and Ammon, Israel's eastern transjordanian neighbors.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vathareyna shtey venoth-Lot me-avihen*: *me-avihen* ('from their father').
historicalTrivia: Ruth the Moabite (*Ruth 4:17*) is the great-grandmother of King David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ (Matt 1:5), demonstrating that grace redeems Moab's dark origins.

dominicalIntent: The firstborn bore a son and called his name Moab (*Mo'av*). He is the father of the Moabites to this day. **Moab** (*Mo-av* = 'From Father'). From Moab's line comes Ruth the Moabite, proving that no person is trapped by ancestral sin when they turn to God.
cccReferences: CCC 401 (Redemption reaching all nations); CCC 488; Ruth 4:17.
historicalContext: Moab occupied the plateau east of the Dead Sea (modern central Jordan).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatteled ha-bekhirah ben vattiqra shemo Mo'av hu avi-Mo'av ad-ha-yom*: *Mo'av* (etymological pun: *me-av* = 'from father').
historicalTrivia: The Mesha Stele (Moabite Stone, c. 840 BC) contains the longest Moabite inscription discovered, written in a West Semitic dialect nearly identical to Biblical Hebrew.

dominicalIntent: The younger also bore a son and called his name Ben-ammi (*Ben-Ammi*). He is the father of the Ammonites to this day. **Ben-ammi** (*Ben-Ammi* = 'Son of My People'). Father of the Ammonites (occupying modern Amman, Jordan). The story of Lot closes, contrasting his tragic cave isolation with Abraham's radiant life of faith.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The contrast between Lot's end and Abraham's ongoing journey of faith); CCC 145.
historicalContext: Ammon occupied the Transjordanian plateau north of Moab, centered around Rabbath-Ammon (modern Amman, Jordan).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-ha-tze'irah gam-hi yaladh ben vattiqra shemo Ben-Ammi hu avi veney-Ammon ad-ha-yom*: *Ben-Ammi* ('Son of my kin / my people').
historicalTrivia: Amman, the capital city of modern Jordan, derives its name directly from *Ben-Ammon* ('Sons of Ammon') of Genesis 19:38.
