dominicalIntent: From there Abraham journeyed toward the territory of the Negeb and lived between Kadesh and Shur; and he sojourned in Gerar (*vayyagar be-Gherar*). Abraham moves south to Gerar in Philistine territory. Continuing his pilgrimage of faith, Abraham sojourns as a resident alien (*ger*), prefiguring the Christian as a stranger and exile in this passing world (1 Pet 2:11).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's continuous sojourn in faith); 1 Pet 2:11; CCC 145.
historicalContext: Gerar (Tell Haror / Tell el-Fari'ah) in the western Negev foothills near Gaza, a fertile agricultural valley ruled by early Aegean/Philistine chieftains.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyissa misham Avraham artzah ha-negev vayyeshev beyn-Qadesh u-veyn Shur vayyagar be-Gherar*: *vayyagar* (sojourned as alien, root *gur* -> *ger*).
historicalTrivia: Archaeological excavations at Tell Haror (*Gerar*) revealed Middle Bronze Age fortifications, grain storage silos, and Aegean pottery imports matching early Philistine presence.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, 'She is my sister.' And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah (*vayyishlach Avimelech melech Gherar vayyiqach eth-Sarah*). Recurrence of fear! Abraham repeats the half-truth used in Egypt (Gen 12:13). This shows that even great saints experience moments of weakness when facing old temptations, demonstrating our constant need for divine grace.
cccReferences: CCC 1854 (Human frailty and repeated temptation); CCC 2477 (Deceptive half-truths); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Abimelech (*Avi-melech* = 'My Father is King') was a royal title for Philistine dynasts of Gerar.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avraham el-Sarah ishto achothi hi vayyishlach Avimelech melech Gherar vayyiqach eth-Sarah*: *Avi-melech* (My father is King).
historicalTrivia: Like 'Pharaoh' in Egypt, *Abimelech* was a royal title used by Philistine kings of Gerar across generations (e.g., Gen 20; Gen 26; Judg 9).

dominicalIntent: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him: 'Behold, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is a man's wife' (*ki-hi be'ulath ba'al*). GOD INTERVENES TO PROTECT SARAH AND THE MESSIANIC LINE! God warns Abimelech in a dream: 'You are a dead man!' (*Hinnekh meth*). God protects the sanctity of marriage and prevents any doubt regarding Isaac's paternity.
cccReferences: CCC 2380 (Adultery as grave sin against marital integrity); CCC 2571 (Divine intervention protecting Sarah); CCC 1607.
historicalContext: Night dream theophany (*chalom ha-laylah*) to a pagan king enforcing international moral law against adultery.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo Elohim el-Avimelech bi-chlom ha-laylah vayyo'mer lo Hinnekh meth al-ha-ishah asher laqachta ve-hi be'ulath ba'al*: *be'ulath ba'al* ('owned/married to a husband').
historicalTrivia: Dream revelations to pagan kings (*bi-chlom ha-laylah*) recur in Scripture for Pharaoh (Gen 41), Nebuchadnezzar (Dan 2), and Pilate's wife (Matt 27:19).

dominicalIntent: Now Abimelech had not approached her. So he said: 'Lord, will you kill an innocent people?' (*Adonai ha-goy gam-tzaddik taharog*). Abimelech's restraint: he had NOT touched Sarah! Abimelech pleads his moral innocence, appealing to divine justice ('Will you kill an innocent nation?'), echoing Abraham's prayer in Genesis 18:23.
cccReferences: CCC 1854 (Objective moral innocence in ignorance); CCC 1793 (Invincible ignorance mitigating guilt); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Pagan king appealing to universal moral law (*natural law*) before the Supreme Judge.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Avimelech lo qarav eleyha vayyo'mar Adonai ha-goy gam-tzaddik taharog*: *lo qarav* (had not approached / touched her carnally).
historicalTrivia: Abimelech's question *ha-goy gam-tzaddik taharog* ('Will you slay an innocent nation?') uses the exact same word *tzaddik* used by Abraham in Genesis 18:23.

dominicalIntent: 'Did he not himself say to me, "She is my sister"? And she herself said, "He is my brother." In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this' (*be-thom-levavi u-ve-niqyon kappay asithi zoth*). Abimelech asserts his integrity of heart (*thom-levav*) and innocence of hands (*niqyon kappay*). God recognizes subjective sincerity while upholding objective truth.
cccReferences: CCC 1793 (Integrity of heart in involuntary ignorance); CCC 1754; Psalm 24:4.
historicalContext: Formal judicial defense asserting clean hands and pure motive.
translationNuances: Hebrew *be-thom-levavi u-ve-niqyon kappay asithi zoth*: *thom* (integrity/completeness). *Niqyon* (cleanness/purity).
historicalTrivia: The phrase *niqyon kappay* ('innocence/cleanness of hands') is the exact ritual formula used in Psalm 24:4 for entering God's holy sanctuary.

dominicalIntent: Then God said to him in the dream: 'Yes, I know that you have done this in the integrity of your heart, and it was I who kept you from sinning against me (*va-echshokh anochi othakha me-chato-li*). Therefore I did not let you touch her.' GOD PREVENTS SIN! God confirms Abimelech's subjective sincerity, revealing that divine grace secretly restrained him from committing adultery! God's preventing grace (*gratia praeveniens*) preserves souls from grave sin.
cccReferences: CCC 2000 (Preventing grace keeping souls from falling into sin); CCC 1793; CCC 2571; Ps 19:13.
historicalContext: Divine providence invisibly governing human circumstances to preserve moral purity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer elav ha-Elohim ba-chalom gam anochi yadati ki be-thom-levavkha asitha zoth va-echshokh anochi othakha me-chato-li*: *va-echshokh* (and I withheld/restrained you).
historicalTrivia: 1 Samuel 25:26 echoes Genesis 20:6 when Abigail stops David from bloodshed: 'the Lord has restrained you (*chasak*) from bloodguilt'.

dominicalIntent: 'Now then, restore the man's wife, for he is a prophet (*ki-navi hu*), and he will pray for you, and you shall live. But if you do not restore her, know that you shall surely die, you and all who are yours.' ABRAHAM IS CALLED A PROPHET FOR THE FIRST TIME! This is the FIRST APPEARANCE OF THE WORD 'PROPHET' (*Navi*) IN THE BIBLE! God reveals that Abraham is a prophet whose intercessory prayer brings healing and life. The prophet is primarily an intercessor before God.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham called a 'prophet' whose intercessory prayer heals and saves); CCC 2581 (The prophetic mission of intercession); CCC 2634; Jer 15:1.
historicalContext: A prophet (*navi*) in ancient Semitic theology was a divine spokesman and authoritative intercessor admitted into the divine council.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah hashev esheth-ha-ish ki-navi hu ve-yithpallel ba'adkha ve-chyeh...*: *navi* (prophet/spokesman, root *nava* = to bubble forth / speak). *Yithpallel* (shall intercede/pray, root *palal*).
historicalTrivia: Psalm 105:15 directly quotes Genesis 20:7: 'Touch not my anointed ones, do my prophets (*nevi'ai*) no harm!'.

dominicalIntent: So Abimelech rose early in the morning and called all his servants and told them all these things. And the men were very much afraid (*vayyir'u ha-anashim me'od*). Abimelech acts with prompt obedience at dawn! Holy fear of God (*yir'ath Elohim*) grips the pagan royal court.
cccReferences: CCC 1831 (Gift of Holy Fear of the Lord); CCC 2571; Ps 111:10.
historicalContext: Early morning royal council assembly of Philistine courtiers and officers.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyasqem Avimelech ba-boqer vayyiqra le-khol-avadav vaydabber eth-kol-ha-devarim ha-elleh be-ozneyhem vayyir'u ha-anashim me'od*: *Vayyasqem* (rose early).
historicalTrivia: The prompt morning assembly *Vayyasqem ba-boqer* demonstrates that Abimelech treated the divine dream with immediate, total urgency.

dominicalIntent: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him: 'What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and my kingdom a great sin?' (*chata'ah gedolah*). Abimelech rebukes Abraham for exposing his kingdom to 'a great sin' (*chata'ah gedolah* = adultery). Adultery is recognized even by pagan natural law as a grave moral evil destroying society.
cccReferences: CCC 2380 (Adultery as a grave sin against society and God); CCC 1756; CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Royal rebuke of a foreign prophet for exposing a nation to divine wrath.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra Avimelech le-Avraham vayyo'mer lo meh-asitha lanu u-mah-chatathi lakh ki-hevetha alai ve-al-mamlakhti chata'ah gedolah*: *chata'ah gedolah* ('great sin/guilt').
historicalTrivia: The phrase *chata'ah gedolah* ('great sin') is used in Exodus 32:21 for the Golden Calf idolatry, showing that adultery carried equal gravity.

dominicalIntent: And Abimelech said to Abraham: 'What did you see, that you did this thing?' Abimelech demands to know Abraham's underlying motive, forcing Abraham to confront his hidden fear and lack of trust in God's protection.
cccReferences: CCC 1752 (Importance of moral intention and motive in human actions); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Judicial inquiry into the psychological motive behind deceptive behavior in an international treaty context.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avimelech el-Avraham mah ra'itha ki asitha eth-ha-davar ha-zeh*: *mah ra'itha* ('what did you see / observe?').
historicalTrivia: Abimelech's question forces Abraham to examine his own inner fear and lack of trust in God's protection before the pagan king.

dominicalIntent: Abraham said: 'I did it because I thought, "There is no fear of God at all in this place (*raq ein-yir'ath Elohim ba-maqom ha-zeh*), and they will kill me because of my wife."' Abraham admits his faulty assumption: he assumed pagans had no fear of God! Yet Abimelech proved to have more fear of God than Abraham expected. We must never judge others' hearts or underestimate God's grace working outside our visible boundaries.
cccReferences: CCC 1831 (Fear of God present even among Gentiles); CCC 2571 (Correction of Abraham's prejudice); Acts 10:34-35.
historicalContext: Abraham's self-justification revealing his underlying survival anxiety in foreign lands.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avraham ki amarthi raq ein-yir'ath Elohim ba-maqom ha-zeh ve-haraguni al-devar ishti*: *yir'ath Elohim* ('fear of God').
historicalTrivia: St. Peter in Acts 10:34-35 echoes the lesson of Genesis 20:11: 'Truly I perceive that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him is acceptable to him'.

dominicalIntent: Besides, she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father though not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife. Abraham explains the technical half-truth: Sarah was his paternal half-sister. A half-truth intended to deceive remains a violation of truthfulness.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Half-truths used to deceive violate the Eighth Commandment); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Endogamous marriage with a paternal half-sister (*daughter of my father*) was practiced in early patriarchal society before the Mosaic prohibitions of Leviticus 18:9.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gham-omnah achothi vath-avi hi ach lo vath-immi vatyehi-li le-ishah*.
historicalTrivia: Leviticus 18:9 later explicitly prohibited marriage with a half-sister, showing that patriarchal customs were refined by Mosaic Law.

dominicalIntent: 'And when God caused me to wander from my father's house, I said to her, "This is the kindness you must do me: at every place to which we come, say of me, He is my brother."' Abraham reveals that this survival pact was established years ago when leaving Ur. Human survival pacts based on deception fail, whereas trust in divine providence never fails.
cccReferences: CCC 2570 (Flaws in human survival strategies vs reliance on providence); CCC 2477.
historicalContext: Pre-arranged family covenant pact (*chesed*) between husband and wife during international travel.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ka-asher hith'u othi Elohim mi-beyth avi... Zeh chasdekh asher ta'asi immadi...*: *hith'u* (caused to wander/pilgrim, Hiphil plural of *ta'ah*). *Chesed* (loyalty/kindness).
historicalTrivia: The verb *hith'u* ('caused to wander') uses a plural verb with *Elohim*, a rare grammatical construction emphasizing the vast international wandering imposed by God.

dominicalIntent: Then Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored Sarah his wife to him. Abimelech acts with noble magnanimity: he returns Sarah untouched and bestows lavish gifts upon Abraham. God turns human failure into covenantal enrichment.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Protection and enrichment of Abraham by divine providence); CCC 1939; Gen 12:16.
historicalContext: Royal restitution gifts sealing diplomatic reconciliation and honoring Abraham's prophetic standing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqach Avimelech tzon u-vaqar va-avadim u-shephachoth vayyitten le-Avraham vayyashev lo eth Sarah ishto*.
historicalTrivia: Proverbs 16:7 ('When a man's ways please the Lord, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him') is illustrated by Abimelech's generosity.

dominicalIntent: And Abimelech said: 'Behold, my land is before you; dwell where it pleases you' (*ba-tov be-eyneykha shev*). Abimelech grants Abraham full residency rights in Gerar! Contrast with Pharaoh who expelled Abram (Gen 12:19): Abimelech welcomes Abraham to dwell anywhere in his land.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Open residency granted to Abraham); CCC 1939 (Hospitality to strangers).
historicalContext: Royal land grant bestowing unrestricted dwelling rights upon a prophetic patriarch.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avimelech hinneh artzi le-phaneykha ba-tov be-eyneykha shev*: *ba-tov be-eyneykha* ('wherever it is good in your eyes').
historicalTrivia: Abimelech's invitation *hinneh artzi le-phaneykha* ('behold, my land is before you') mirrors Abram's generous invitation to Lot in Gen 13:9.

dominicalIntent: To Sarah he said: 'Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is a sign of your innocence in the eyes of all who are with you, and before everyone you are vindicated' (*ve-eth kol ve-nikhachath*). Abimelech gives 1,000 shekels of silver as a public vindication of Sarah's purity! Sarah's honor is publicly cleared before all nations.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Public vindication of reputation and honor); CCC 2521 (Purity vindicated); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: 1,000 shekels of silver (approx. 25 lbs / 11.5 kg of silver) was a massive royal sum, serving as a legal 'covering of the eyes' (*kesuth eynayim*) to wipe away any social stigma.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-le-Sarah amar hinneh nathatti eleph kesepu le-achikh hinneh hu-lakha kesuth eynayim le-khol asher ittakh ve-eth kol ve-nikhachath*: *kesuth eynayim* ('a covering of the eyes' = public vindication). *Nikhachath* (righted/vindicated).
historicalTrivia: 1,000 shekels of silver was equivalent to 50 times the standard slave price in the Middle Bronze Age (Gen 37:28), demonstrating immense Pharaonic-level restitution.

dominicalIntent: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, and also healed his wife and his female slaves, so that they bore children (*Vayyithpallel Avraham el-ha-Elohim vayyirpa Elohim eth-Avimelech*). ABRAHAM'S INTERCESSORY PRAYER HEALS ABIMELECH'S HOUSEHOLD! Abraham fulfills his prophetic office (v. 7) by praying for Abimelech. God hears Abraham's prayer and heals their barrenness. The intercession of the righteous brings healing and fertility to others.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's intercessory prayer bringing divine healing); CCC 2634 (Power of intercession for others); CCC 1505 (Divine healing through prayer); Jas 5:16.
historicalContext: Prophetic intercessory prayer (*yithpallel*) lifting a divine curse of temporary barrenness from a royal household.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyithpallel Avraham el-ha-Elohim vayyirpa Elohim eth-Avimelech ve-eth-ishto ve-amchothav vayyeledu*: *vayyirpa* (and he healed, root *rapa* -> *Yahweh-Rapha*).
historicalTrivia: James 5:16 ('The prayer of a righteous person has great power as it is working') is directly illustrated by Abraham healing Abimelech's household in Genesis 20:17.

dominicalIntent: For the Lord had closed fast all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham's wife (*ki-atzor atzar YHVH be-ad kol-rechem le-veyth Avimelech al-devar Sarah esheth Avraham*). God had closed every womb in Abimelech's house to guard Sarah's purity. Now, with Abimelech's household healed of barrenness, the stage is set for Genesis 21, where Sarah herself conceives and gives birth to Isaac!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God controlling fertility to preserve the messianic line); CCC 489; CCC 2374.
historicalContext: Temporary divine closure of wombs (*atzor atzar*) as a supernatural sign protecting Sarah.
translationNuances: Hebrew *ki-atzor atzar YHVH be-ad kol-rechem le-veyth Avimelech al-devar Sarah esheth Avraham*: *atzor atzar* (infinitive absolute: 'closing He had closed fast'). *Rechem* (womb).
historicalTrivia: The healing of Abimelech's household wombs in Gen 20:17-18 immediately precedes Sarah's womb opening in Gen 21:1, showing that Abraham's prayer for others unlocked his own blessing.

dominicalIntent: The Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did to Sarah as he had promised (*Va-YHVH paqad eth-Sarah ka-asher amar*). DIVINE FIDELITY! God's promises never fail. The verb *paqad* ('visited') marks divine intervention fulfilling covenant promises. God's visitation of Sarah prefigures the visitation of the Holy Spirit to the Virgin Mary at the Annunciation (Luke 1:68).
cccReferences: CCC 489 (The divine visitation of Sarah preparing for the Virgin Birth); CCC 212 (Infallibility of divine promises); CCC 706; Luke 1:68.
historicalContext: Covenant fulfillment after 25 years of waiting in Canaan (Abram 75 at call, 100 at Isaac's birth).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va-YHVH paqad eth-Sarah ka-asher amar vayya'as YHVH le-Sarah ka-asher dibber*: *paqad* (visited/attended to/remembered).
crossReferences: Luke 1:68; Luke 7:16; Genesis 17:19; Genesis 18:10; Galatians 4:23; Hebrews 11:11.
historicalTrivia: The verb *paqad* (visited) is translated in the LXX as *epe-skepsato*, the exact word used by Zechariah in Luke 1:68 ('Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has visited and redeemed his people').

dominicalIntent: And Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age at the time of which God had spoken to him (*la-mo'ed asher-dibber oto Elohim*). FULFILLMENT AT THE APPOINTED TIME! Isaac is born at the exact *mo'ed* ('appointed sacred time') promised by God in Gen 17:21 and 18:14. God's grace acts with mathematical and chronological perfection.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (Birth of Isaac as child of promise); CCC 60; Gal 4:23; Rom 9:7-9.
historicalContext: Miraculous birth to a 100-year-old father and 90-year-old mother.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatthar vatteleth Sarah le-Avraham ben li-vqurav la-mo'ed asher-dibber oto Elohim*: *la-mo'ed* ('at the appointed sacred time/feast').
historicalTrivia: Galatians 4:23 stresses the contrast: 'The son of the free woman was born through promise (*di epaggelias*)'.

dominicalIntent: Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore him, Isaac (*Yitzchaq*). Abraham names his son **Isaac** (*Yitzchaq* = 'Laughter'), obeying God's previous command (Gen 17:19). Isaac's name permanently commemorates the joyful divine laughter of faith.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (Isaac named by God); CCC 2571; Gal 4:28.
historicalContext: Formal patriarchal naming ceremony on the day of birth.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra Avraham eth-shem-bno ha-nollad-lo asher-yaldah-lo Sarah Yitzchaq*: *Yitzchaq* ('He laughs / Laughter').
historicalTrivia: Naming Isaac (*Yitzchaq*) before his birth links him with John the Baptist and Jesus as the only three Old Testament children named by God prior to birth.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him (*ka-asher tzivvah oto Elohim*). OBEDIENCE ON THE EIGHTH DAY! Abraham circumcises Isaac on the 8th day, fulfilling Genesis 17:12. This is the first recorded 8th-day circumcision in Scripture, prefiguring Jesus' 8th-day circumcision (Luke 2:21) and Christian Infant Baptism.
cccReferences: CCC 527 (Circumcision of Isaac on the 8th day prefiguring Christ's circumcision and Infant Baptism); CCC 1219; Luke 2:21; Acts 7:8.
historicalContext: Infant circumcision on the 8th day establishing formal entry into the Abrahamic Covenant.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyamol Avraham eth-Yitzchaq bno ben-shemonath yamim ka-asher tzivvah oto Elohim*.
historicalTrivia: Acts 7:8 records St. Stephen's summary: 'And he gave him the covenant of circumcision. And so Abraham became the father of Isaac, and circumcised him on the eighth day'.

dominicalIntent: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him (*ben-me'ath shanah*). At 100 years old, Abraham receives the promise. 25 years of patient waiting in faith are rewarded. God's delays are not denials, but preparations for greater glory.
cccReferences: CCC 1817 (Virtue of patient hope rewarded); CCC 145-147; Rom 4:19-21.
historicalContext: Abraham 100 years old; Sarah 90 years old; Ishmael 14 years old.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Avraham ben-me'ath shanah be-hikkavled lo eth Yitzchaq bno*.
historicalTrivia: 25 years elapsed between Abraham's call at 75 (Gen 12:4) and Isaac's birth at 100 (Gen 21:5).

dominicalIntent: And Sarah said: 'God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me' (*Tzchoq asah li Elohim kol ha-shome'a yitzchaq-li*). JOYFUL SANCTIFIED LAUGHTER! Sarah's earlier inner laughter of doubt (Gen 18:12) is converted by divine grace into the triumphant laughter of holy joy! Sarah's joy prefigures the joy of the Virgin Mary in the *Magnificat* ('My spirit rejoices in God my Savior', Luke 1:47).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Sarah's holy joy in divine fulfillment); CCC 489; Luke 1:47.
historicalContext: Public poetic exclamation celebrating miraculous birth.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatyo'mer Sarah tzchoq asah li Elohim kol ha-shome'a yitzchaq-li*: *tzchoq* (laughter/joy). *Yitzchaq-li* ('will laugh/rejoice with me').
historicalTrivia: Psalm 126:2 ('Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with shouts of joy') directly echoes Sarah's words in Genesis 21:6.

dominicalIntent: And she said: 'Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.' Sarah marveled at God's impossible grace. Nursing a son at 90 years old is a physical sign of supernatural divine rejuvenation.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (Miraculous nursing by barren Sarah); CCC 2374.
historicalContext: Maternal nursing (*heniqah*) in ANE culture typically lasted 2 to 3 years.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatyo'mer mi millel le-Avraham heniqah vanim Sarah ki-yaladti ven li-vqurav*.
historicalTrivia: The rhetorical question *Mi millel le-Avraham* ('Who would have declared to Abraham?') emphasizes that no human wisdom could foresee God's miraculous plan.

dominicalIntent: And the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned (*vayya'as Avraham mishteh gadol be-yom higgamel eth-Yitzchaq*). Isaac's weaning feast (approx. age 3). The weaning feast (*mishteh gadol*) prefigures the Eucharistic banquet celebrating growth in spiritual childhood.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Family celebration of growth in faith); CCC 1334 (Sacramental banquets).
historicalContext: In Levantine culture, weaning (*gamel*) at age 2 or 3 was a major infant survival milestone celebrated with a clan covenant feast.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyigdal ha-yeled vayyiggamel vayya'as Avraham mishteh gadol be-yom higgamel eth-Yitzchaq*: *higgamel* (was weaned, root *gamal*).
historicalTrivia: Psalm 131:2 uses the weaned child metaphor: 'I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child (*gamul*) with its mother'.

dominicalIntent: But Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing (*metzacheq*). Ishmael (now approx. 17 years old) mocks or persecutes young Isaac (age 3). St. Paul explicitly cites this verse in Galatians 4:29: 'As at that time he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so it is now!' The child of the flesh persecutes the child of the Spirit.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Ishmael mocking Isaac as persecution of the spirit by the flesh); Gal 4:29; CCC 401.
historicalContext: Teenage Ishmael mocking or asserting rival inheritance claims against the young legitimate heir Isaac during the weaning feast.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatthar Sarah eth-ben-Hagar ha-Mitzrith asher-yaldah le-Avraham metzacheq*: *metzacheq* (Piel participle: 'mocking / making sport / playing aggressively'). LXX *paizonta*.
historicalTrivia: Galatians 4:29 provides the inspired apostolic interpretation of *metzacheq*: 'he who was born according to the flesh PERSECUTED (*ediōken*) him born according to the Spirit'.

dominicalIntent: She said to Abraham: 'Cast out this slave woman with her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac' (*Gharesh ha-amoh ha-zoth ve-eth-benah ki lo yiyrash ben-ha-amoh ha-zoth im-beni im-Yitzchaq*). Sarah demands the expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael. St. Paul quotes Sarah's exact words in Galatians 4:30 ('Cast out the slave woman and her son!'), revealing that the Law of bondage has no inheritance alongside the Gospel of freedom!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Sarah's demand cited by St. Paul as the decree of Christian freedom); Gal 4:30; CCC 1964.
historicalContext: Legal expulsion of a concubine and her son under ANE inheritance laws to ensure undivided title for the primary heir.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatyo'mer le-Avraham Gharesh ha-amoh ha-zoth ve-eth-benah...*: *Gharesh* (Piel imperative: 'Drive out! / Cast out! / Expel!'). *Amoh* (handmaid/slave woman).
historicalTrivia: Galatians 4:30 quotes Genesis 21:10 verbatim: 'Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman'.

dominicalIntent: And the thing was very displeasing to Abraham on account of his son (*Vayyera ha-davar me'od be-eyney Avraham al odoth bno*). Abraham is deeply grieved because he loves Ishmael as his son. Paternal affection causes Abraham intense interior pain over family division.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's grief for Ishmael); CCC 2221.
historicalContext: Patriarchal grief at severing ties with his firstborn son.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyera ha-davar me'od be-eyney Avraham al odoth bno*: *Vayyera* (was evil / displeasing / painful).
historicalTrivia: Abraham's grief for Ishmael mirrors David's grief for Absalom (2 Sam 18:33), highlighting the agony of paternal love.

dominicalIntent: But God said to Abraham: 'Be not displeased because of the boy and because of your slave woman. Whatever Sarah says to you, do as she tells you, for through Isaac shall your offspring be named' (*ki ve-YITZCHAQ yikkare lekha zera*). GOD CONFIRMS SARAH'S DEMAND! God tells Abraham: 'Listen to Sarah, for through ISAAC shall your seed be named!' St. Paul (Rom 9:7; Heb 11:18) cites this exact verse to prove that divine election depends not on natural flesh descent, but on God's sovereign call.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (The Messianic election through Isaac); Rom 9:7; Heb 11:18; Gal 4:28; CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Divine legal ruling settling the messianic line exclusively upon Isaac.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Elohim el-Avraham al-yera be-eyneykha... kol asher tho'mar eleykha Sarah shema be-qolah ki ve-Yitzchaq yikkare lekha zera*: *shema be-qolah* ('listen to / obey her voice').
historicalTrivia: Romans 9:7 quotes Genesis 21:12: 'Not all are children of Abraham because they are his offspring, but "Through Isaac shall your offspring be named".'

dominicalIntent: And I will make a nation of the son of the slave woman also, because he is your offspring (*ki zar'akha hu*). God comforts Abraham by promising to bless Ishmael because he is Abraham's seed. God's providential care extends mercy even outside the central covenant line.
cccReferences: CCC 58 (God's providential care for Ishmael's nation); CCC 841; CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Providential national blessing promised to Ishmael's descendants.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-gam eth-ben-ha-amoh le-goy asimenno ki zar'akha hu*: *asimenno* (I will set/make him).
historicalTrivia: The Catholic Church's document *Nostra Aetate* (NA 3) references God's blessing on Ishmael's lineage in Genesis 21:13.

dominicalIntent: So Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water (*lechem ve-chemath mayim*) and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, along with the child, and sent her away. And she departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. Abraham obeys God immediately at dawn. Hagar and teenage Ishmael depart into the desert of Beersheba with bread and a water skin.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's immediate morning obedience); CCC 145.
historicalContext: Provisions for desert travel: flat bread (*lechem*) and a tanned leather water skin (*chemath mayim*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyasqem Avraham ba-boqer vayyiqach-lechem ve-chemath mayim vayyitten el-Hagar... vay-shallecheha vattellech vatthetha be-midbar Be'er Sheva*: *vatthetha* (wandered/strayed, root *ta'ah*).
historicalTrivia: Hagar wandering in the wilderness of Beersheba (*midbar Be'er Sheva*) prefigures Israel's later 40-year wandering in the Negev and Sinai deserts.

dominicalIntent: When the water in the skin was gone, she cast the child under one of the bushes (*vattashlech eth-ha-yeled thachath achad ha-sichim*). Provisions run out in the desert heat. Despair grips Hagar as she places her exhausted son under a desert shrub (*sichim*). Human strength fails, setting the stage for divine intervention.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Hagar's extreme plight in the desert); CCC 305.
historicalContext: Desert broom bushes (*Retama raetam* / *sichim*) provided the only shade against fatal sunstroke in the Negev.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyikhlu ha-mayim min-ha-chemath vattashlech eth-ha-yeled thachath achad ha-sichim*: *sichim* (desert shrubs/bushes).
historicalTrivia: Elijah under the broom tree in 1 Kings 19:4 (*rothem*) directly echoes Hagar under the desert bush in Genesis 21:15.

dominicalIntent: Then she went and sat down opposite him a good way off, about the distance of a bowshot, for she said: 'Let me not look on the death of the child.' And as she sat opposite him, she lifted up her voice and wept (*vattissa eth-qolah vatnevkh*). Hagar cannot bear to watch her son die. Her weeping cry (*vatnevkh*) touches the Heart of God. God never ignores the tears of a grieving mother.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God hearing Hagar's maternal weeping); CCC 2569; Ps 56:8.
historicalContext: Maternal grief posture: sitting a bowshot away (*kimthachavey qeshet*) to avoid witnessing the final death agonies.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattellech vatteshev lah mi-neged harcheq kimthachavey qeshet... vattissa eth-qolah vatnevkh*: *kimthachavey qeshet* (about the draw of a bow / bowshot).
historicalTrivia: Psalm 56:8 ('You have kept count of my tossings; put my tears in your bottle') mirrors God's attentiveness to Hagar's weeping.

dominicalIntent: And God heard the voice of the boy (*Vayyishma Elohim eth-qol ha-na'ar*), and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her: 'What troubles you, Hagar? Fear not, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.' GOD HEARS THE CRY OF THE CHILD! God fulfills Ishmael's name ('God Hears' / *Yishma-El*): *Vayyishma Elohim*! The Angel of God speaks from heaven, comforting Hagar and promising life.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God fulfilling the name Ishmael by hearing the boy's voice); CCC 332; CCC 707; Exod 3:7.
historicalContext: Angelic voice from heaven (*min-ha-shamayim*) delivering divine comfort.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishma Elohim eth-qol ha-na'ar vayyiqra mal'akh Elohim el-Hagar min-ha-shamayim... Mah-lakh Hagar al-thir'i ki-shama Elohim eth-qol ha-na'ar*: *Vayyishma Elohim* (echoing *Yishma-El*).
historicalTrivia: The shift from *Mal'akh YHVH* in Gen 16 to *Mal'akh Elohim* in Gen 21 reflects the universal creation relationship outside the covenant.

dominicalIntent: 'Arise, lift up the boy, and hold him fast with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation.' The Angel commands Hagar to lift up the boy and hold him fast. God reaffirms the promise of a great nation, renewing hope in the midst of despair.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Angel restoring hope to Hagar); CCC 305.
historicalContext: Physical resuscitation and encouragement of a dying child.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Qumi se'i eth-ha-na'ar ve-hachaziqi eth-yadekh bo ki-le-goy gadol asimenno*: *hachaziqi* (hold fast / grasp tightly).
historicalTrivia: The command *hachaziqi* ('hold him fast') prefigures Elijah and Elisha lifting dead children to restore them to life (1 Kings 17; 2 Kings 4).

dominicalIntent: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water (*Vayyiphqach Elohim eth-eyneyha vatther be'er mayim*). And she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink. EYES OPENED TO SEE LIVING WATER! The well was already there, but Hagar could not see it until God opened her eyes (*Vayyiphqach Elohim eth-eyneyha*). God opens our eyes to see the well of Living Water—the Holy Spirit and Holy Eucharist—present right beside us in our wilderness!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God opening eyes to see the well of salvation); CCC 698 (Living water of the Holy Spirit); CCC 1335; Luke 24:31.
historicalContext: Hidden desert spring (*be'er mayim*) unveiled by divine illumination.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiphqach Elohim eth-eyneyha vatther be'er mayim vattellech vattemalle eth-ha-chemath mayim vatashq eth-ha-na'ar*: *Vayyiphqach* (opened, same verb used in Luke 24:31).
historicalTrivia: Luke 24:31 ('And their eyes were opened (*diēnoichthēsan*) and they recognized him') uses the exact Septuagint verb of Genesis 21:19 (*anēōxen* / opened eyes).

dominicalIntent: And God was with the boy (*Vayehi Elohim eth-ha-na'ar*), and he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became an archer (*roveh qasshat*). God was with Ishmael! Even outside the messianic covenant line, God's providential presence (*Elohim eth-ha-na'ar*) protects and sustains Ishmael as he grows into a master archer in the desert.
cccReferences: CCC 305 (Divine providence caring for all human beings); CCC 2571; CCC 841.
historicalContext: Nomadic desert archer (*roveh qasshat*) lifestyle in the Paran wilderness.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi Elohim eth-ha-na'ar vayyigdal vayyeshev ba-midbar vayehi roveh qasshat*: *roveh qasshat* (a shooter of the bow / archer).
historicalTrivia: The phrase *Vayehi Elohim eth-ha-na'ar* ('And God was with the boy') is reused for Joseph in Egypt (Gen 39:2: 'The Lord was with Joseph').

dominicalIntent: He lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt (*me-eretz Mitzrayim*). Ishmael settles in Paran (Sinai peninsula) and marries an Egyptian wife chosen by Hagar, connecting his lineage back to Egypt.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Ishmael's settlement in Paran); Gen 25:18.
historicalContext: The wilderness of Paran (*Midbar Paran*) covers the central plateau of the Sinai Peninsula.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyeshev be-midbar Paran vattiqach-lo immo ishah me-eretz Mitzrayim*.
historicalTrivia: Habakkuk 3:3 connects Mount Paran to divine manifestations: 'God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran'.

dominicalIntent: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham: 'God is with you in all that you do' (*Elohim immakhe be-khol asher-atah oseh*). PAGAN TESTIMONY TO GOD'S PRESENCE! Abimelech and his general Phicol come to Abraham acknowledging: 'God is with you in ALL that you do!' The holiness of the faithful compels world leaders to recognize the presence of God.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Gentile recognition of God's blessing on Abraham); CCC 2044 (Christian witness to the world); Gen 26:28.
historicalContext: Formal diplomatic visit by the Philistine king and his commander-in-chief (*sar-tzeva'o*) to establish a non-aggression treaty.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ba-eth ha-hi vayyo'mer Avimelech u-Phiikhol sar-tzeva'o el-Avraham... Elohim immakhe be-khol asher-atah oseh*: *sar-tzeva'o* (captain/commander of the army).
historicalTrivia: Zechariah 8:23 echoes Genesis 21:22: 'Ten men from nations of every language shall take hold of the robe of a Jew, saying, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you".'

dominicalIntent: 'Now therefore swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my descendants or with my posterity, but as I have dealt kindly with you, so you will deal with me and with the land where you have sojourned.' Abimelech requests a perpetual non-aggression treaty (*covenant of kindness*) based on his past favor to Abraham.
cccReferences: CCC 2101 (Solemn treaty oaths taken before God); CCC 1939 (International peace treaties).
historicalContext: Non-aggression treaty (*covenant of peace*) protecting dynastic descendants (*niqri ve-nechdi* = offspring and posterity).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah hissava-li Veloheim hennah im-tishqor li u-le-ninni u-le-nechdi ka-chesed asher-asithi immakha ta'aseh immadi...*: *ninni ve-nechdi* ('my off-spring and my progeny').
historicalTrivia: The legal idiom *ninni ve-nechdi* ('my progeny and posterity') is an ancient West Semitic legal formula found in Ugaritic and Phoenician royal treaties.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham said: 'I will swear' (*Anochi issava*). Abraham agrees to the treaty, demonstrating that Christians are called to live peacefully with all men, making solemn covenants of peace.
cccReferences: CCC 2305 (Seeking peace with all neighbors); CCC 2101; Rom 12:18.
historicalContext: Patriarchal acceptance of an international peace alliance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avraham Anochi issava*: *issava* (Niphal imperfect: 'I will swear / bind myself by oath').
historicalTrivia: Romans 12:18 ('If possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all') reflects Abraham's treaty with Abimelech.

dominicalIntent: When Abraham reproved Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized (*ve-hochiach Avraham eth-Avimelech al-odoth be'er ha-mayim*). Before ratifying the treaty, Abraham addresses a real grievance: water rights! True peace requires addressing unresolved injustices rather than sweeping them under the rug.
cccReferences: CCC 2304 (Peace as the work of justice: resolving real grievances); CCC 2477.
historicalContext: Water wells in arid Negev were high-value legal real estate essential for flock survival; seizing a well was an act of war.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hochiach Avraham eth-Avimelech al-odoth be'er ha-mayim asher gazlu avdey Avimelech*: *hochiach* (reproved/rebuked/rectified). *Gazlu* (seized by robbery).
historicalTrivia: Matthew 18:15 ('If your brother sins against you, go and tell him his fault') mirrors Abraham's direct reproof (*hochiach*) to Abimelech.

dominicalIntent: Abimelech said: 'I do not know who has done this thing; you did not tell me, and I have not heard of it until today.' Abimelech disavows knowledge of his servants' illegal seizure, accepting Abraham's correction.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Accepting correction in truth); CCC 2304.
historicalContext: Royal disavowal of unauthorized actions committed by regional boundary guards.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avimelech lo yadati mi asah eth-ha-davar ha-zeh ve-gam-atah lo-higgadtha li ve-gam anochi lo shama'ti bilti ha-yom*.
historicalTrivia: Abimelech's prompt disavowal allows the dispute to be resolved legally through covenant restitution rather than armed conflict.

dominicalIntent: So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant (*vayyikhrthu sheneyhem berith*). Abraham bestows sacrificial livestock gifts upon Abimelech, and they cut a covenant (*karath berith*) together. Peace is sealed through mutual covenant gifts.
cccReferences: CCC 2304 (Establishment of peace treaties); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Formal treaty sealing involving exchange of sacrificial animals and covenant oaths.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqach Avraham tzon u-vaqar vayyitten le-Avimelech vayyikhrthu sheneyhem berith*: *vayyikhrthu* (and they cut / ratified).
historicalTrivia: This is the first international peace treaty between Israel's patriarch and a foreign ruler recorded in Scripture.

dominicalIntent: Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves (*Vayyatzev Avraham eth-sheva kevasoth ha-tzon levadhen*). Abraham sets apart SEVEN EWE LAMBS (*sheva kevasoth*) as a special legal testimony.
cccReferences: CCC 2101 (Legal pledge under oath); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Special 7-lamb legal deposit establishing permanent well ownership title.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyatzev Avraham eth-sheva kevasoth ha-tzon levadhen*: *sheva* (seven / covenant). *Kevasoth* (female lambs).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew root for 'seven' (*sheva*) is identical to the root for 'swearing an oath' (*shava*), linking the 7 lambs directly to oath-taking.

dominicalIntent: And Abimelech said to Abraham: 'What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?' Abimelech inquires about the specific legal symbol of the seven lambs.
cccReferences: CCC 1145 (Understanding covenantal signs).
historicalContext: Legal inquiry into a unique treaty gesture.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avimelech el-Avraham mah hennah sheva kevasoth ha-eleh asher hitzavtha levadhen*.
historicalTrivia: In ancient Semitic legal transactions, setting items apart 'by themselves' (*levadhen*) indicated an independent legal Quitclaim deed.

dominicalIntent: He said: 'These seven ewe lambs you will accept from my hand, that this may be a witness for me that I dug this well' (*le-ma'an thihyeh-li le-edah ki chapharther eth-ha-be'er ha-zoth*). The seven lambs serve as an unassailable legal WITNESS (*edah*) confirming Abraham's sole ownership of the well he dug.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Truth and legal witness); CCC 2101.
historicalContext: Quitclaim deed and bill of sale establishing water rights title.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer ki eth-sheva kevasoth tiqqach mi-yadi le-ma'an thihyeh-li le-edah ki chapharther eth-ha-be'er ha-zoth*: *le-edah* ('for a legal testimony/witness').
historicalTrivia: Receiving gifts from a party's hand (*mi-yadi*) in ANE law constituted legally binding acceptance of the associated terms.

dominicalIntent: Therefore that place was called Beersheba (*Be'er Sheva*), because there both of them swore an oath (*ki sham nishbe'u sheneyhem*). FOUNDING OF BEERSHEBA! The city is named **Beersheba** (*Be'er Sheva*), which means both 'Well of Seven' and 'Well of the Oath' (*sheva / shava*). Beersheba becomes the sacred southern sanctuary of the Promised Land ('From Dan to Beersheba').
cccReferences: CCC 2101 (Sanctuary of the oath); CCC 2571 (Beersheba as holy site of peace); 1 Kings 4:25.
historicalContext: Beersheba (Tell es-Saba / modern Beer Sheva) controlling the southern trade routes and desert springs.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Al-ken qara la-maqom ha-hu Be'er Sheva ki sham nishbe'u sheneyhem*: *Be'er Sheva* (Well of Seven / Well of Oath). *Nishbe'u* (they swore an oath, root *shava*).
historicalTrivia: The proverbial phrase 'from Dan to Beersheba' (1 Sam 3:20) defined the complete north-to-south biblical extent of the Holy Land.

dominicalIntent: So they made a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army rose up and returned to the land of the Philistines. The non-aggression covenant is successfully ratified. Abimelech departs in peace.
cccReferences: CCC 2304 (Successful peace treaty established); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Conclusion of the international treaty conference at Beersheba.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyikhrthu verith bi-V'er Sheva vayyaqam Avimelech u-Phiikhol sar-tzeva'o vayyashuvu el-eretz Pelishtim*.
historicalTrivia: This covenant at Beersheba secured peaceful grazing rights for Abraham's clan for decades in the southern Negev.

dominicalIntent: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba (*Vayyitta eshel bi-V'er Sheva*) and called there on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God (*El Olam*). THIS IS THE FIRST APPEARANCE OF THE DIVINE NAME EL OLAM ('The Everlasting God')! Abraham plants a long-living tamarisk tree (*eshel*) and invokes Yahweh as **El Olam**—the Eternal, Unchanging God who endures across all generations.
cccReferences: CCC 212 (God as El Olam—Eternal, Unchanging, and Faithful); CCC 2570 (Abraham worshipping El Olam); CCC 2097; Ps 90:2; Isa 40:28.
historicalContext: Tamarisk trees (*Tamarix aphylla* / *eshel*) are evergreen desert trees with deep taproots capable of reaching deep groundwater, living for centuries in arid soil.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyitta eshel bi-V'er Sheva vayyiqra-sham be-shem YHVH El Olam*: *eshel* (tamarisk tree). *El Olam* ('God of Eternity / Everlasting God').
historicalTrivia: Tamarisk trees secrete salt on their leaves, absorbing night humidity and producing a natural cooling condensation mist beneath their branches—making them iconic desert shade trees.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham sojourned many days in the land of the Philistines (*Vayyagar Avraham be-eretz Pelishtim yamim rabbim*). Abraham lives in peaceful sojourn in the Negev. This season of peaceful rest at Beersheba prepares Abraham for the ultimate trial of his faith in Genesis 22—the Sacrifice of Isaac on Mount Moriah.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The peaceful interlude at Beersheba preparing Abraham for his supreme test on Moriah); CCC 145; Heb 11:17.
historicalContext: Extended peaceful pastoral residence in the Negev around Beersheba.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyagar Avraham be-eretz Pelishtim yamim rabbim*: *yamim rabbim* ('many days / long years').
historicalTrivia: Genesis 21 concludes at Beersheba with Abraham at peace, setting up the sudden, dramatic opening of Genesis 22: 'After these things God tested Abraham'.

dominicalIntent: After these things God tested Abraham (*ha-Elohim nissah eth-Avraham*) and said to him, 'Abraham!' And he said, 'Here I am' (*Hinneni*). THIS IS THE AKEDAH (THE BINDING OF ISAAC)—THE SUPREME TEST OF FAITH IN THE OLD TESTAMENT! God tests (*nissah*) Abraham not to cause him to fall, but to refine, prove, and manifest his heroic faith to all generations. Abraham's immediate response *Hinneni* ('Here I am!') expresses absolute availability to the divine call, prefiguring Our Lady's *Fiat* (Luke 1:38) and Christ's *Ecce venio* (Heb 10:7).
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (The Sacrifice of Isaac as the supreme test of Abraham's faith); CCC 145 (Obedience of faith pushed to the ultimate limit); CCC 603; Heb 11:17; Jas 2:21.
historicalContext: The supreme test (*nissah*) of Abraham's 50-year journey of faith (from Gen 12 call to Gen 22 Moriah).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi achar ha-devarim ha-elleh ve-ha-Elohim nissah eth-Avraham vayyo'mer elav Avraham vayyo'mer Hinneni*: *nissah* (tested/proved/refined, root *nasah*). *Hinneni* ('Behold me! / Here I am!').
crossReferences: Hebrews 11:17; James 2:21; Luke 1:38; Hebrews 10:7; 1 Maccabees 2:52; Sirach 44:20.
historicalTrivia: 1 Maccabees 2:52 summarizes this verse: 'Was not Abraham found faithful when tested (*en peirasmo*), and it was reckoned to him as righteousness?'

dominicalIntent: He said: 'Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love (*Qach-na eth-bincha eth-yechidcha asher-ahavtha eth-Yitzchaq*), and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I shall tell you.' THIS IS THE SUPREME TYPOLOGICAL PROMISE OF THE CROSS! God says: 'Take your son, YOUR ONLY SON (*yechidcha*), WHOM YOU LOVE (*asher-ahavtha*), and offer him as a burnt offering (*olah*)!' This is the FIRST TIME THE WORD 'LOVE' (*ahav*) APPEARS IN THE BIBLE! It appears in the context of a father offering his only beloved son as a sacrifice! This is the exact prefiguration of John 3:16: 'For God so loved the world that He gave His ONLY SON (*Ton Huion ton monogenē*)'! Mount Moriah is the exact location of Golgotha/Jerusalem!
cccReferences: CCC 603 (God spared not His own Son, prefigured by Abraham offering his only son Isaac); CCC 2572 (The ultimate sacrifice); CCC 599; John 3:16; Rom 8:32; 2 Chron 3:1.
historicalContext: Land of Moriah (*Eretz Moriyyah*): 2 Chronicles 3:1 explicitly identifies Mount Moriah as the Temple Mount in Jerusalem, where Solomon built the Temple and where Golgotha is situated!
translationNuances: Hebrew *Qach-na eth-bincha eth-yechidcha asher-ahavtha eth-Yitzchaq ve-lech-lekha el-eretz ha-Moriyyah ve-ha'alehu sham le-olah*: *yechidcha* (your only one / beloved one). *Ahavtha* (you loved, FIRST MENTION of love in Scripture!). *Moriyyah* (from *ra'ah* = 'Yahweh provides / Yahweh reveals').
crossReferences: John 3:16; Romans 8:32; 2 Chronicles 3:1; Hebrews 11:17-19; 1 John 4:9; Matthew 3:17.
historicalTrivia: 2 Chronicles 3:1 explicitly records: 'Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah (*be-har ha-Moriyyah*)', proving that Isaac was offered on the exact site of Jerusalem!

dominicalIntent: So Abraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and his son Isaac. And he cut the wood for the burnt offering and arose and went to the place of which God had told him. ABSOLUTE PROMPT OBEDIENCE! Abraham rises at early dawn (*Vayyasqem ba-boqer*). He does not delay, debate, or complain; he personally splits the wood for his own son's sacrifice. Abraham's silent obedience prefigures Christ silently carrying the wood of the Cross.
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (Abraham's heroic silent obedience); CCC 145 (The obedience of faith); CCC 612.
historicalContext: Preparation for a 3-day trekking journey from Beersheba to Mount Moriah (approx. 50 miles / 80 km).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyasqem Avraham ba-boqer vayyachavosh eth-chamoro vayyiqach eth-sheny ne'arav itto ve-eth Yitzchaq bno vayvatta eth-atzei ha-olah...*: *vayvatta* (split/cleaved).
historicalTrivia: Abraham splitting the wood (*atzei ha-olah*) with his own hands underscores his active, personal participation in the sacrificial preparation.

dominicalIntent: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from afar (*Ba-yom ha-shelishi vayyissa Avraham eth-eynav vayyar eth-ha-maqom me-rachoq*). THE THIRD DAY! For three days, in Abraham's mind and heart, Isaac was ALREADY DEAD! On the Third Day, Isaac is restored to life! St. Paul (1 Cor 15:4) states that Christ rose on the Third Day 'according to the Scriptures'—referring directly to Genesis 22:4 and Hosea 6:2! Isaac's 3-day journey is the supreme Old Testament type of Christ's 3-day Resurrection!
cccReferences: CCC 627 (The Third Day Resurrection prefigured in the Old Testament); CCC 2572 (Faith on the Third Day); 1 Cor 15:4; Heb 11:19; Hos 6:2.
historicalContext: 3-day trek from Beersheba across the Judean desert arriving at the ridge overlooking Mount Moriah (Jerusalem).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ba-yom ha-shelishi vayyissa Avraham eth-eynav vayyar eth-ha-maqom me-rachoq*: *Ba-yom ha-shelishi* ('On the third day'). *Ha-maqom* ('The Place' = sacred sanctuary site).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:19 explicitly commentary on the Third Day: 'He considered that God was able to raise men even from the dead, hence, figuratively speaking, he did receive him back (*en parabolē*)'.

dominicalIntent: Then Abraham said to his young men: 'Stay here with the donkey; I and the boy will go over there and worship and come again to you' (*ve-nishtachaveh ve-nashuvah aleykhem*). ABRAHAM'S FAITH IN THE RESURRECTION! Notice what Abraham says to the servants: 'I and the boy will go yonder and worship, AND WE WILL COME AGAIN TO YOU' (*nashuvah* = WE shall return)! Abraham believed that even if he slaughtered Isaac, God WOULD RAISE HIM FROM THE DEAD (Heb 11:19)! Abraham defines the supreme act of sacrifice as **worship** (*nishtachaveh*).
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (Abraham's faith in the Resurrection when offering Isaac); CCC 992 (Early revelation of resurrection faith); Heb 11:19; CCC 2099.
historicalContext: Leaving the servants and transport animals behind at the base of Moriah so that father and son ascend the holy mountain alone.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avraham el-ne'arav Shevu-lakhem poh im-ha-chamor ve-ani ve-ha-na'ar nelekhah ad-koh ve-nishtachaveh ve-nashuvah aleykhem*: *nashuvah* (1st person plural cohortative: 'WE shall return!'). *Nishtachaveh* (we will prostrate/worship).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:19 states: 'He considered that God was able to raise men even from the dead', providing the inspired commentary on Abraham's plural verb *nashuvah* ('WE shall return').

dominicalIntent: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son (*vayyasem al-Yitzchaq bno*); and he took in his hand the fire and the knife. So they went both of them together (*vayyelechu sheneyhem yachdav*). ISAAC CARRYING THE WOOD OF HIS OWN SACRIFICE! Isaac carries the heavy wood of the burnt offering up Mount Moriah upon his own shoulders. This is the exact, unassailable prefiguration of Jesus Christ carrying the wood of His own Cross up Mount Calvary (*Golgotha*)! Father and Son walk 'both of them together' (*yachdav*) in complete, harmonious self-giving.
cccReferences: CCC 603 (Isaac carrying the wood of the sacrifice prefiguring Christ carrying the Cross); CCC 2572; John 19:17; St. Melito of Sardis *Peri Pascha*.
historicalContext: Ascending the steep slopes of Mount Moriah; the father carrying the sacrificial brazier (*fire*) and slaughtering cleaver (*machete/knife*), the son carrying the heavy firewood.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqach Avraham eth-atzei ha-olah vayyasem al-Yitzchaq bno vayyiqach be-yado eth-ha-esh ve-eth-ha-ma'acheleth vayyelechu sheneyhem yachdav*: *ma'acheleth* (slaughter knife, root *akhal* = to consume). *Yachdav* (together / in perfect unity).
historicalTrivia: 2nd-century Father St. Melito of Sardis wrote: 'Christ carried the wood upon His shoulders as Isaac carried the wood for his father's altar; Christ was bound like a ram, sacrificed like a lamb'.

dominicalIntent: And Isaac said to his father Abraham: 'My father!' And he said: 'Here I am, my son.' He said: 'Behold, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?' (*ve-ayyeh ha-seh le-olah*). ISAAC'S QUESTION: 'WHERE IS THE LAMB?' Isaac notices that all sacrificial elements are present except the victim: 'Where is the lamb (*ha-seh*)?' This question echoes down 2,000 years of salvation history until John the Baptist points to Jesus by the Jordan River and answers Isaac's question: 'BEHOLD THE LAMB OF GOD (*Ecce Agnus Dei*), who takes away the sin of the world!' (John 1:29)!
cccReferences: CCC 608 (Jesus as the Lamb of God fulfilling Isaac's question); CCC 2572; John 1:29; 1 Pet 1:19; Rev 5:6.
historicalContext: Dialogue between loving father and trusting son climbing Mount Moriah.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Yitzchaq el-Avraham aviv vayyo'mer Avi vayyo'mer Hinneni veni vayyo'mer hinneh ha-esh ve-ha-etz ve-ayyeh ha-seh le-olah*: *ha-seh* (the lamb / young sheep).
crossReferences: John 1:29; John 1:36; 1 Peter 1:19; Revelation 5:6; Isaiah 53:7; Exodus 12:3.
historicalTrivia: John the Baptist's proclamation *Behold the Lamb of God* (John 1:29) is the explicit theological answer to Isaac's question *Where is the lamb?* in Genesis 22:7.

dominicalIntent: Abraham said: 'God will provide for himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son' (*Elohim yir'eh-lo ha-seh le-olah beni*). So they went both of them together. ABRAHAM'S PROPHETIC RESPONSE: 'GOD WILL PROVIDE HIMSELF THE LAMB!' Abraham utters a supreme prophecy: God Himself will provide the Lamb for the offering. This was fulfilled when God the Father provided His own Son, Jesus Christ—the true Lamb of God—on that very mountain! Again, the refrain is repeated: 'they went both of them together' (*yachdav*), showing Father and Son united in redemptive purpose.
cccReferences: CCC 603 (God providing the true Lamb in Christ); CCC 2572 (Prophetic trust of Abraham); John 1:29; Heb 10:5-7.
historicalContext: Prophetic declaration of divine provision (*Elohim yir'eh*) establishing the theological foundation for Mount Moriah.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avraham Elohim yir'eh-lo ha-seh le-olah beni vayyelechu sheneyhem yachdav*: *Elohim yir'eh* ('God will see/provide for Himself').
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew verb *yir'eh* means both 'to see' and 'to provide' (as in English *pro-vision* = seeing ahead), establishing that God's sight is His provision.

dominicalIntent: When they came to the place of which God had told him, Abraham built the altar there and laid the wood in order and bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood (*vayya'avoz eth-Yitzchaq bno vayyasem otho al-ha-mizbeach*). ISAAC'S VOLUNTARY SUBMISSION! Isaac was a strong young man (capable of carrying 50 lbs of wood up a mountain), while Abraham was over 100 years old. Isaac could easily have resisted or run away! Instead, Isaac VOLUNTARILY SUBMITS to be bound (*akedah*) and laid upon the altar. Isaac prefigures Jesus Christ, who voluntarily surrendered Himself to be bound and nailed to the Cross out of obedience to the Father!
cccReferences: CCC 612 (Christ's voluntary self-surrender on the Cross prefigured by Isaac's binding); CCC 2572; Phil 2:8; John 10:17-18.
historicalContext: The binding (*Akedah*) of Isaac upon the wooden altar. In Jewish tradition, this event is called *The Akedah* ('The Binding').
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo'u el-ha-maqom... vayyiven sham Avraham eth-ha-mizbeach vayya'arokh eth-ha-atziym vayya'aqod eth-Yitzchaq bno vayyasem otho al-ha-mizbeach mi-ma'al la-atziym*: *vayya'aqod* (and he bound/fettered, root *aqad* -> *Akedah*!).
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew root *aqad* (to bind the legs of a sacrificial victim) occurs as a verb ONLY HERE in the entire Hebrew Bible, giving birth to the iconic title *The Akedah*.

dominicalIntent: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son (*vayyiqach eth-ha-ma'acheleth li-shchot eth-bno*). THE MOMENT OF ABSOLUTE SURRENDER! Abraham raises the slaughtering knife (*ma'acheleth*) to slay his beloved son. In his heart and intent, the sacrifice was 100% completed! Abraham held nothing back from God. This prefigures God the Father, who 'spared not his own Son, but gave him up for us all' (Rom 8:32).
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (Abraham offering his son completely in his heart); CCC 603; Rom 8:32; Heb 11:17.
historicalContext: The climax of the sacrificial ritual: raising the sacrificial cleaver (*ma'acheleth*) for the ritual throat-slitting (*shachat*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyishlach Avraham eth-yado vayyiqach eth-ha-ma'acheleth li-shchot eth-bno*: *li-shchot* (infinitive of *shachat*, to slaughter/throat-slit a sacrificial victim).
historicalTrivia: James 2:21 states: 'Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered his son Isaac upon the altar?' pointing to this exact moment in v. 10.

dominicalIntent: But the Angel of the Lord called to him from heaven and said: 'Abraham, Abraham!' And he said: 'Here I am' (*Hinneni*). THE ANGEL INTERVENES FROM HEAVEN! At the precise millisecond before the knife falls, the Angel of the Lord (*Mal'akh YHVH*) shouts from heaven, calling Abraham's name twice: 'Abraham, Abraham!' Abraham answers a second time: *Hinneni* ('Here I am!'). God halts the physical slaying because Abraham's heart has already proven total love.
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (God arresting the knife and sparing Isaac); CCC 332 (Angelic intervention); CCC 707.
historicalContext: Urgent double-name invocation (*Avraham, Avraham*) from heaven arresting an immediate action.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra elav mal'akh YHVH min-ha-shamayim vayyo'mer Avraham Avraham vayyo'mer Hinneni*: double name call (*Avraham Avraham*) signals supreme spiritual crisis.
historicalTrivia: Double-name calls from God occur only four times in Scripture: 'Abraham, Abraham!' (Gen 22:11), 'Jacob, Jacob!' (Gen 46:2), 'Moses, Moses!' (Exod 3:4), and 'Saul, Saul!' (Acts 9:4).

dominicalIntent: He said: 'Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God (*ki attah yadati ki-yere Elohim attah*), seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.' DIVINE TESTIMONY TO ABRAHAM'S FAITH! God declares: 'NOW I KNOW THAT YOU FEAR GOD!' Abraham proved he loved God above all created gifts, even his own only son. God abolishes human sacrifice forever, showing that He desires not human blood, but total spiritual surrender.
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (Abraham proving total love and holy fear of God); CCC 2096 (Fear of the Lord as reverence and total love); CCC 2100; Heb 11:17-19.
historicalContext: Formal divine rejection and condemnation of human child sacrifice, separating Israelite worship from Canaanite Molech rites.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Al-tishlach yadkha el-ha-na'ar ve-al-ta'as lo me'umah ki attah yadati ki-yere Elohim attah ve-lo chasakhta eth-bincha eth-yechidcha mimmenni*: *ve-lo chasakhta* ('and you did not withhold/spare').
historicalTrivia: Romans 8:32 ('He who did not spare (*epheisato*) his own Son') directly quotes the Septuagint translation of Genesis 22:12 (*ouk epheisō* / 'you did not spare').

dominicalIntent: And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by his horns. And Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son (*vayya'alehu le-olah thachath bno*). THE RAM SUBSTITUTED FOR ISAAC! Abraham sees a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. Abraham sacrifices the RAM IN PLACE OF HIS SON (*thachath bno*). The ram's head caught in thorns prefigures Jesus Christ, crowned with thorns, who dies as our SACRIFICING SUBSTITUTE on the Cross!
cccReferences: CCC 603 (Substitutionary sacrifice: the ram in place of Isaac prefiguring Christ dying in place of humanity); CCC 2572; CCC 614; Matt 27:29; 1 Pet 2:24.
historicalContext: Substitutionary sacrificial victim (*thachath bno* = 'instead of / in place of his son') establishing the theology of vicarious atonement.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyissa Avraham eth-eynav vayyar ve-hinneh-ayil achar ne'echaz ba-ssevakh be-qarnav... vayya'alehu le-olah thachath bno*: *ayil* (ram). *Sevakh* (thicket/thorns). *Thachath bno* ('in place of his son').
historicalTrivia: Early Church Fathers (St. Augustine, St. Ambrose, St. Melito) noted: Isaac represents Christ's divine nature which could not die; the ram caught in thorns represents Christ's human nature crowned with thorns and sacrificed.

dominicalIntent: So Abraham called the name of that place 'The Lord will provide' (*YHVH Yir'eh*); as it is said to this day, 'On the mount of the Lord it shall be provided' (*Be-har YHVH yira'eh*). FOUNDING OF THE SACRED NAME JEHOVAH-JIREH (*YHVH Yir'eh*)! Abraham names the mountain **YHVH Yir'eh** ('The Lord Will Provide' / 'The Lord Will See'). The proverbial saying arose in Israel: 'On the Mount of the Lord it shall be provided!' On this exact mountain (Moriah / Golgotha), God provided the ultimate Sacrifice for the redemption of the world.
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (YHVH Yir'eh—God providing salvation on the Holy Mountain); CCC 603; CCC 212; 2 Chron 3:1.
historicalContext: Naming the sacred mountain site (Mount Moriah / Jerusalem) to commemorate divine provision.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra Avraham shem-ha-maqom ha-hu YHVH Yir'eh asher yeyamer ha-yom be-har YHVH yira'eh*: *YHVH Yir'eh* ('Yahweh will see / provide'). *Be-har YHVH yira'eh* ('In the mountain of Yahweh it shall be seen / provided').
historicalTrivia: Mount Moriah (*be-har YHVH*) became the site of Solomon's Temple where all Israelite sacrifices were offered, and just outside its walls, the site of Christ's Crucifixion.

dominicalIntent: And the Angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time from heaven (*Vayyiqra mal'akh YHVH el-Avraham shenith min-ha-shamayim*). The Angel calls a second time from heaven to bestow the supreme, unalterable Oath Covenant upon Abraham.
cccReferences: CCC 2572 (The second call from heaven ratifying the Oath Covenant); CCC 59-60; Heb 6:13-18.
historicalContext: Second divine utterance solemnizing the Oath Covenant following the completion of the test.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra mal'akh YHVH el-Avraham shenith min-ha-shamayim*: *shenith* (a second time).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 6:13-18 bases the absolute unchangeable certainty of Christian hope on this second call of Genesis 22:15-18.

dominicalIntent: And said: 'By myself I have sworn, declares the Lord (*Bi nishba'ti ne'um-YHVH*), because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son...' GOD SWARS BY HIMSELF! Because there was no one greater to swear by, GOD SWORES AN OATH BY HIS OWN DIVINE ESSENCE (*Bi nishba'ti*)! This is the ONLY TIME IN THE PENTATEUCH that God swears an oath to Abraham! This Oath Covenant (*Berith Shevu'ah*) makes the promise irrevocably unalterable, guaranteed by God's own existence.
cccReferences: CCC 59-60 (The Oath Covenant sworn by God Himself); CCC 212; Heb 6:13-18; Luke 1:73.
historicalContext: The highest legal solemnization possible in the cosmos: the Creator swearing by His own eternal self-existence.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Bi nishba'ti ne'um-YHVH ki ya'an asher asitha eth-ha-davar ha-zeh ve-lo chasakhta eth-bincha eth-yechidkha*: *Bi nishba'ti* ('By Myself I have sworn!'). *Ne'um-YHVH* (oracle/declaration of Yahweh).
crossReferences: Hebrews 6:13-18; Luke 1:73; Psalm 105:9; Isaiah 45:23; Jeremiah 22:5; Exodus 32:13.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 6:13 commentary: 'For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he had no one greater by whom to swear, HE SWORE BY HIMSELF, saying, "Surely I will bless you..."'.

dominicalIntent: I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and as the sand that is on the seashore (*ka-kokhavey ha-shamayim u-khe-chol asher al-sephath ha-yam*). And your offspring shall possess the gate of his enemies (*ve-yirash zar'akha eth sha'ar oyevav*). THE DUAL PROMISE OF MULTITUDE AND VICTORY! Abraham's seed will be as the stars of heaven (heavenly saints) and sand of the seashore (earthly believers). Furthermore, the singular Seed (*zar'akha*) shall **POSSESS THE GATE OF HIS ENEMIES**! Christ, the Seed of Abraham, smashes the gates of Hell and death (Matt 16:18)!
cccReferences: CCC 60 (Innumerable offspring as stars and sand); CCC 552 (Christ smashing the gates of Hades, prefigured by possessing the gate of enemies); Matt 16:18; Heb 11:12; Rev 1:18.
historicalContext: Possessing a city's gate (*sha'ar*) meant total military conquest and occupation of the enemy's stronghold.
translationNuances: Hebrew *ki-varekh avarekhkha ve-harbah arbeh eth-zar'akha ka-kokhavey ha-shamayim... ve-yirash zar'akha eth sha'ar oyevav*: *ki-varekh avarekhkha* (blessing I will bless you). *Sha'ar oyevav* ('gate of his enemies').
crossReferences: Matthew 16:18; Genesis 24:60; Luke 1:74; Hebrews 11:12; Revelation 1:18; Psalm 127:5.
historicalTrivia: Jesus' promise to Peter in Matthew 16:18 ('the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it') directly echoes the messianic victory prophecy of Genesis 22:17.

dominicalIntent: And in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed (*ve-hithbarakhu ve-zar'akha kol goyey ha-aretz*), because you have obeyed my voice. THE ULTIMATE COVENANT PROMISE! In Abraham's SEED (*zar'akha* = singular, Jesus Christ), ALL NATIONS OF THE EARTH SHALL BE BLESSED! St. Paul in Galatians 3:16 proves that 'Seed' refers specifically to Christ. Through Christ's sacrifice on Moriah/Calvary, salvation is poured out upon all Gentiles in the Catholic Church.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (Universal blessing of all nations through Christ, the Seed of Abraham); CCC 706; Gal 3:8; Gal 3:16; Acts 3:25; Luke 1:55.
historicalContext: Culmination of the 7 covenant promises to Abraham, elevated to an unalterable sworn Oath Covenant.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hithbarakhu ve-zar'akha kol goyey ha-aretz eqev asher shama'ta be-qoli*: *Ve-hithbarakhu* (Hithpael: 'shall bless themselves / find blessing'). *Eqev* ('because / in consequence of').
crossReferences: Galatians 3:8; Galatians 3:16; Acts 3:25; Genesis 12:3; Genesis 26:4; Luke 1:55.
historicalTrivia: Acts 3:25 quotes Genesis 22:18: 'You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant... saying to Abraham, "And in your posture/seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed".'

dominicalIntent: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they arose and went together to Beersheba; and Abraham lived at Beersheba (*vayyeshev Avraham bi-V'er Sheva*). Abraham returns down the mountain to his young men and dwells at Beersheba. Notice: Isaac is not explicitly mentioned returning down the mountain! Typologically, Isaac remains 'on the mountain' (ascended/sacrificed) until he reappears in Genesis 24 to receive his Bride (Rebekah)—prefiguring Christ ascending to heaven and coming to receive His Bride, the Church!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham returning to Beersheba in peace); CCC 757 (Christ and the Bride).
historicalContext: Return trek to the southern sanctuary encampment at Beersheba.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyashav Avraham el-ne'arav vayyaqumu vayyelechu yachdaw el-Be'er Sheva vayyeshev Avraham bi-V'er Sheva*.
historicalTrivia: Patristic writers noted that Isaac does not appear again in the Genesis narrative until Genesis 24:62, where he meets his bride Rebekah in the field at evening.

dominicalIntent: Now after these things it was told to Abraham: 'Behold, Milcah also has borne children to your brother Nahor.' The narrative turns to the genealogy of Abraham's brother Nahor in Mesopotamia. God is quietly preparing the family line from which **Rebekah**—the bride of Isaac—will emerge!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Providential preparation of Isaac's bride); CCC 307.
historicalContext: News conveyed by trade caravans from Haran/Mesopotamia regarding Nahor's clan expansion.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi acharey ha-devarim ha-elleh vayyuggad le-Avraham le'mor hinneh yaldah Milcah gam-hi banim le-Nachor achikha*.
historicalTrivia: Caravan news networks along the Fertile Crescent regularly brought family reports across 500 miles between Haran and Canaan.

dominicalIntent: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram. Uz and Buz represent Aramean and North Arabian tribal ancestors.
cccReferences: CCC 842 (Genealogical preservation).
historicalContext: Aramean tribal ancestors; Uz (Job's homeland, Job 1:1); Elihu the Buzite (Job 32:2).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Eth-Uz bekhoro ve-eth-Buz achiv ve-eth-Qemu'el avi Aram*.
historicalTrivia: Elihu in Job 32:2 is called 'Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite', directly linking his family to Buz son of Nahor in Genesis 22:21.

dominicalIntent: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel. The genealogy reaches **Bethuel**—the father of Rebekah!
cccReferences: CCC 307 (Providential genealogy).
historicalContext: Nahor's line in Upper Mesopotamia.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-eth-Kesed ve-eth-Chazo ve-eth-Pildash ve-eth-Yidlaph ve-eth Bethu'el*.
historicalTrivia: Bethuel (*Bethu'el*) means 'Dweller in God' or 'House of God'.

dominicalIntent: Bethuel fathered Rebekah (*U-Vethu'el yalad eth-Rivqah*). These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother. REBEKAH IS INTRODUCED! The entire genealogy of vv. 20-24 was recorded for one primary purpose: to introduce **Rebekah** (*Rivqah*)! Rebekah will become the holy wife of Isaac, prefiguring the Church, the spotless Bride of Christ.
cccReferences: CCC 757 (Rebekah as bride of Isaac prefiguring the Church as Bride of Christ); CCC 507; CCC 1655.
historicalContext: Introducing the future matriarch of Israel born in Haran.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-Vethu'el yalad eth-Rivqah shemonah elleh yaldah Milcah le-Nachor achi Avraham*: *Rivqah* (Rebekah, meaning 'captivating beauty' or 'tied/secured').
historicalTrivia: Rebekah is the second matriarch of Israel, whose miraculous birth and willingness to leave her homeland (Gen 24:58) mirrors Abraham's faith.

dominicalIntent: Moreover, his concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah. Nahor's four concubine sons, completing his 12 sons (8 by Milcah, 4 by Reumah), matching the 12-tribe structures of Ishmael (Gen 17:20) and Jacob (Gen 35:23).
cccReferences: CCC 842 (Preservation of Semitic tribal registers).
historicalContext: 12-tribe clan organization in Aram-Naharaim.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-phiylagsho u-shemah Re'umah vatyeled gam-hi eth-Tevach ve-eth-Gacham ve-eth-Tachash ve-eth-Ma'akhah*.
historicalTrivia: Maacah (*Ma'akhah*) became a Syrian kingdom near Mount Hermon mentioned in Joshua 13:13 and 2 Samuel 10:6.

dominicalIntent: Sarah lived 127 years; these were the years of the life of Sarah (*Vayyehyu chayyei Sarah me'ah shanah u-vessrim shanah ve-sheva shanim*). SARAH IS THE ONLY WOMAN IN SCRIPTURE WHOSE EXACT AGE AT DEATH IS RECORDED! Sarah dies at 127 years old, having witnessed the miraculous birth of Isaac (at 90) and his preservation on Moriah. She stands as the premier matriarch of faith in salvation history.
cccReferences: CCC 489 (Sarah as the premier Old Testament matriarch of faith); CCC 2571 (The passing of the matriarch); Heb 11:11; 1 Pet 3:6.
historicalContext: Sarah's lifespan of 127 years makes her 37 years older than Isaac (born when she was 90), meaning Isaac was 37 years old at the time of Sarah's death.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyehyu chayyei Sarah me'ah shanah u-vessrim shanim ve-sheva shanim shney chayyei Sarah*: repetition of *shney chayyei Sarah* ('years of the life of Sarah').
historicalTrivia: Sarah is the only woman in the entire Bible whose lifespan, age at death, and burial details are formally recorded in a dedicated chapter.

dominicalIntent: And Sarah died at Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her (*li-ssppod le-Sarah u-li-vvkhothah*). HOLY GRIEF FOR THE DEAD! Abraham enters to mourn (*li-ssppod*) and weep (*li-vvkhothah*) for Sarah. True Christian faith does not eliminate natural grief, but sanctifies it with hope in the Resurrection (1 Thess 4:13).
cccReferences: CCC 1681-1683 (Christian mourning for the dead in hope of the Resurrection); CCC 2571; 1 Thess 4:13; John 11:35.
historicalContext: Kiriath-arba ('City of Four', modern Hebron in the Judean hill country, 19 miles south of Jerusalem).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattomath Sarah bi-Qiryath Arba hi Chevron be-eretz Kena'an vayyavo Avraham li-ssppod le-Sarah u-li-vvkhothah*: *Qiryath Arba* (City of Four / Arba the giant). *Li-ssppod* (to wail/lament). *Li-vvkhothah* (to weep for her).
historicalTrivia: In Masoretic Hebrew manuscripts of Genesis 23:2, the letter *Khaf* in *li-vvkhothah* ('to weep for her') is written small (*littera minuta*), which rabbinic tradition interprets as Abraham weeping with restraint, tempering grief with faith.

dominicalIntent: And Abraham rose up from before his dead and said to the Hittites (*bney-Cheth*)... After performing the initial rites of mourning, Abraham rises up to secure a permanent, honorable burial plot in the Promised Land. Honoring the human body in death reflects faith in the bodily Resurrection.
cccReferences: CCC 2300 (Reverence and honorable burial for the bodies of the deceased); CCC 992 (Resurrection of the body); CCC 1683.
historicalContext: Negotiating with the Sons of Heth (*bney-Cheth*, Anatolian Hittite enclave residing around Hebron in the Middle Bronze Age).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyaqam Avraham me-al pney metho vaydabber el-bney-Cheth le'mor*: *bney-Cheth* (Sons of Heth / Hittites).
historicalTrivia: Hittite legal tablets discovered at Boghazköy (Hattusa) confirm the exact Hittite property transaction procedures recorded in Genesis 23 (purchasing a field along with its perimeter trees).

dominicalIntent: 'I am a stranger and a sojourner among you (*Ger-ve-thoshav anochi immakhem*); give me property for a burying place among you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.' ABRAHAM ADMITS HIS EARTHLY SOJOURN! Abraham calls himself a 'stranger and sojourner' (*Ger ve-thoshav*). St. Peter (1 Pet 2:11) and the Epistle to the Hebrews (Heb 11:13) quote this exact phrase to define the identity of all Christians on earth: we are strangers and exiles seeking a Heavenly Homeland!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham as stranger and sojourner); 1 Pet 2:11; Heb 11:13-16; CCC 2692; Ps 39:12.
historicalContext: A resident alien (*ger ve-thoshav*) lacked native property rights and required civic permission to purchase land.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ger-ve-thoshav anochi immakhem teni-li achuzzath-qever immakhem ve-eqberah methi mi-le-phanay*: *Ger* (resident alien/stranger). *Thoshav* (sojourner/tenant). *Achuzzath-qever* (possession of a burial tomb).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:13-14 commentary: 'These all died in faith... having acknowledged that they were strangers and exiles on the earth (*xenoi kai parepidēmoi*). For people who speak thus make it clear that they are seeking a homeland'.

dominicalIntent: The Hittites answered Abraham... The Hittites respond to Abraham with high diplomatic honor in the city gate assembly.
cccReferences: CCC 1939 (Respect and courtesy between nations).
historicalContext: Formal diplomatic protocol in an ANE civic assembly at the city gate.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'anu vney-Cheth eth-Avraham le'mor lo*.
historicalTrivia: Negotiating land purchases required full public assembly of city elders (*all who went in at the gate of his city*) to act as legal witnesses.

dominicalIntent: 'Hear us, my lord; you are a prince of God among us (*nesi Elohim attah be-thokhenu*). Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. None of us will withhold from you his tomb...' GENTILE TESTIMONY TO ABRAHAM'S HOLINESS! The Hittites call Abraham a **PRINCE OF GOD** (*nesi Elohim*)! Abraham's holy life compelled pagan neighbors to recognize his divine dignity.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Pagan recognition of Abraham as a Prince of God); CCC 2044; Gen 21:22.
historicalContext: High diplomatic title *nesi Elohim* ('mighty prince / divine chieftain') granting royal burial privileges.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Shema'enu adoni nesi Elohim attah be-thokhenu be-mivchar qavaraynu qevor eth-methokha...*: *nesi Elohim* ('Prince/Chieftain of God'). *Mivchar* (choicest/best).
historicalTrivia: The title *nesi Elohim* is the highest secular honorific granted to any patriarch in Genesis, proving Abraham's immense regional standing.

dominicalIntent: Abraham rose and bowed to the Hittites, the people of the land (*vayyishtachu le-am-ha-aretz le-vney-Cheth*). Abraham bows in humble, courteous reverence (*vayyishtachu*) before the people of the land. True Christian sanctity produces noble manners, humility, and deep respect for all people.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Abraham's humility and courtesy); CCC 1939; Rom 12:10.
historicalContext: Eastern court courtesy: deep bow of respect (*proskynēsis*) to civic hosts.
