translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi Yitzchaq ben-arba'im shanah be-qachto eth-Rivqah bath-Bethu'el ha-Arammi mi-Paddan Aram achoth Lavan ha-Arammi le-lo le-ishah*: *Paddan Aram* ('Plain of Aram' / Haran).
historicalTrivia: Hosea 12:12 references this region: 'Jacob fled to the land of Aram; there Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he guarded sheep'.

dominicalIntent: And Isaac prayed to the Lord for his wife, because she was barren. And the Lord granted his prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceived (*Vayye'etar Yitzchaq le-YHVH le-nokhach ishto ki aqarah hi vayye'ather lo YHVH vatthar Rivqah ishto*). ISAAC'S INTERCESSION FOR BARREN REBEKAH! Rebekah is barren for 20 years (Isaac 40 at marriage, 60 at twins' birth!). Isaac enters intensive intercessory prayer (*Vayye'etar* = pleaded intensely) face-to-face with his wife (*le-nokhach ishto*). God hears Isaac's prayer and opens Rebekah's womb! Holy spouses pray together for God's gift of children.
cccReferences: CCC 2374 (The trial of involuntary childlessness overcome through intense prayer); CCC 2571 (Isaac's intercession for Rebekah); CCC 2634; Gen 11:30; Gen 29:31.
historicalContext: 20 years of childlessness (c. 1856-1836 BC) testing their faith before Isaac's persistent prayer is granted.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayye'etar Yitzchaq le-YHVH le-nokhach ishto ki aqarah hi vayye'ather lo YHVH vatthar Rivqah ishto*: *Vayye'etar* (pleaded / offered burning incense-like prayer, root *atar*). *Le-nokhach* ('opposite/facing her').
historicalTrivia: The Hebrew verb *atar* (to entreat/plead) literally means to burn incense, describing Isaac's prayer as a sweet-smelling rising incense before Yahweh.

dominicalIntent: The children struggled together within her, and she said: 'If it is thus, why is this happening to me?' So she went to inquire of the Lord (*Vattellech li-drosh eth-YHVH*). THE PRE-NATAL STRUGGLE! The twins struggle violently (*yithrotzetzu*) within Rebekah's womb. Distressed, Rebekah goes **TO INQUIRE OF THE LORD** (*li-drosh eth-YHVH*). Rebekah models turning to God in prayer whenever interior trials confuse us.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Rebekah inquiring of the Lord in prayer); CCC 2697 (Seeking God's oracle in trial); Rom 9:10-12.
historicalContext: Inquiring of Yahweh (*li-drosh*) through an authoritative prophet (likely Melchizedek or Abraham, who was still living!).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyithrotzetzu ha-banim be-qirbah vatyo'mer im-ken lammah zeh anochi vattellech li-drosh eth-YHVH*: *Vayyithrotzetzu* (crushed/struggled/collided against each other, Hithpael of *ratzatz*). *Li-drosh* (to seek/inquire of an oracle).
historicalTrivia: Romans 9:10-12 cites this exact womb struggle to demonstrate divine election before either child had done good or evil.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord said to her: 'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you shall be divided; the one shall be stronger than the other, the elder shall serve the younger' (*ve-rav ya'avod tza'ir*). THE SUPREME ORACLE OF DIVINE ELECTION! God reveals: **'THE ELDER SHALL SERVE THE YOUNGER!'** (*ve-rav ya'avod tza'ir*). St. Paul in Romans 9:10-13 quotes this oracle to prove that God's election is entirely gratuitous, based on grace rather than birth order or natural merit! Jacob represents the chosen Church; Esau represents the rejected flesh.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (Divine election of Jacob over Esau); CCC 2571; Rom 9:10-13; Mal 1:2-3; Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: Divine prophetic oracle reversing traditional ANE primogeniture rights.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer YHVH lah Sheny goyim be-vitnekha u-sheny le'ummim mi-me'ayikh yipparedu... ve-rav ya'avod tza'ir*: *ve-rav ya'avod tza'ir* ('and the greater/older shall serve the lesser/younger').
historicalTrivia: Romans 9:11-12 commentary: 'In order that God's purpose of election might continue, not because of works but because of his call, she was told, "The elder shall serve the younger".'

dominicalIntent: When her days to give birth were completed, behold, there were twins in her womb (*ve-hinneh thomim be-vitnah*). Birth of the twin brothers, marking the start of two distinct national lineages (Israel and Edom).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Birth of the twin brothers).
historicalContext: Twin birth (*thomim*) in the Negev encampment.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyimle'u yameyha la-ledeth ve-hinneh thomim be-vitnah*: *thomim* (twins).
historicalTrivia: This is the first of two twin births recorded in Genesis (the second being Perez and Zerah to Tamar in Gen 38:27).

dominicalIntent: The first came out red, all his body like a hairy cloak; so they called his name Esau (*Vayyetze ha-ri'shon admoni kullo ke-adareth se'ar vayyiqre'u shemo Esav*). BIRTH OF ESAU! The firstborn comes out **RED** (*admoni*) and **HAIRY** (*ke-adareth se'ar*). They name him **Esau** (*Esav* = 'Hairy / Rough'). His reddish color also gives him the title **Edom** (*Edom* = 'Red'), father of the Edomites.
historicalContext: Physical traits giving rise to the names Esau (Hairy), Seir (Hairy mountain), and Edom (Red).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyetze ha-ri'shon admoni kullo ke-adareth se'ar vayyiqre'u shemo Esav*: *admoni* (reddish/ruddy). *Adareth se'ar* (hairy cloak/garment). *Esav* (rough/hairy).
historicalTrivia: 1 Samuel 16:12 uses the same word *admoni* ('ruddy/reddish') to describe young David, but while David's ruddiness marked royal beauty, Esau's marked wild carnality.

dominicalIntent: Afterward his brother came out with his hand holding Esau's heel; so his name was called Jacob (*Vayyiqra shemo Ya'aqov*). Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them. BIRTH OF JACOB! The second twin comes out grasping Esau's heel (*ahev*), so he is named **Jacob** (*Ya'aqov* = 'Heel-grasper' / 'Supplanter'). Grasping the heel symbolizes Jacob's destiny to supplant the flesh and inherit the covenant. Isaac is 60 years old at their birth.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (The divine election of Jacob); CCC 2571; Hos 12:3; Rom 9:13.
historicalContext: Isaac is 60 years old (1836 BC); Abraham is 160 years old (living another 15 years!).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-acharey-khen yatza achiv ve-yado ochezerh be-aqev Esav vayyiqra shemo Ya'aqov ve-Yitzchaq ben-shesim shanah be-ledeth othah*: *Ya'aqov* (from *aqev* = heel -> 'he grasps the heel / supplants').
historicalTrivia: Hosea 12:3 references this moment: 'In the womb he took his brother by the heel (*aqav*), and in his manhood he strove with God'.

dominicalIntent: When the boys grew up, Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents (*ve-Ya'aqov ish tam yoshev ohalim*). CONTRAST OF CHARACTERS! Esau is a wild, carnally-minded hunter of the field; Jacob is a quiet, blameless man (*ish tam*) dwelling in tents (*yoshev ohalim*). *Tam* ('blameless/wholesome') is the exact word used for Noah (Gen 6:9) and Job (Job 1:1)!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The contrasting spiritual temperaments of Esau and Jacob); Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: Nomadic shepherd lifestyle (*yoshev ohalim*) vs wild game hunting (*ish tzayid*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyigdlu ha-ne'arim vayehi Esav ish yode'a tzayid ish sadeh ve-Ya'aqov ish tam yoshev ohalim*: *tam* (quiet/blameless/wholesome, root *tamam*).
historicalTrivia: The word *tam* used for Jacob (*ish tam*) is translated in the LXX as *aplastos* ('guileless/unmolded'), prefiguring Jesus describing Nathanael: 'An Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!' (John 1:47).

dominicalIntent: Isaac loved Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah loved Jacob (*ve-Rivqah oheveth eth-Ya'aqov*). PARENTAL FAVORITISM! Isaac favors Esau because of his palate (tasting wild game), whereas Rebekah loves Jacob because she remembered God's prophecy ('the elder shall serve the younger', v. 23). Family division arises when natural taste overrides divine revelation.
cccReferences: CCC 2214 (Parental duties and avoiding destructive favoritism); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Domestic tension between Isaac's natural preference for Esau's game and Rebekah's alignment with divine prophecy.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vavye'ehav Yitzchaq eth-Esav ki-tzayid be-phiv ve-Rivqah oheveth eth-Ya'aqov*: *ki-tzayid be-phiv* ('for game was in his mouth').
historicalTrivia: Rebekah's preference for Jacob was not mere personal bias, but spiritual fidelity to the divine oracle of v. 23.

dominicalIntent: Once when Jacob was cooking stew, Esau came in from the field, and he was exhausted (*ve-hu ayeph*). Setting the stage for the sale of the birthright: Jacob cooking a red lentil stew (*nezid adashim*), Esau returning famished.
historicalContext: Red lentil stew (*nezid adashim*) cooked over a campfire.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyazed Ya'aqov nazid vayyavo Esav min-ha-sadeh ve-hu ayeph*: *nazid* (boiled stew/soup). *Ayeph* (faint/exhausted).
historicalTrivia: Red lentils (*adashim*) are still a staple crop across the Levant, yielding a thick reddish-brown stew.

dominicalIntent: And Esau said to Jacob: 'Let me gulp down some of that red stuff, for I am exhausted!' (Therefore his name was called Edom). ESAU'S CARNAL DEMAND! Esau demands to gulp down (*hal'itheni-na*) 'that red red stuff' (*ha-adom ha-adom ha-zeh*). His obsession with immediate physical appetite earns him the nickname **Edom** (*Edom* = 'Red'). Carnal desire blinds the soul to eternal treasures.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Carnal gluttony sacrificing spiritual inheritance); CCC 1866 (Gluttony as a capital sin); Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: Coarse, impatient demand using the crude verb *hal'itheni* ('stuff into my mouth / gulp down').
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Esav el-Ya'aqov Hal'itheni-na min-ha-adom ha-adom ha-zeh ki ayeph anochi al-ken qara-shemo Edom*: *Hal'itheni* (cause me to gulp down - used for feeding animals!). *Ha-adom ha-adom* ('this red red stuff').
historicalTrivia: Philippians 3:19 describes Esau's mindset: 'Their god is their belly, and they glory in their shame, with minds set on earthly things'.

dominicalIntent: Jacob said: 'Sell me your birthright now' (*Mikhrah k-ayom eth-bechorathkha li*). JACOB STRIPES FOR THE BIRTHRIGHT! Jacob seizes the opportunity to buy the **birthright** (*bechorah*). The birthright carried double land inheritance and, supremely, the spiritual priesthood of the family to transmit the Messianic Covenant!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Jacob prizing the spiritual birthright); Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: The primogeniture birthright (*bechorah*) conferred headship of the clan, double inheritance portion (Deut 21:17), and patriarchal priesthood.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Ya'aqov Mikhrah k-ayom eth-bechorathkha li*: *bechorathkha* (your birthright / right of the firstborn).
historicalTrivia: Under patriarchal custom before the Levites were set apart at Sinai, the firstborn son held the sacred family priesthood to offer sacrifices at the altar.

dominicalIntent: Esau said: 'I am about to die; of what use is a birthright to me?' (*Ve-lammah-zeh li bechorah*). CARNAL DESPISING OF SACRED THINGS! Esau exaggerates his hunger ('I am about to die!') and dismisses his sacred birthright as worthless! Esau represents the profane, unspiritual man who trades eternal salvation for fleeting worldly pleasure.
cccReferences: CCC 1866 (Gluttony and profanity); CCC 2571; Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: Drama of a profane man surrendering eternal covenant rights for one meal.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Esav Hinneh anochi holech la-muth ve-lammah-zeh li bechorah*: *holech la-muth* ('going to die').
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 12:16 warns all Christians using Esau as the premier archetype: 'that no one be ungodly like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal (*brōseōs mias*)'.

dominicalIntent: Jacob said: 'Swear to me now.' So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob (*Vayyishava lo vayyimkor eth-bechoratho le-Ya'aqov*). THE RATIFIED SALE! Jacob demands a binding oath. Esau swears the oath and legally transfers his birthright to Jacob. Jacob becomes the legitimate legal owner of the birthright.
cccReferences: CCC 2101 (Solemnity of binding oaths); CCC 2571; Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: Oaths sworn over food sales were legally binding under ANE custom (e.g., Nuzi tablets record a brother trading an orchard for three sheep).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Ya'aqov Hisshava li k-ayom vayyishava lo vayyimkor eth-bechoratho le-Ya'aqov*: *vayyimkor* (and he sold/alienated).
historicalTrivia: Nuzi tablet NEN 5:29 records a legal land sale between brothers: 'Tupkitilla transferred his inheritance share to his brother Kurpazah for three sheep', confirming Genesis 25:33.

dominicalIntent: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew, and he ate and drank and rose and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright (*Vayyiz Esav eth-ha-bechorah*). THE FINAL DIVINE VERDICT: ESAU DESPRISED HIS BIRTHRIGHT! Esau eats, drinks, gets up, and walks away without a second thought. The Holy Spirit delivers the indictment: **'Thus Esau DESPISED (*Vayyiz*) his birthright!'** Selling eternal glory for a bowl of pottage is the ultimate tragedy of the carnal soul.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The tragedy of despising spiritual gifts); CCC 1866; Heb 12:16-17; Mal 1:2-3.
historicalContext: The verb *vav-yigz / vayyiz* ('despised/disdained') marks total moral contempt for holy things.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Ya'aqov nathan le-Esav lechem u-nezid adashim vayyo'khal vayyesht vayyaqam vayyelech vayyiz Esav eth-ha-bechorah*: *Vayyiz* (and he despised / treated with contempt, root *bazah*).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 12:17 records the tragic conclusion: 'For you know that afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no chance to repent, though he sought it with tears'.

dominicalIntent: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Gerar to Abimelech king of the Philistines. A second famine tests the patriarch! Like Abraham (Gen 12:10), Isaac faces a severe famine. Isaac travels to Gerar in the western Negev foothills.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Testing of Isaac through famine); CCC 145.
historicalContext: Gerar under King Abimelech II (royal dynastic title for Philistine rulers of Gerar).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ra'av ba-aretz mi-llechadh ha-ra'av ha-ri'shon asher hayah bi-ymey Avraham vayyelech Yitzchaq el-Avimelech melech-Pelishtim Gherarah*.
historicalTrivia: This second famine is explicitly distinguished from Abraham's famine in Gen 12:10, highlighting repeating historical cycles.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord appeared to him and said: 'Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land of which I shall tell you' (*Al-thered Mitzraymah shekhon ba-aretz asher omar eleykha*). GOD FORBIDS EGYPT! Unlike Abraham who went down to Egypt in famine (Gen 12:10), God commands Isaac: 'DO NOT GO DOWN TO EGYPT!' Isaac must remain in the Promised Land, trusting in divine providence.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Isaac commanded to remain in Canaan); CCC 1817 (Trust in divine providence).
historicalContext: Divine command restricting Isaac to the Promised Land during a regional agricultural crisis.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyera elav YHVH vayyo'mer Al-thered Mitzraymah shekhon ba-aretz asher omar eleykha*: *Al-thered* ('Do not descend!').
historicalTrivia: Isaac is the only patriarch (unlike Abraham, Jacob, or Joseph) who NEVER stepped foot outside the Promised Land during his entire life.

dominicalIntent: 'Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and will bless you, for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father' (*ve-haqimothi eth-ha-sshevu'ah asher nishba'ti le-Avraham avikha*). THE ABRAHAMIC OATH COVENANT CONFIRMED TO ISAAC! God ratifies the sworn Oath Covenant of Moriah (Gen 22:16-18) directly with Isaac!
cccReferences: CCC 60 (The Oath Covenant confirmed to Isaac); CCC 2571; Heb 6:13-18; Luke 1:73.
historicalContext: Formal covenant renewal conferring full patriarchal land rights upon Isaac.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Gur ba-aretz ha-zoth ve-ehyeh immakha va-avarkhekha ki-lekha u-le-zar'akha ethen eth-kol-ha-aratzoth ha-el ve-haqimothi eth-ha-sshevu'ah...*: *ha-sshevu'ah* (the sworn oath).
historicalTrivia: Luke 1:73 in Zechariah's *Benedictus* quotes Genesis 26:3: 'the oath which he swore to our father Abraham'.

dominicalIntent: 'I will multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and will give to your offspring all these lands. And in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.' MESSIANIC BLESSING REAFFIRMED! The universal blessing through the Seed (*zar'akha* = Jesus Christ) is pledged to Isaac's offspring.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (Universal blessing through Christ, Isaac's seed); Gal 3:16.
historicalContext: Re-issuing the cosmic star-multitude and Gentile blessing promises.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hirbeythi eth-zar'akha ke-kokhavey ha-shamayim ve-nathatti le-zar'akha eth kol-ha-aratzoth ha-el ve-hithbarakhu ve-zar'akha kol goyey ha-aretz*.
historicalTrivia: Galatians 3:16 applies *zar'akha* ('your seed') to Christ as the ultimate fulfillment of Genesis 26:4.

dominicalIntent: '...because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws' (*eqev asher-shama Avraham be-qoli vayyishmor mishmarti mitzvothai chuqqothai ve-thorothai*). ABRAHAM'S TOTAL LAW FULFILLMENT! God declares that Abraham kept His **charge (*mishmereth*), commandments (*mitzvoth*), statutes (*chuqqoth*), and laws (*thoroth*)**! Long before Sinai, Abraham lived the spiritual reality of the Law through faith working in love (Gal 5:6).
cccReferences: CCC 145 (Abraham's total obedience of faith); CCC 2052 (Prefiguration of the Commandments); Gal 5:6; Jas 2:22.
historicalContext: Fourfold technical classification of divine law (*mishmarti, mitzvothai, chuqqothai, thorothai*) applied retroactively to Abraham.
translationNuances: Hebrew *eqev asher-shama Avraham be-qoli vayyishmor mishmarti mitzvothai chuqqothai ve-thorothai*: *thorothai* (my instructions/laws, plural of *Torah*!).
historicalTrivia: This is the FIRST MENTION of *Thoroth* (Laws/Instructions) in the Bible, establishing that Abraham lived the fullness of divine law.

dominicalIntent: So Isaac settled in Gerar (*Vayyeshev Yitzchaq be-Gherar*). Isaac obeys God's command, remaining in Gerar.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Isaac's obedience).
historicalContext: Settling in the western Negev foothills.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyeshev Yitzchaq be-Gherar*.
historicalTrivia: Gerar provided rich grain fields suitable for agricultural cultivation.

dominicalIntent: When the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said, 'She is my sister,' for he feared to say, 'My wife,' thinking, 'lest the men of the place should kill me because of Rebekah, because she was attractive in appearance.' Human frailty recurs! Isaac repeats Abraham's fear-driven half-truth, calling Rebekah his sister. Faith is a lifelong growth process.
cccReferences: CCC 1854 (Repeated human weakness); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Fear of host city violence against a wealthy foreign husband.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyish'alu anshey ha-maqom le-ishto vayyo'mer achothi hi ki yare le-emor ishti pen-yaharghuni anshey ha-maqom al-Rivqah ki-thovath mar'eh hi*.
historicalTrivia: Proverbs 29:25 ('The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the Lord is safe') is illustrated by Isaac's lapse.

dominicalIntent: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window and saw Isaac fondling Rebekah his wife (*metzacheq eth Rivqah ishto*). ABIMELECH DISCOVERS THE TRUTH! Abimelech looks out a window and sees Isaac caressing/fondling (*metzacheq*) Rebekah! The playful marital affection (*metzacheq*, same root as Isaac!) exposes that Rebekah is his wife.
cccReferences: CCC 1601 (Marital intimacy and affection); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Private palace courtyard observation through a high latticed window.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ki-arakhu-lo sham ha-yamim vayyashqeph Avimelech... vayyar ve-hinneh YITZCHAQ metzacheq eth Rivqah ishto*: *metzacheq* (playing affectionately with / laughing with, root *tzachaq* -> *Yitzchaq*!).
historicalTrivia: The word *metzacheq* is a wordplay on Isaac's own name (*Yitzchaq*): Isaac was 'Isaacing' (expressing joyful marital love) with Rebekah!

dominicalIntent: So Abimelech called Isaac and said: 'Behold, she is indeed your wife! How could you say, "She is my sister"?' Isaac said to him: 'Because I thought, "Lest I die because of her."' Abimelech rebukes Isaac for deception.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Reproof of deception by a secular ruler); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Royal interrogation of Isaac.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra Avimelech le-Yitzchaq vayyo'mer ach hinneh ishtekha hi ve-eykh amartha achothi hi...*.
historicalTrivia: Abimelech's prompt correction shows that Philistine law strictly forbade adultery.

dominicalIntent: Abimelech said: 'What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.' Abimelech emphasizes the community guilt (*asham*) that adultery brings upon a whole nation.
cccReferences: CCC 2380 (Adultery as a sin polluting society); CCC 1867.
historicalContext: ANE legal concept of communal guilt (*asham*) incurred by violation of marriage law.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avimelech mah-zoth asitha lanu ki-m'at shakhav achad ha-am eth-ishtekha ve-hevetha aleynu asham*: *asham* (guilt/guilt offering).
historicalTrivia: The word *asham* used here is the exact Leviticus term for a 'guilt offering', showing that adultery required ritual atonement.

dominicalIntent: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying: 'Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death' (*Moth yumath*). ROYAL DECREE OF PROTECTION! Abimelech issues an absolute royal decree threatening death (*Moth yumath*) to anyone who harms Isaac or Rebekah. God uses a pagan king to shield His covenant heir.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Divine protection through secular authority); CCC 1900; Ps 105:15.
historicalContext: Royal edict granting diplomatic immunity and capital protection.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vaytzav Avimelech eth-kol-ha-am le'mor ha-noge'a ba-ish ha-zeh u-ve-ishto moth yumath*: *moth yumath* (dying he shall die / capital punishment).
crossReferences: Psalm 105:15; Genesis 20:15; Exodus 19:12; Touch not my anointed ones.
historicalTrivia: Psalm 105:14-15 commentary: 'He allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their account, saying, "Touch not my anointed ones!"'.

dominicalIntent: And Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in the same year a hundredfold (*me'ah she'arim*). The Lord blessed him. THE HUNDREDFOLD HARVEST! Isaac becomes an agricultural farmer in Gerar, and Yahweh blesses him with a **HUNDREDFOLD HARVEST (*me'ah she'arim*)** in a single year during a famine! Jesus uses this exact figure in the Parable of the Sower: 'some a hundredfold (*hekaton*)' (Matt 13:8)!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The hundredfold blessing of God during famine); CCC 305; Matt 13:8; Mark 4:8.
historicalContext: 100-fold crop yield (*me'ah she'arim*) was an extraordinary miraculous yield (average Levantine yield was 10-fold to 15-fold).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyizra Yitzchaq ba-aretz ha-hi vayyimtza ba-shanah ha-hi me'ah she'arim vayvarakhehu YHVH*: *me'ah she'arim* (a hundred measures / hundredfold).
historicalTrivia: Mea Shearim ('Hundred Gates / Hundredfold'), one of the oldest Jewish neighborhoods outside the Old City of Jerusalem (built 1874), was named after Genesis 26:12.

dominicalIntent: The man became rich, and gained more and more until he became very wealthy (*vayyigdal ha-ish vayyelech halokh ve-gadel ad ki-gadal me'od*). Isaac's prosperity grows continually under divine favor.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Providential growth).
historicalContext: Accumulation of immense pastoral and agricultural wealth.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyigdal ha-ish vayyelech halokh ve-gadel ad ki-gadal me'od*: triple repetition of *gadal* (grew, kept growing, became exceedingly great!).
historicalTrivia: The intensive Hebrew construction *halokh ve-gadel* ('went on growing bigger and bigger') conveys exponential economic growth.

dominicalIntent: He had possessions of flocks and herds and a great household, so that the Philistines envied him (*vayqan'u otho Pelishtim*). ENVY OF THE WORLD! Isaac's vast wealth triggers envy (*vayqan'u*) among the Philistines. Worldly envy often targets the blessed children of God.
cccReferences: CCC 2538 (Envy as a capital sin destroying peace); CCC 2539; Gen 37:11.
historicalContext: Envy (*qin'ah*) arising between native inhabitants and wealthy resident patriarchs.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi-lo miqneh-tzon u-miqneh vaqar va-avuddah rabbah vayqan'u otho Pelishtim*: *qin'ah* (envy/jealousy).
historicalTrivia: CCC 2539 notes that envy represents a refusal of charity, generating hatred, detraction, and hostility toward neighbors.

dominicalIntent: (Now the Philistines had stopped and filled with earth all the wells that his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father.) SABOTAGE OF WELLS! The Philistines maliciously fill Abraham's wells with dirt. Stopping a well in the desert was an act of economic warfare intended to drive Isaac out.
cccReferences: CCC 2417 (Malicious destruction of property and resources); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Filling desert wells with rocks and dirt to destroy pastoral infrastructure.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-khol-ha-be'eroth asher chapharu avdey aviv bi-ymey Avraham aviv sithmum Pelishtim vaymalle'um afar*: *sithmum* (stopped/plugged them up).
historicalTrivia: 2 Kings 3:19 records stopping wells (*kol-ma'yan-mayim tistom*) as a scorched-earth military tactic used against Moab.

dominicalIntent: And Abimelech said to Isaac: 'Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we' (*Lech me-immanu ki-atzamta mimmennu me'od*). EXPULSION FROM GERAR! Abimelech requests Isaac's departure because Isaac's clan has become more powerful (*atzamta*) than the Philistine state itself!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The growing power of the covenant family); Exod 1:9.
historicalContext: State policy requesting peaceful relocation of a powerful foreign clan.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Avimelech el-Yitzchaq Lech me-immanu ki-atzamta mimmennu me'od*: *atzamta* (you have become mighty/numerous).
historicalTrivia: Exodus 1:9 echoes Abimelech's fear when Pharaoh says of Israel: 'Behold, the people of Israel are too many and too mighty for us (*atzum mimmennu*)'.

dominicalIntent: So Isaac departed from there and encamped in the Valley of Gerar and dwelt there (*vayyichan be-nachal Gherar vayyeshev sham*). PEACEMAKING DEPARTURE! Isaac peacefully yields without conflict, moving to the Valley of Gerar (*Nachal Gherar*). Isaac models Christ's Beatitude: 'Blessed are the peacemakers' (Matt 5:9).
cccReferences: CCC 2305 (Seeking peace over conflict); CCC 2571; Matt 5:9; Rom 12:18.
historicalContext: Relocating from Gerar city to the rural wadi valley (*nachal*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyelech misham Yitzchaq vayyichan be-nachal Gherar vayyeshev sham*: *nachal* (seasonal wadi/river valley).
historicalTrivia: 1 Corinthians 6:7 ('Why not rather suffer wrong? Why not rather be defrauded?') reflects Isaac's peaceful retreat.

dominicalIntent: And Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped after the death of Abraham. And he gave them the names that his father had given them. DIGGING AGAIN THE WELLS OF THE FATHERS! Isaac re-opens the ancient wells of Abraham and restores their original names. In spiritual theology, **re-digging the wells of our fathers** means returning to sacred Tradition, ancient orthodoxy, and the original springs of apostolic faith!
cccReferences: CCC 78 (Preserving Sacred Tradition and re-digging apostolic wells); CCC 84; CCC 2571; Jer 6:16.
historicalContext: Clearing debris from clogged Middle Bronze Age wells to restore water access.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyashav Yitzchaq vayyachpor eth-be'eroth ha-mayim... vayyiqra lahen shemoth ka-shemoth asher-qara lahen aviv*: *Vayyashav vayyachpor* ('And he returned and redug').
historicalTrivia: Jeremiah 6:16 echoes Isaac's work: 'Stand by the roads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is; and walk in it'.

dominicalIntent: But when Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of spring water (*be'er mayim chayyim*). SPRING OF LIVING WATER! Isaac's servants discover **A WELL OF LIVING WATER** (*be'er mayim chayyim* = spring of fresh running water). This is the FIRST APPEARANCE OF THE EXACT PHRASE 'LIVING WATER' (*mayim chayyim*) IN SCRIPTURE! Living Water prefigures the Holy Spirit poured out by Christ (John 4:10-14; John 7:37-39)!
cccReferences: CCC 698 (Living Water as the biblical symbol of the Holy Spirit); CCC 2571; John 4:10-14; John 7:37-39; Rev 21:6.
historicalContext: Artesian spring (*mayim chayyim* = bubbling fresh groundwater) as opposed to stagnant cistern water.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyachporu avdey-Yitzchaq ba-nachal vayyimtze'u-sham be'er mayim chayyim*: *mayim chayyim* ('living / running water'). LXX *hydatos zōntos*.
historicalTrivia: Jeremiah 2:13 contrasts God as the 'fountain of living waters' (*meqor mayim chayyim*) with broken cisterns.

dominicalIntent: The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying: 'The water is ours.' So he called the name of the well Esek (*Eseq*), because they contended with him. WELL 1: ESEK (*Contention*). Isaac names the well **Esek** (*Eseq* = 'Contention / Dispute'). Rather than fighting back, Isaac surrenders the well and moves on.
cccReferences: CCC 2305 (Surrendering rights for the sake of peace); CCC 2571; Matt 5:39.
historicalContext: Pastoral water dispute in the Valley of Gerar.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyarivu ro'ey Gherar im-ro'ey Yitzchaq le'mor lanu ha-mayim vayyiqra shem-ha-be'er Eseq ki hith'assequ immo*: *Eseq* (Contention/Dispute, root *asaq*).
historicalTrivia: Matthew 5:39 ('If any one strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also') reflects Isaac's non-violent response.

dominicalIntent: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that also; so he called its name Sitnah (*Sitnah*). WELL 2: SITNAH (*Hostility / Accusation*). Isaac digs a second well, but they quarrel over it too; he names it **Sitnah** (*Sitnah* = 'Hostility / Enmity / Satanic Accusation', from root *satan*!). Again, Isaac peacefully retreats.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Overcoming hostility through peaceful non-resistance); CCC 2851 (Satan as the Accuser).
historicalContext: Second water dispute in the wadi.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyachporu be'er achereth vayyarivu gam-aleha vayyiqra shemah Sitnah*: *Sitnah* (Enmity/Accusation, same root as *Satan* / Accuser!).
historicalTrivia: The noun *Sitnah* derives from *satan* (adversary/accuser), marking the second well as a site of spiritual opposition.

dominicalIntent: And he moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. So he called its name Rehoboth (*Rechovoth*), saying: 'For now the Lord has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land' (*Ki-attah hirchiv YHVH lanu u-pharinu va-aretz*). WELL 3: REHOBOTH (*Broad Places / Room*). Isaac moves a third time and digs a well with NO DISPUTE! He names it **Rehoboth** (*Rechovoth* = 'Broad Room / Open Spaces'), declaring: 'NOW THE LORD HAS MADE ROOM FOR US!' Patient non-resistance yields divine expansion and fruitful peace.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Patient meekness rewarded with room and fruitfulness); CCC 1716 (The Beatitude of Meekness: 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth'); Matt 5:5; Ps 18:19.
historicalContext: Rehoboth (Ruheibeh, 19 miles southwest of Beersheba) where ample water was found without Philistine conflict.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavtheq misham vayyachpor be'er achereth ve-lo rarivu aleha vayyiqra shemah Rechovoth vayyo'mer ki-attah hirchiv YHVH lanu u-pharinu va-aretz*: *hirchiv* (has broadened / made room, root *rachav* -> *Rechovoth*).
historicalTrivia: Psalm 18:19 ('He brought me out into a broad place (*la-merchav*)') echoes Isaac's declaration at Rehoboth.

dominicalIntent: From there he went up to Beersheba (*Vayya'al misham Be'er Sheva*). Isaac ascends to the sacred sanctuary of **Beersheba**, returning to the holy ground where Abraham built an altar (Gen 21:33).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Ascending to the sanctuary of Beersheba); Gen 21:33.
historicalContext: Ascending from the Negev wadi basin up to the Beersheba plateau.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'al misham Be'er Sheva*.
historicalTrivia: Beersheba remains the central covenant sanctuary in the Negev for Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Elijah.

dominicalIntent: And the Lord appeared to him that same night and said: 'I am the God of Abraham your father; fear not, for I am with you and will bless you and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham's sake' (*Al-thira ki-ittakha anochi va-verakhtikha...*). NIGHT THEOPHANY AT BEERSHEBA! Yahweh appears to Isaac that very night: 'FEAR NOT, FOR I AM WITH YOU!' (*Al-thira ki-ittakha anochi*). God rewards Isaac's peacemaking with divine presence and covenant reassurance.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Night theophany reassuring Isaac); CCC 212 ('Fear not, I am with you'); Isa 41:10; Matt 28:20.
historicalContext: Night vision (*ba-laylah ha-hu*) confirming the patriarchal covenant.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyera elav YHVH ba-laylah ha-hu vayyo'mer Anochi Elohey Avraham avikha al-thira ki-ittakha anochi va-verakhtikha ve-hirbeythi eth-zar'akha ba-avur Avraham avdi*: *Al-thira* ('Fear not!').
historicalTrivia: The command *Al-thira* ('Fear not!') occurs 365 times in Scripture—one 'Fear not' for every single day of the year!

dominicalIntent: So he built an altar there and called upon the name of the Lord and pitched his tent there. And there Isaac's servants dug a well (*Vayyiven sham mizbeach... vayyachporu-sham avdey-Yitzchaq be'er*). ALTAR, TENT, AND WELL! Isaac's three priorities: (1) **Altar** (*mizbeach*) for worship, (2) **Tent** (*ohel*) for family life, (3) **Well** (*be'er*) for daily water. Worship comes first!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Building the altar before digging the well: priority of divine worship); CCC 2096; CCC 1145.
historicalContext: Constructing a stone altar (*mizbeach*) at Beersheba alongside the residential camp.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiven sham mizbeach vayyiqra be-shem YHVH vayyet-sham oholo vayyachporu-sham avdey-Yitzchaq be'er*.
historicalTrivia: Isaac's three-fold sequence—Altar (Worship), Tent (Home), Well (Work)—establishes the ideal order of a holy life.

dominicalIntent: When Abimelech went to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army... THE WORLD COMES SUING FOR PEACE! Abimelech, his royal advisor Ahuzzath, and general Phicol travel to Beersheba to seek a peace treaty with Isaac. Those who walk in peaceful non-resistance eventually see their enemies come seeking reconciliation.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Peaceful meekness compelling enemies to seek peace); CCC 2305; Prov 16:7.
historicalContext: State delegation including the king, chief counselor (*Ahuzzath*), and military commander (*Phicol*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Avimelech halakh elav mi-Gherar va-Ahuzzath mere'ehu u-Phiikhol sar-tzeva'o*: *mere'ehu* (his friend/adviser).
historicalTrivia: Proverbs 16:7 ('When a man's ways please the Lord, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him') is fulfilled in Genesis 26:26.

dominicalIntent: Isaac said to them: 'Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me and have sent me away from you?' Isaac speaks with honest candor, confronting their past hostility.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Honesty in diplomatic relations); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Direct diplomatic inquiry into the delegation's true motives.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer alehem YITZCHAQ Mmaduath ba'them elai ve-athem sene'them othi vat-shallechu othi me-ithkhem*: *sene'them* (you hated me).
historicalTrivia: Isaac's question mirrors Jephthah's challenge to the elders of Gilead in Judges 11:7.

dominicalIntent: They said: 'We see plainly that the Lord has been with you (*Ra'o ra'inu ki-hayah YHVH immakh*); so we said, let there be a sworn pact between the two of us, between you and us, and let us make a covenant with you...' PAGAN TESTIMONY: 'WE SEE PLAINLY THAT YAHWEH IS WITH YOU!' (*Ra'o ra'inu*). Abimelech confesses that Yahweh's presence with Isaac is undeniable! The world is compelled to acknowledge God when believers walk in peace.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Pagan recognition of God's presence with Isaac); CCC 2044; 1 Cor 14:25.
historicalContext: Formal treaty proposal (*shevu'ah / berith*) between the Philistine state and Isaac's clan.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mru Ra'o ra'inu ki-hayah YHVH immakh...*: *Ra'o ra'inu* (infinitive absolute: 'Seeing we have clearly seen!').
historicalTrivia: 1 Corinthians 14:25 echoes v. 28: 'He will worship God and declare that God is really among you'.

dominicalIntent: '...that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you and have done to you nothing but good and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the Lord' (*Attah berukh YHVH*). THE TITLE: 'BLESSED OF THE LORD!' Abimelech concludes: **'YOU ARE NOW THE BLESSED OF THE LORD!'** (*Attah berukh YHVH*).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Pagan recognition of divine blessing); Luke 1:28.
historicalContext: Non-aggression treaty clause.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Im-ta'aseh immanu ra'ah ka-asher lo noga'nukha ve-kha-asher asinu immakha raq-tov... attah attah berukh YHVH*: *berukh YHVH* ('Blessed of Yahweh').
historicalTrivia: The title *berukh YHVH* ('Blessed of Yahweh') is the exact phrase used by Melchizedek for Abraham in Gen 14:19.

dominicalIntent: So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank (*Vayya'as lahem mishteh vayyo'khlu vayyishtthu*). THE COVENANT FEAST! Isaac prepares a celebratory banquet (*mishteh*). Shared table communion seals the international peace treaty.
cccReferences: CCC 2304 (Feast sealing a treaty of peace); CCC 1334; CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Covenant banquet (*mishteh*) ratifying non-aggression pacts.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as lahem mishteh vayyo'khlu vayyishtthu*: *mishteh* (banquet/feast).
historicalTrivia: Covenant meals in the Old Testament prefigure the Holy Eucharist as the ultimate Covenant Feast of Peace.

dominicalIntent: In the morning they rose early and took oath with one another. And Isaac sent them on their way, and they departed from him in peace (*vayyelechu me-itto be-shalom*). At early dawn, they swear mutual covenant oaths (*nishbe'u*) and depart in peace (*be-shalom*).
cccReferences: CCC 2101 (Solemnity of covenant oaths); CCC 2305.
historicalContext: Dawn oath-taking ceremony finalizing the treaty.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyasqimu ba-boqer vayyishave'u ish le-achiv vay-shallechem Yitzchaq vayyelechu me-itto be-shalom*: *be-shalom* ('in peace').
historicalTrivia: The departure *be-shalom* ('in peace') completes the resolution of the Philistine conflict.

dominicalIntent: That same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well that they had dug and said to him: 'We have found water' (*Matza'nu mayim*). DISCOVERY OF WATER ON THE DAY OF PEACE! On the selfsame day the peace treaty is sworn, Isaac's servants rush in declaring: 'WE HAVE FOUND WATER!' (*Matza'nu mayim*). God crowns peacemaking with abundant living water.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Divine confirmation of peace with water); CCC 698; Isa 12:3.
historicalContext: Striking a rich water aquifer on the day of treaty ratification.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ba-yom ha-hu vayyavo'u avdey Yitzchaq vayyaggidu lo al-odoth ha-be'er asher chapharu vayyo'mru lo Matza'nu mayim*: *Matza'nu mayim* ('We have found water!').
historicalTrivia: Isaiah 12:3 ('With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation') reflects the joy of *Matza'nu mayim* in Genesis 26:32.

dominicalIntent: He called it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day (*Al-ken shem-ha-ir Be'er Sheva ad ha-yom ha-zeh*). ISAAC RATIFIES BEERSHEBA! Isaac names the well **Shibah** (*Shiv'ah* = 'Oath / Seven'), re-confirming the name **Beersheba** (*Be'er Sheva*) established by his father Abraham (Gen 21:31).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Re-confirming the sacred sanctuary of Beersheba); Gen 21:31.
historicalContext: Re-naming the well and city *Be'er Sheva* ('Well of the Oath').
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiqra othah Shiv'ah al-ken shem-ha-ir Be'er Sheva ad ha-yom ha-zeh*: *Shiv'ah* (Oath / Seven).
historicalTrivia: Beersheba is the only holy site in Genesis whose naming is recorded twice: first by Abraham (Gen 21:31) and second by Isaac (Gen 26:33).

dominicalIntent: When Esau was forty years old, he took Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite to be his wife, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite. ESAU'S REBELLIOUS MARRIAGES! At 40 years old, Esau marries TWO PAGAN HITTITE WOMEN (Judith and Basemath). Defying Abraham's strict prohibition (Gen 24:3), Esau marries idolatrous Canaanites, proving again his reckless disregard for the covenant.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Esau's pagan marriages in defiance of the covenant); CCC 1633; Gen 24:3; Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: Polygamous intermarriage with local Anatolian/Hittite women.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi Esav ben-arba'im shanah vayyiqach ishah eth-Yehudith bath-Be'eri ha-Chitti ve-eth-Basmath bath-Eylon ha-Chitti*: *Yehudith* (Judith = 'Praised / Jewess'). *Basmath* (Basemath = 'Fragrant').
historicalTrivia: Esau's first wife Judith (*Yehudith*) is the earliest person in the Bible to bear the name *Judith* ('Praised').

dominicalIntent: And they made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah (*vattyheyrena morath ruach le-Yitzchaq u-le-Rivqah*). GRIEF TO THE HOLY PARENTS! Esau's pagan wives bring 'bitterness of spirit' (*morath ruach*) to Isaac and Rebekah. Idolatrous marriages bring grief and domestic fracture into covenant families.
cccReferences: CCC 2221 (Parental grief over children's spiritual rebellion); CCC 2571; Gen 27:46.
historicalContext: Pagan idolatrous practices brought into the patriarchal encampment causing constant friction.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattheyena morath ruach le-Yitzchaq u-le-Rivqah*: *morath ruach* ('bitterness of spirit', root *marar* = bitter + *ruach* = spirit).
historicalTrivia: Proverbs 17:25 directly reflects Genesis 26:35: 'A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness (*memer*) to her who bore him'.

dominicalIntent: When Isaac was old and his eyes were dim so that he could not see, he called Esau his oldest son and said to him, 'My son'; and he answered, 'Here I am.' Aging Isaac suffers physical blindness (*va-tikhkeyna eynav me-re'oth*). His physical blindness mirrors his spiritual misjudgment in seeking to bestow the patriarchal covenant blessing upon carnal Esau rather than Jacob, whom God chose before birth (Gen 25:23).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The trial of Isaac's aging and spiritual testing); CCC 60; Heb 11:20.
historicalContext: Isaac approx. 137 years old (Jacob and Esau 77 years old!). Isaac lived another 43 years (dying at 180, Gen 35:28).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ki-zaqen Yitzchaq vatikhkeyna eynav me-re'oth vayyiqra eth-Esav bno ha-gadol...*: *vatikhkeyna* (became dim/clouded/blind).
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:20 commentary: 'By faith Isaac invoked future blessings on Jacob and Esau', showing that God used Isaac's mistake to fulfill His sovereign plan.

dominicalIntent: He said: 'Behold, I am old; I do not know the day of my death.' Isaac acknowledges his mortality, seeking to settle the irrevocable patriarchal succession.
cccReferences: CCC 1010-1014 (Preparation for death); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Setting the solemn deathbed covenant blessing (*berakhah*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Hinneh-na zaqanti lo yadati yom mothi*.
historicalTrivia: Although Isaac believed his death was near at 137, God granted him another 43 years of life to see Jacob return from Haran with his 12 sons.

dominicalIntent: 'Now then, take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt game for me.' Isaac charges Esau to hunt wild game, conditioning the spiritual blessing upon physical food.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Isaac's natural preference for Esau's game); Gen 25:28.
historicalContext: Archery hunting in the Negev hills.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah ssa-na kheleydkha thalyakha ve-qashtekha ve-tze ha-sadeh ve-tzudah li tzayid*: *thalyakha* (quiver/gear).
historicalTrivia: Isaac conditioning the holy blessing on wild game (*tzayid*) underscores how natural appetites obscured his spiritual vision.

dominicalIntent: 'And prepare for me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me that I may eat, that my soul may bless you before I die' (*ba-avur tevarkhkha naphshi be-terem amuth*). THE COVENANT BLESSING FEAST! Isaac seeks a covenant meal (*tevarkhkha naphshi*) to impart the primary patriarchal blessing. The blessing is irrevocable once spoken.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The solemnity and irrevocability of the patriarchal blessing); Heb 11:20; Gen 27:33.
historicalContext: Sacramental banquet before imparting the testamentary patriarchal blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Va-aseh-li mat'ammim ka-asher ahavthi ve-havi'ah li ve-okhela ba-avur tevarkhkha naphshi be-terem amuth*: *mat'ammim* (savory delicacies).
historicalTrivia: In ancient Semitic law, a father's deathbed blessing (*berakhah*) spoken over a meal possessed legally binding, unalterable status.

dominicalIntent: Rebekah was listening when Isaac spoke to his son Esau. So when Esau went to the field to hunt for game and bring it... REBEKAH OVERHEARS! Rebekah remembers the divine oracle given to her by God before their birth: 'The elder shall serve the younger' (Gen 25:23). She acts to prevent Isaac from frustrating God's revealed will.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Rebekah acting to preserve God's divine oracle of election); Rom 9:10-12; Gen 25:23.
historicalContext: Rebekah listening at the tent flap, recognizing Isaac was about to subvert divine revelation.
translationNuances: Hebrew *U-Rivqah shoma'ath be-dabber Yitzchaq el-Esav bno vayyelech Esav ha-sadeh li-tzud tzayid le-havi*.
historicalTrivia: Rebekah's intervention was motivated by her 77-year fidelity to God's explicit word in Genesis 25:23.

dominicalIntent: Rebekah said to her son Jacob: 'Behold, I heard your father speak to your brother Esau...' Rebekah initiates the plan to secure the blessing for Jacob.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Rebekah initiating the intervention); Rom 9:10.
historicalContext: Private maternal counsel in the inner tent.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-Rivqah amrah el-Ya'aqov bnah le'mor hinneh shama'ti eth-avikha medabber el-Esav achikha le'mor*.
historicalTrivia: Rebekah addresses Jacob as 'my son', taking full personal responsibility for the plan.

dominicalIntent: '"Bring me game and prepare for me savory food, that I may eat it and bless you before the Lord before I die."' Rebekah notes that Isaac intended to bless Esau 'before the Lord' (*li-phney YHVH*), making it a binding covenant act.
historicalContext: Solemn invocation of Yahweh's presence (*li-phney YHVH*) in deathbed blessings.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Havi'ah li tzayid va-aseh-li mat'ammim ve-okhelah va-avarekhkha li-phney YHVH li-phney mothi*.
historicalTrivia: The phrase *li-phney YHVH* ('before the Lord') added by Rebekah highlights the sacral nature of the blessing.

dominicalIntent: 'Now therefore, my son, obey my voice as I command you' (*shema be-qoli le-asher ani me-tzavvah othakh*). MATERNAL MANDATE! Rebekah commands Jacob's obedience, taking full responsibility for the strategy to fulfill God's promise.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Rebekah commanding Jacob); CCC 2216 (Filial respect).
historicalContext: Maternal authority directing a son to secure divine inheritance.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah beni shema be-qoli le-asher ani me-tzavvah othakh*: *shema be-qoli* ('listen to / obey my voice').
historicalTrivia: Rebekah's command *shema be-qoli* uses the exact words God used to Abraham in Gen 21:12 ('listen to her voice').

dominicalIntent: 'Go to the flock and fetch me two good young goats, that I may prepare from them savory food for your father, such as he loves.' Rebekah substitutes two young goats (*sheny gedayei izzim*) for wild game, relying on her culinary skill to match Isaac's palate.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Domestic substitution of goat meat for wild game); CCC 1334.
historicalContext: Young kid goat meat cooked with spiced curds closely mimicked venison taste.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Lech-na el-ha-tzon ve-qach-li misham sheny gedayei izzim tovim ve-e'eseh otham mat'ammim le-avikha ka-asher ahav*.
historicalTrivia: Goat meat (*gedayei izzim*) prepared with wine, herbs, and clarified butter was widely used to imitate wild gazelle.

dominicalIntent: 'And you shall bring it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before he dies.' Jacob is to present the meal and receive the irrevocable patriarchal blessing.
historicalContext: Presenting the covenant feast to the patriarch.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-hevetha le-avikha ve-akhal ba-avur asher yevarekhkha li-phney motho*.
historicalTrivia: The urgency *li-phney motho* ('before his death') reflects the ancient fear of missing the deathbed blessing.

dominicalIntent: But Jacob said to Rebekah his mother: 'Behold, my brother Esau is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man' (*Esav achi ish sa'ir ve-anochi ish chalaq*). JACOB'S HESITATION AND FEAR OF DECEPTION! Jacob raises a physical objection: Esau is hairy (*sa'ir*), while Jacob is smooth-skinned (*chalaq*). Jacob fears being exposed as a deceiver and bringing a curse instead of a blessing.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Jacob's fear of deception and curse); CCC 2477; CCC 1854.
historicalContext: Contrast between Esau's dense body hair (*sa'ir*) and Jacob's smooth skin (*chalaq*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Ya'aqov el-Rivqah immo hen Esav achi ish sa'ir ve-anochi ish chalaq*: *sa'ir* (hairy/shaggy). *Chalaq* (smooth).
historicalTrivia: The word *sa'ir* (hairy) is also the root for *Seir* (Mount Seir), the hairy mountain region settled by Esau's descendants (Edom).

dominicalIntent: 'Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall seem to be mocking him and bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing' (*ve-hevethi alai qelalah ve-lo verakhah*). Jacob fears Isaac feeling his skin (*ye-mushsheni*) and perceiving him as a mocker (*metata'a*), which would incur a curse (*qelalah*).
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Fear of deception and bringing a curse); CCC 1854; Deut 27:18.
historicalContext: Tactile identification (*touch/feeling*) used by a blind patriarch to verify identity.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ulay ye-mushsheni avi ve-hayithi ve-eynav ke-mith'ata'a ve-hevethi alai qelalah ve-lo verakhah*: *ye-mushsheni* (shall feel/touch me). *Mith'ata'a* (mocker/deceiver/impostor).
historicalTrivia: Deuteronomy 27:18 pronounces a curse: 'Cursed be he who misleads a blind man on the road', which Jacob desperately feared.

dominicalIntent: His mother said to him: 'Upon me be your curse, my son; only obey my voice, and go, fetch them to me' (*Alai qilalathkha beni*). HEROIC MATERNAL SACRIFICE: 'UPON ME BE YOUR CURSE!' Rebekah utters heroic words: **'Upon me be your curse, my son!'** (*Alai qilalathkha beni*). She takes full spiritual responsibility and liability for the act. Rebekah prefigures Our Blessed Mother Mary, who willingly takes on sword-piercing sorrow and spiritual co-suffering for her children (Luke 2:35).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Rebekah taking the curse upon herself to fulfill God's promise); CCC 494 (Mary's co-suffering prefigured); Luke 2:35; Gal 3:13.
historicalContext: Solemn maternal pledge of vicarious substitution for any divine curse.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vatyo'mer lo immo Alai qilalathkha beni aq shema be-qoli ve-lech qach-li*: *Alai qilalathkha* ('Upon me be your curse!').
historicalTrivia: Galatians 3:13 ('Christ redeemed us from the curse... by becoming a curse for us') echoes Rebekah taking the curse upon herself for her son.

dominicalIntent: So he went and took them and brought them to his mother, and his mother prepared savory food, such as his father loved. Jacob submits to his mother's command. Rebekah prepares the savory meal.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Filial submission to maternal strategy); CCC 2216.
historicalContext: Preparing the substitute savory feast.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyelech vayyiqach vayyave le-immo vattha'as immo mat'ammim ka-asher ahav aviv*.
historicalTrivia: Rebekah's culinary mastery ensured the goat meat matched Isaac's exact preference.

dominicalIntent: Then Rebekah took the best garments of Esau her oldest son (*eth-bigdey Esav... ha-chamudoth*), which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son. CLOTHING JACOB IN THE FIRSTBORN'S GARMENTS! Rebekah clothes Jacob in **Esau's best garments** (*bigdey ha-chamudoth* = 'sacred priestly garments of desire'). In patriarchal tradition, these were the sacred priestly garments of the firstborn! This prefigures **Holy Baptism**, where the believer is clothed in the glorious robe of Jesus Christ, the true Firstborn (Gal 3:27; Rom 13:14)!
cccReferences: CCC 1243 (The white garment of Baptism prefigured by being clothed in the firstborn's robes); CCC 2571; Gal 3:27; Rom 13:14; Luke 15:22.
historicalContext: Sacred priestly robes (*bigdey ha-chamudoth*) of the primogeniture firstborn kept preserved in fragrant chests.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattiqach Rivqah eth-bigdey Esav bnah ha-gadol ha-chamudoth asher ittah ba-bayith vatthalbesh eth-Ya'aqov bnah ha-qatan*: *ha-chamudoth* (the coveted/precious/delightful ones). *Vatthalbesh* (and she clothed him).
historicalTrivia: Patristic commentary (St. Ambrose *De Jacob* 2.2): 'Jacob put on the garments of his elder brother Esau... as Christians put on the righteous garments of Christ to receive the Father's blessing'.

dominicalIntent: And the skins of the young goats she put on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck (*ve-eth oroth gedayei ha-izzim hilbishah al-yadav ve-al chelqath tzavvarav*). Rebekah covers Jacob's hands and smooth neck with goat skins (*oroth gedayei ha-izzim*) to deceive Isaac's tactile sense.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Tactile disguise using goat skins); CCC 2477.
historicalContext: Angora goat skins in the Levant possessed soft, dense, coarse hair mimicking human body hair.
translationNuances: Hebrew *ve-eth oroth gedayei ha-izzim hilbishah al-yadav ve-al chelqath tzavvarav*: *chelqath* (smooth part).
historicalTrivia: Syrian Angora goat hair was notoriously long and soft, remarkably resembling coarse human hair to a blind person's touch.

dominicalIntent: And she delivered the savory food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob. Rebekah hands the sacrificial meal to Jacob to present to Isaac.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Maternal presentation).
historicalContext: Handing over the completed meal for the deathbed blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vattitten eth-ha-mat'ammim ve-eth-ha-lechem asher asath be-yad Ya'aqov bnah*.
historicalTrivia: The meal consisted of both savory goat meat (*mat'ammim*) and fresh bread (*lechem*).

dominicalIntent: So he went in to his father and said: 'My father'; and he said: 'Here I am; who are you, my son?' Jacob enters Isaac's chamber. Isaac immediately inquires about his identity.
historicalContext: Entering the patriarch's private sleeping quarters.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyavo el-aviv vayyo'mer Avi vayyo'mer Hinneni mi attah beni*.
historicalTrivia: Isaac's instant question 'Who are you, my son?' reveals his underlying suspicion due to the unexpectedly rapid return.

dominicalIntent: Jacob said to his father: 'I am Esau your firstborn; I have done as you told me; now sit up and eat of my game, that your soul may bless me' (*Anochi Esav bekhorakha*). JACOB'S DECEPTIVE WORDS! Jacob states: 'I am Esau your firstborn' (*Anochi Esav bekhorakha*). While Jacob was legally the owner of the birthright by purchase (Gen 25:33), using Esau's personal name was a verbal untruth. St. Augustine explains that while the action mystically prefigured Christ's clothing of believers, Jacob's verbal deceit was a human flaw.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Verbal deception and truthfulness); CCC 2571; St. Augustine *Against Lying* 10.24.
historicalContext: Jacob claiming the identity of the firstborn to receive the patriarchal blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Ya'aqov el-aviv Anochi Esav bekhorakha asithi ka-asher dibbartah elai...*: *Anochi Esav bekhorakha* ('I am Esau your firstborn').
historicalTrivia: St. Augustine wrote (*City of God* 16.37): 'Jacob's statement "I am Esau your firstborn" is not a lie, but a mystery: for Jacob had legally acquired the firstborn rights'.

dominicalIntent: But Isaac said to his son: 'How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?' He answered: 'Because the Lord your God granted me success' (*Ki hiqrah YHVH Eloheykha le-phanay*). Isaac questions the rapid speed of the hunt. Jacob attributes the speed to Yahweh's providence (*hiqrah*), using the exact verb used by Abraham's steward in Gen 24:12.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Invoking God's name in deception); CCC 2571; Gen 24:12.
historicalContext: Rapid return (within 1 hour) provoking suspicious interrogation by Isaac.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Yitzchaq el-bno mah-zeh mihartha limtzo beni vayyo'mer Ki hiqrah YHVH Eloheykha le-phanay*: *hiqrah* (caused it to meet / granted success).
historicalTrivia: In invoking God's providence (*hi qrah YHVH*), Jacob used the exact word of Eliezer in Genesis 24:12.

dominicalIntent: Then Isaac said to Jacob: 'Come near, that I may feel you, my son, to know whether you are really my son Esau or not' (*Gesh-na ve-amushkha beni*). ISAAC'S TACTILE INSPECTION! Suspicious Isaac demands to feel (*amushkha*) Jacob. Physical touch is brought to bear to resolve the doubt.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Isaac testing identity by touch); John 20:27.
historicalContext: Blind patriarch requiring tactile confirmation before imparting the blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Yitzchaq el-Ya'aqov Gesh-na ve-amushkha beni ha-attah zeh beni Esav im-lo*: *ve-amushkha* (and that I may feel/touch you, root *mashash*).
historicalTrivia: Isaac demanding to feel Jacob (*amushkha*) prefigures Thomas touching Christ's wounds (John 20:27) and 1 John 1:1 ('which our hands have touched').

dominicalIntent: So Jacob went near to Isaac his father, who felt him and said: 'The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau' (*Ha-qol qol Ya'aqov ve-ha-yadayim yedey Esav*). 'THE VOICE IS JACOB'S VOICE, BUT THE HANDS ARE THE HANDS OF ESAU!' THIS IS ONE OF THE MOST FAMOUS CONTRASTS IN PATRISTIC EXEGESIS! Isaac perceives the truth through hearing, but is deceived by touch. Typologically, the Voice represents the Word of God (the Church's prayer), while the Hairy Hands represent the rough flesh of humanity assumed by Christ!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The voice of Jacob and hands of Esau as mystical type); St. Ambrose *De Jacob* 2.2; St. Augustine *City of God* 16.37.
historicalContext: Sensory conflict between auditory perception (*voice*) and tactile perception (*hairy hands*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiggash Ya'aqov el-Yitzchaq aviv vaymushshehu vayyo'mer Ha-qol qol Ya'aqov ve-ha-yadayim yedey Esav*: *Ha-qol qol Ya'aqov* ('The voice is the voice of Jacob').
crossReferences: Genesis 27:16; Song of Solomon 2:14; John 10:4; 1 John 1:1.
historicalTrivia: St. Ambrose wrote: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob (the Church praying), but the hands are the hands of Esau (Christ carrying our heavy flesh for our salvation)'.

dominicalIntent: And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau's hands; so he blessed him (*vayvarakhehu*). THE BLESSING IS IMPARTED! Isaac does not recognize him because of the hairy goat skins. Isaac prepares to impart the irrevocable blessing.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The bestowal of the patriarchal blessing); Heb 11:20.
historicalContext: Tactile confirmation overriding auditory doubt, leading to the blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-lo hikkiro ki-hayu yadav ki-ydey Esav achiv se'iroth vayvarakhehu*: *hikkiro* (recognized/discerned him).
historicalTrivia: The verb *vayvarakhehu* ('and he blessed him') marks the formal beginning of the blessing ceremony.

dominicalIntent: He said: 'Are you really my son Esau?' He answered: 'I am' (*Vayyo'mer Attah zeh beni Esav vayyo'mer Ani*). Isaac asks one final direct question; Jacob answers simply: 'I am' (*Ani*).
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Verbal deception); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Final verbal confirmation before eating the feast.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Attah zeh beni Esav vayyo'mer Ani*: *Ani* ('I am').
historicalTrivia: Jacob's one-word answer *Ani* ('I am') was his final verbal step of deception.

dominicalIntent: Then he said: 'Bring it near to me, that I may eat of my son's game and bless you.' So he brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank. THE COVENANT FEAST CONSUMMATED! Isaac eats the meat and drinks the wine brought by Jacob. Eating bread, meat, and wine seals the covenant blessing meal, prefiguring the Eucharistic Banquet.
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Bread and wine sealing the covenant blessing); CCC 2571; Gen 14:18; Gen 27:4.
historicalContext: Sacramental meal of bread, goat meat, and wine ratifying the testamentary blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Haggishah li ve-okhelah mi-tzeyd beni le-ma'an tevarkhkha naphshi vayyaggesh-lo vayyo'khal vayyave lo yayin vayyest*.
historicalTrivia: The addition of **wine** (*yayin*) in v. 25 links Isaac's blessing meal to Melchizedek's bread and wine (Gen 14:18) and the Last Supper.

dominicalIntent: Then his father Isaac said to him: 'Come near and kiss me, my son' (*Gesh-na u-shaqah-li beni*). THE KISS OF COVENANT LOVE! Isaac calls Jacob near to kiss him (*shaqah*). The holy kiss seals affection and allows Isaac to smell his garments.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The holy kiss sealing the blessing); CCC 2096; Rom 16:16.
historicalContext: Filial kiss of affection (*neshiqah*) preceding the formal blessing formula.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer elav Yitzchaq aviv Gesh-na u-shaqah-li beni*: *shaqah-li* ('kiss me').
historicalTrivia: The holy kiss (*philēma hagion*) in Romans 16:16 and the liturgical Kiss of Peace derive from patriarchal blessings like Genesis 27:26.

dominicalIntent: So he came near and kissed him. And Isaac smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him and said: 'See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field that the Lord has blessed!' (*Re'eh re'ach beni ke-re'ach sadeh asher berakho YHVH*). THE FRAGRANCE OF THE BLESSED FIELD! Isaac smells **Esau's sacred garments** worn by Jacob! He exclaims: 'The smell of my son is as the smell of a FIELD WHICH THE LORD HAS BLESSED!' The fragrance of Christ's righteousness (2 Cor 2:15) covers the believer, making us pleasing to the Father!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The fragrance of the blessed field prefiguring Christ's righteousness); 2 Cor 2:15; Eph 5:2; Heb 11:20.
historicalContext: Aromas of wild Negev herbs, frankincense, and myrrh embedded in the firstborn's sacred robes.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyiggash vayyishshaq-lo vayyarach eth-re'ach begadav vayvarakhehu vayyo'mer Re'eh re'ach beni ke-re'ach sadeh asher berakho YHVH*: *re'ach* (aroma/fragrance).
crossReferences: 2 Corinthians 2:15; Ephesians 5:2; Song of Solomon 4:11; Hosea 14:6.
historicalTrivia: 2 Corinthians 2:15 ('For we are the aroma of Christ (*Christou euōdia*) to God') is the exact New Testament fulfillment of Genesis 27:27.

dominicalIntent: 'May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth and plenty of grain and wine' (*Ve-yitten-lekha ha-Elohim mi-ttal ha-shamayim u-mi-shmanney ha-aretz ve-rov dagan ve-thirosh*). THE EARTHLY AND SACRAMENTAL BLESSING! Isaac bestows: (1) **Dew of Heaven** (*ttal ha-shamayim* = divine grace and the Holy Spirit), (2) **Fatness of the Earth** (*shmanney ha-aretz* = temporal fruitfulness), (3) **Plenty of Grain and Wine** (*dagan ve-thirosh* = THE EUCHARISTIC SPECIES OF BREAD AND WINE!).
cccReferences: CCC 1334 (Grain and wine as Eucharistic symbols in Isaac's blessing); CCC 2571; CCC 698 (Dew of the Spirit); Heb 11:20; Deut 33:28.
historicalContext: The triad of agricultural wealth in Canaan: Dew (*tal*), Grain (*dagan*), and New Wine (*tirosh*).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-yitten-lekha ha-Elohim mi-ttal ha-shamayim u-mi-shmanney ha-aretz ve-rov dagan ve-thirosh*: *dagan* (grain/wheat). *Thirosh* (new wine).
historicalTrivia: The pairing *Dagan ve-Thirosh* ('Grain and Wine') occurs 30 times in the Old Testament, forming the central Old Testament prefiguration of the Holy Eucharist.

dominicalIntent: 'Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you!' THE MESSIANIC DOMINION BLESSING! Isaac bestows universal royal dominion: 'Let peoples serve you... Be lord over your brothers... Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you!' This is the exact royal covenant of Abraham (Gen 12:3), transferred irrevocably to Jacob and fulfilled in Jesus Christ, the King of kings!
cccReferences: CCC 60 (The Messianic royal dominion given to Jacob); CCC 2571; Heb 11:20; Rev 19:16; Rom 9:12.
historicalContext: Sovereign royal primacy (*be-lor over your brothers*) conferring covenant leadership over all patriarchal clans.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ya'avdukha ammim ve-yishtachavu lekha le'ummim heyeh gevayr le-acheykha ve-yishtachavu lekha beney immekha oraraykha arur u-mvarakheykha barukh*: *gevayr* (lord/master/ruler).
historicalTrivia: Numbers 24:9 (Balaam's prophecy) quotes Genesis 27:29 word-for-word: 'Blessed be everyone who blesses you, and cursed be everyone who curses you'.

dominicalIntent: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, when Jacob had scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting. DRAMATIC TIMING! The instant Jacob leaves, Esau arrives from the hunt. God's providential timing locked the blessing upon Jacob before Esau entered.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Providential timing securing the blessing); Rom 9:11.
historicalContext: Dramatic collision of timing in the patriarchal tent.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayehi ka-asher kullah Yitzchaq le-varekh eth-Ya'aqov... ve-Esav achiv ba mi-tzeydo*: *kullah* (had completed). *Mi-tzeydo* (from his hunt).
historicalTrivia: The precise timing (*scarcely gone out*) demonstrates that divine providence orchestrated every second of the encounter.

dominicalIntent: He also prepared savory food and brought it to his father. And he said to his father: 'Let my father arise and eat of his son's game, that your soul may bless me.' Esau presents his savory meal, expecting the blessing.
historicalContext: Esau presenting his hunt to Isaac.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'as gam-hu mat'ammim vayyave le-aviv vayyo'mer le-aviv Yaqum avi ve-yo'khal mi-tzeyd bno ba-avur tevarkhani naphshekha*.
historicalTrivia: Esau uses the exact words Isaac had commanded him in v. 4.

dominicalIntent: His father Isaac said to him: 'Who are you?' He answered: 'I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.' Isaac's shock upon hearing Esau's voice.
historicalContext: Moment of dramatic revelation in Isaac's chamber.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer lo Yitzchaq aviv mi-attah vayyo'mer Ani bincha bekhorakha Esav*.
historicalTrivia: Isaac asks the exact same question ('Who are you?') he asked Jacob in v. 18.

dominicalIntent: Then Isaac trembled very violently and said: 'Who was it then that hunted game and brought it to me, and I ate it all before you came, and I have blessed him? YES, AND HE SHALL BE BLESSED!' (*GAM-BARUKH YIHYEH!*). ISAAC'S VIOLENT TREMBLING AND THE IRREVOCABLE BLESSING! Isaac trembles with violent terror (*vacharedah gedolah ad-me'od*). Why does he tremble? Because Isaac suddenly realizes that HE HAD TRIED TO FIGHT GOD'S ORACLE (Gen 25:23), BUT GOD HAS OVERRULED HIM! Isaac submits to divine sovereignty and proclaims with absolute finality: **'YES, AND HE SHALL BE BLESSED!'** (*Gam-barukh yihyeh!*). The blessing is completely irrevocable!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Isaac's violent trembling and realization of God's irrevocable decree); CCC 60; Heb 11:20 (By faith Isaac recognized Jacob as blessed); Rom 11:29.
historicalContext: Prophetic terror (*charedah gedolah*) seizing Isaac upon realizing he had been overruled by Almighty God.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyecheradh Yitzchaq charedah gedolah ad-me'od vayyo'mer... va-avarakhehu gam-barukh yihyeh*: *charedah gedolah ad-me'od* ('a great trembling unto exceedingly!'). *Gam-barukh yihyeh* ('Indeed, blessed he shall remain!').
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 11:20 praises Isaac's FAITH (*By faith Isaac blessed Jacob*) because at this exact moment in v. 33, Isaac surrendered his own preference and confirmed Jacob's blessing.

dominicalIntent: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out with an exceeding great and bitter cry and said to his father: 'Bless me, even me also, O my father!' ESAU'S BITTER CRY OF DESPAIR! Esau lets out a loud and bitter cry (*tza'aqah gedolah u-marah ad-me'od*). St. Paul (Heb 12:17) cites this exact moment: Esau sought the blessing with tears, but found no chance to repent, because he wanted the material blessing without genuine spiritual repentance for despising his birthright!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Esau's bitter cry of despair); CCC 1431 (False sorrow vs true repentance); Heb 12:16-17; Mal 1:3.
historicalContext: Eastern wailing of a son who has permanently lost his birthright and patriarchal blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ki-shmo'a Esav eth-divrey aviv vayyitz'aq tze'aqah gedolah u-marah ad-me'od vayyo'mer le-aviv barakheni gam-ani avi*: *tze'aqah gedolah u-marah* ('a great and bitter outcry').
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 12:17 commentary: 'For you know that afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no chance to repent (*metanoias topon ouch heuren*), though he sought it with tears'.

dominicalIntent: But he said: 'Your brother came deceitfully (*be-mirmah*), and he has taken away your blessing.' Isaac explains that Jacob came with subtlety/deceit (*be-mirmah*) and received the unalterable blessing.
cccReferences: CCC 2477 (Deceit in human actions); CCC 2571.
historicalContext: Patriarchal explanation of irrevocable legal transfer.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer ba achikha be-mirmah vayyiqach birkhathekha*: *be-mirmah* (with deceit/guile).
historicalTrivia: The LXX translates *be-mirmah* as *meta dolou* ('with guile'), echoing Psalm 32:2 ('in whose spirit there is no guile').

dominicalIntent: Esau said: 'Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has cheated me these two times. He took away my birthright, and behold, now he has taken away my blessing.' Then he said: 'Have you not reserved a blessing for me?' ESAU ACCUSES JACOB: 'HE HAS SUPPLANTED ME TWICE!' Esau plays on Jacob's name (*Ya'aqov* = Supplanter): 'He took my birthright, now my blessing!' Yet Esau conveniently forgets that HE VOLUNTARILY SOLD HIS BIRTHRIGHT for a bowl of stew (Gen 25:33)!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Esau blaming Jacob for his own profane decision); CCC 1866; Heb 12:16.
historicalContext: Wordplay on Jacob's name (*Ya'aqov* -> *vayya'qveni* = he has supplanted me).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer ha-khi qara shemo Ya'aqov vayya'qveni zeh pa'amayim eth-bechorathi laqach ve-hinneh attah laqach birkhathi...*: *vayya'qveni* (he has supplanted/tricked me, root *aqav*).
historicalTrivia: Jeremiah 9:4 uses Esau's verb: 'Every brother is a supplanter (*aqov ya'qov*), and every neighbor goes about as a slanderer'.

dominicalIntent: Isaac answered and said to Esau: 'Behold, I have made him your lord (*hen gevayr samtiiv lakh*), and all his brothers I have given to him for servants, and with grain and wine I have sustained him. What then can I do for you, my son?' Isaac confirms the absolute irrevocability of the primary blessing: Jacob IS made lord over Esau, endowed with the grain and wine.
cccReferences: CCC 60 (Irrevocability of the Messianic primacy); CCC 2571; Heb 11:20.
historicalContext: Declaring the unchangeable legal reality of the primary testamentary blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'an Yitzchaq vayyo'mer le-Esav hen gevayr samtiiv lakh ve-eth-kol-echav nathatti lo le-avadim u-dagan ve-thirosh ssamakhthiiv...*: *gevayr* (lord/master).
historicalTrivia: 2 Samuel 8:14 records the historical fulfillment: 'David put garrisons in Edom... and all the Edomites became David's servants'.

dominicalIntent: Esau said to his father: 'Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, O my father.' And Esau lifted up his voice and wept (*vayyissa Esav qolo vayyevkh*). ESAU WEEPS BITTERLY! Esau lifts up his voice and weeps (*vayyevkh*), begging for any secondary blessing.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Esau weeping for a secondary blessing); Heb 12:17.
historicalContext: Filial weeping begging for a secondary territorial blessing.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyo'mer Esav el-aviv ha-verakhah achath hi-lekha avi barakheni gam-ani avi vayyissa Esav qolo vayyevkh*.
historicalTrivia: Hebrews 12:17 emphasizes that Esau's tears (*meta dakryōn*) could not alter Isaac's completed blessing.

dominicalIntent: Then Isaac his father answered and said to him: 'Behold, away from the fatness of the earth shall your dwelling be, and away from the dew of heaven on high' (*Hinneh mi-shmanney ha-aretz yihyeh moshavekha u-mi-ttal ha-shamayim me-al*). THE SECONDARY BLESSING FOR ESAU (EDOM)! Isaac bestows a secondary anti-blessing: Esau's dwelling shall be AWAY FROM (*mi-*) the fatness of the earth and dew of heaven—residing in the dry, craggy red mountains of Mount Seir (Edom).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (The secondary prophecy for Esau/Edom); Mal 1:3; Obad 1:3.
historicalContext: Prophetic description of the arid, mountainous sandstone geography of Mount Seir (Edom / Petra in southern Jordan).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayya'an Yitzchaq aviv vayyo'mer elav Hinneh mi-shmanney ha-aretz yihyeh moshavekha u-mi-ttal ha-shamayim me-al*: *mi-* ('away from / lacking').
historicalTrivia: Malachi 1:3 commentary: 'I have loved Jacob, but Esau I have hated; I have laid waste his hill country and left his heritage to jackals of the desert'.

dominicalIntent: 'By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother; but when you grow restless you shall break his yoke from your neck' (*ve-al-charbekha thichyeh ve-eth-achikha tha'avod ve-hayah ka-asher tharid u-pharatzta ollo me-al tzavva'rekha*). PROPHECY OF THE SWORD AND FREEDOM! Esau shall live by the sword (*al-charbekha thichyeh*) and serve Jacob. But when Edom revolts (*tharid*), he will break Jacob's yoke from his neck! Fulfilled when Edom revolted against Judah under King Jehoram (2 Kings 8:20-22).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Prophetic history of Edom and Israel); 2 Kings 8:20-22.
historicalContext: Historical prophecy of Edomite military vassalage to Israel, punctuated by periodic bloody rebellions.
translationNuances: Hebrew *ve-al-charbekha thichyeh... ve-hayah ka-asher tharid u-pharatzta ollo me-al tzavva'rekha*: *tharid* (grow restless / revolt). *Ollo* (his yoke).
historicalTrivia: 2 Kings 8:20 records the exact fulfillment 900 years later: 'In his days Edom revolted from under the rule of Judah, and set up a king of their own'.

dominicalIntent: Now Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and Esau said to himself: 'The days of mourning for my father are approaching; then I will kill my brother Jacob' (*eharghah eth-Ya'aqov achi*). ESAU'S MURDEROUS INTENT! Esau harbors murderous hatred (*vayyistom*) against Jacob, planning to assassinate Jacob as soon as Isaac dies: 'Then I will kill my brother Jacob!' Fratricidal hatred echoes Cain killing Abel (Gen 4:8).
cccReferences: CCC 2259 (Fratricidal hatred as a grave sin against the Fifth Commandment); CCC 2571; 1 John 3:12-15; Gen 4:8.
historicalContext: Plotting fraternal blood vengeance (*vendetta*) under cover of anticipated mourning.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyistom Esav eth-Ya'aqov al-ha-berakhah... vayyo'mer Esav be-libbo yiqrevu yemey evel avi ve-eharghah eth-Ya'aqov achi*: *vayyistom* (harbored deep grudge/hatred). *Eharghah* (I will slay/kill).
historicalTrivia: 1 John 3:15 declares: 'Anyone who hates his brother is a murderer (*anthrōpoktonos*)', directly reflecting Esau's inner monologue.

dominicalIntent: When the words of Esau her older son were told to Rebekah, she sent and called Jacob her younger son and said to him: 'Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself about you by planning to kill you.' Rebekah learns of Esau's assassination plot and acts to save Jacob's life.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Rebekah protecting Jacob's life); CCC 307.
historicalContext: Maternal intelligence warning the younger son of an imminent blood feud assassination.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Vayyuggad le-Rivqah eth-divrey Esav bnah ha-gadol vatthishlach vatthiqra le-Ya'aqov... hinneh Esav achikha mithnachem lekha le-harghakha*: *mithnachem* (comforting himself / satisfying his anger).
historicalTrivia: Rebekah's vigilance saves Jacob's life, preserving the Messianic Seed from fratricidal assassination.

dominicalIntent: 'Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; arise, flee to Laban my brother in Haran...' REBEKAH SENDS JACOB TO HARAN! Rebekah commands Jacob to flee 500 miles north to her brother Laban in Haran until Esau's fury subsides.
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Fleeing persecution to preserve life and faith); Matt 10:23.
historicalContext: Evacuation to Upper Mesopotamia (Haran).
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-attah beni shema be-qoli ve-qum berach-lekha el-Lavan achi Charanah*: *berach-lekha* ('flee for yourself!').
historicalTrivia: Jesus in Matthew 10:23 reflects Rebekah's command: 'When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next'.

dominicalIntent: '...and stay with him a few days, until your brother's fury turns away...' Rebekah expects Jacob's absence to last only 'a few days' (*yamim achadim*). In God's providence, those 'few days' became **20 YEARS** of trial in Haran!
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (God using exile to purify Jacob); CCC 307; Gen 31:41.
historicalContext: Anticipated brief exile that expanded into 20 years of purification.
translationNuances: Hebrew *Ve-yashavtha immo yamim achadim ad asher-thashuv chamath achikha*: *yamim achadim* ('a few days / a short time').
historicalTrivia: Rebekah never saw her beloved son Jacob again on earth; she died while Jacob was away during his 20-year exile in Haran.

dominicalIntent: '...until your brother's anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him; then I will send and fetch you from there. Why should I be bereft of you both in one day?' Rebekah fears losing both sons in one day (Jacob by murder, Esau by blood-avenger execution).
cccReferences: CCC 2571 (Maternal anguish over family destruction); 2 Sam 14:7.
